title: Software Development Engineer II, DC Bridge
description:
Application deadline: Oct 13, 2026

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Help us push the availability and reliability of cloud infrastructure to new heights! The AWS Data Center Systems team builds services to monitor and data center infrastructure controls monitoring and alerting systems. Our services directly contribute to the high availability of AWS data centers and Amazon’s sustainability goals. Teams in Data Center Systems solve problems of massive metric ingestion, distributed systems/cloud computing, data visualization, anomaly detection, analytics, and graph networks.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer who is passionate about leading the architecture and development of application software that helps keep Amazon data centers running efficiently and securely. On any given day, we use Python, Java, Go, Lambda, DynamoDB, and CloudFormation, as well as other public AWS services and a host of Amazon-internal tools.



Key job responsibilities
In this role you’ll be leading the design, development, testing and launch of new data acquisition and transport services in the data center infrastructure space. You will work with senior members and junior members in the team to build new features. You will make sure enough test has been done to maintain the quality of the delivered software. You will join the oncall rotation to help solving customer issues in the production system and drive best practices that enable a quality product. Above all, you will care deeply about the customer and delight in creating simple and elegant solutions that solve our customers’ biggest challenges.

A day in the life
We are an Agile team following the best practices of this metrology. Members own the services and help drive the requirements from start to finish. You will have the opportunity a write your own destiny here.


About the team
About AWS

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

title: Leasing Agent

description:

title: Electronics Technologist –Power Conditioning System Operations and Maintenance
description:
The National Ignition Facility (NIF) is seeking talented and self‐motivated Electronics Technologists in the Plasma-Electrode Pockels Cell (PEPC) and Power Conditioning System (PCS) team. The NIF laser is the world’s most powerful laser system, capable of producing over 2 MJ of optical energy. You will operate the Power Conditioning System (PCS) and the Plasma-Electrode Pockels Cell (PEPC) systems through the high-level computer control system following detailed procedures. The PCS employs one hundred ninety-two high voltage (24 KV), high-energy (1.7 MJ per module) capacitor bank modules used to power the large flash lamps in the NIF solid-state laser amplifiers. The PEPC system employs high voltage electronics and sophisticated controls hardware and software to implement an optical switch topology for the 192 beams of the NIF main laser. These systems include high voltage power supplies, pulsed power hardware and circuits, analog, and digital controls hardware and software, embedded computers and diagnostics. The successful candidate will be expected to operate both systems remotely using Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) and perform site maintenance including electrical distribution, high voltage -equipment, digital circuits analog circuits, vacuum controls, compressed air controls and/or major system configurations across multiple engineering disciplines. Primary interactions will be with the lead operators, shot directors, system managers and electrical engineering support personnel.

NIF is a 24/7 operational facility, with the operators typically working an alternating three and four-day 12hr shift, with the last two hours of each shift being overtime. The dayshift work hours are from 06:30-19:30 with the night shift hours from 18:30-07:30. Dayshifts work Wednesday-Tuesday and every other Wednesday, or Thursday to Saturday and every other Wednesday. Night shifts work either Sunday to Tuesday and every other Saturday night or Wednesday to Friday and every other Saturday night. You will be required to pass various on‐site training modules to pursue work assignments. Some work will occur in radiological environments, and training will be provided prior to having access to those areas. This position is in the Laser Systems Engineering and Operations (LSEO) Division, within the Engineering Directorate.

This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work.

In this role, you will

  • Operate the Power Conditioning System (PCS) and Plasma-Electrode Pockels Cell (PEPC) through computer-based controls to support the National Ignition Facility laser operations.
  • Safely troubleshoot, repair, upgrade, and maintain moderately complex high-voltage, control, vacuum, and mechanical systems.
  • Diagnose and resolve issues with high-voltage modules, analog and digital circuits, and control systems using diagnostic tools such as oscilloscopes and computer-based systems.
  • Perform maintenance and acceptance testing of critical components, including plasma pulse generators and turbo pumps, to ensure operational readiness.
  • Accurately document repairs, maintenance actions, and system status, and communicate effectively to ensure smooth shift transitions and minimal downtime.
  • Maintain inventory of critical spare parts and ensure essential components are available.
  • Follow established procedures to place high-voltage systems safe for maintenance, conduct area “sweeps” before laser operations, and uphold Environmental, Safety & Health (ES&H) standards.
  • Provide input on new and existing procedures, automate trend reviews, and contribute to a culture of innovation and excellence.
  • Collaborate with scientists, engineers, and technicians to solve moderately complex problems in a 24/7 environment.
  • Adapt to changing system configurations, priorities, and processes to support experiments.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship.
  • Associate degree in engineering technology such as Electronics or Mechanical Technologies, or equivalent combination of education and experience related to the essential skills, knowledge, and abilities.
  • Intermediate knowledge and experience working with high-voltage and power systems
  • Experience with computer-based control systems and diagnostics, with the ability to learn new technologies quickly
  • Experience in electrical/electronic troubleshooting and using tools such as digital multimeters and oscilloscopes.
  • Ability to interpret technical data, schematics, operating procedures, and equipment documentation.
  • Experience working in a multi-disciplinary team environment.
  • Effective written and verbal communication/presentation skills.
  • Ability to exhibit workplace professionalism by adhering to ethical standards, respecting colleagues, and fostering a positive & productive work environment.
  • Ability to lift 25 lbs. in a safe & controlled manner and climb ladders.

Qualifications We Desire

  • Familiarity of the control of remote devices/hardware using computer-based systems.
  • Experience in LASER table alignment.
  • Experience with opto-mechanical and electro-optical troubleshooting.
  • Experience working within a nuclear, military, or highly technical laboratory environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to work on integrated technical systems including optical, electrical, and mechanical components.
  • Experience with Microsoft Excel.

Pay Range

$43.55 - $53.36 Hourly

This is the lowest to highest salary in good faith we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. Pay will not be below any applicable local minimum wage. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

title: Associate Product Manager
description:
About the role:

We're looking for an Associate Product Manager to be Rezdy's dependable NA presence — covering the hours our Sydney/Melbourne-based PM and dev team aren't online. This is a strong fit for someone energized by operational rigor and real-time problem-solving: comfortable triaging under pressure, translating between technical and commercial audiences, and building product judgment by working closely alongside a senior PM rather than owning a roadmap from day one. Pacific timezone

What you'll do:

  • Connect the time zones. Be the dependable daily link between North America stakeholders — support and account management teams — and the Sydney/Melbourne-based PM and dev team, flagging decisions and blockers in real time rather than letting them wait for the next overlap window.
  • Be the NA distribution conduit for Commercial leads and distribution partners (Viator, GYG, etc) and Distribution Resellers
  • Keep incidents moving and visible during NA hours. Triage escalations that occur in NA working hours against a defined severity framework, looping in the senior PM and dev lead when judgment calls exceed current scope, and making sure NA support and AM teams get clear, live updates rather than waiting for the next AU working day.
  • Surface and track AM churn risk. Own intake of NA account-manager-flagged churn risk — capturing impact and urgency the moment it's raised — so it's framed and ready to compete fairly when the senior PM and dev lead plan the sprint.
  • Answer for what's in flight. Be NA's go-to for "is this expected / is this known / what's the status" questions on Booking Manager and Distribution, working from close sync with the senior PM's roadmap and known-issues context rather than independent authority over it.
  • Share release communication in NA hours. Help execute the existing release process — communication and post-release follow-up specifically during NA hours — rather than owning release planning or prioritization.
  • Partner with Engineering at a working level. Build enough fluency in our data architecture to relay NA-side context accurately to engineering, without owning technical trade-off decisions.
  • Put AI tools to work. Use AI tools to speed up research, troubleshooting, and day-to-day tasks — a lever for moving faster, not a replacement for judgment.

What you'll bring:

  • 2+ years of experience in product management, product operations, or a closely related operational/customer-facing role, ideally in B2B SaaS.
  • Comfort working within another PM's priorities and roadmap — bringing your own judgment and context to how that work gets executed
  • Experience with incident or issue management processes, and communicating through them clearly under time pressure.
  • Comfort working with legacy technology systems and the teams that maintain them — able to translate between legacy constraints and current product priorities for both engineering and commercial audiences.
  • Strong written communication skills — able to adjust tone and depth for audiences ranging from support and account management teams to engineering.
  • Ease operating in process-driven environments (Jira, Slack, or equivalent).
  • Comfort picking up domain concepts across different product types — e.g., transactional booking flows versus distribution/channel connectivity — without needing deep expertise in both on day one.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in the travel, tours, or activities booking software space.
  • Familiarity with multi-brand or multi-product portfolios (Expedition Software operates Checkfront, Rezdy, and Regiondo).
  • Prior experience in a support, account management, or customer-facing product role.
The salary range for this position is $80,000-$95,000, commensurate with years of experience, skillset, and qualifications.

title: Biomarker & Bioanalytical Development Lead (Director / Senior Director)
description:
Company:

Chronic kidney diseases are a severe and growing worldwide health challenge that affects 1 in 7 people. Without effective treatments patients can experience kidney failure leading to dialysis and transplantation, a high burden to patients, families and the health care system. Despite recent advances for certain kidney disease patients, many forms of highly prevalent kidney diseases do not have effective treatments.

At Borealis Biosciences, Patients are our True North. Borealis was founded on the premise that a convergence of scientific and translational breakthroughs will enable RNA therapeutics to address some of the largest untreated kidney diseases and beyond. Borealis builds on the success of Chinook Therapeutics, a kidney disease company with a research site in Vancouver that was acquired by Novartis in 2023 for up to $3.5 billion. The Borealis team retains Chinook's strong experience in kidney diseases, while also bringing deep expertise in RNA therapeutics, to create a company uniquely focused on RNA-based solutions to renal diseases. We are headquartered in Vancouver, BC, with state-of-the-art wet labs for molecular and cellular biology, in vivo pharmacology, chemistry, DMPK, bioinformatics and analytical capabilities.

We are a creative and innovative team that strives for excellence in all we do and has fun along the way. Our core focus is on helping patients and advancing science. For more information on Borealis, visit or find us on LinkedIn.

We seek applicants from all backgrounds to ensure we get the best, most innovative talent on our team. We are building a diverse and inclusive workforce – come and be a part of our growth! We strongly encourage candidates with less traditional backgrounds or those who may meet the qualifications in a different way to apply.

Position:

The Biomarker & Bioanalytical Development Lead is Borealis' senior scientific owner of bioanalytical and biomarker strategy across our RNA therapeutics portfolio. This leader will design, build, and oversee the assays that measure drug exposure, target engagement, pharmacodynamic response, and safety in support of IND-enabling nonclinical and early clinical development. This is a highly visible, hands-on scientific leadership role with the opportunity to shape how Borealis generates the translational data that drives program decisions.

The immediate focus for this role is preparing Borealis for its upcoming Phase 1/2 trial, including development, transfer, and validation of regulated PK assays for oligonucleotide therapeutics, selection, contracting, and scientific oversight of bioanalytical CROs and specialty laboratories, delivery of a fit-for-purpose clinical biomarker strategy that demonstrates target engagement in the kidney, and ensuring assay robustness and GxP compliance

Over time, the successful candidate will build and develop the Biomarker & Bioanalytical team, thoughtfully balancing in-house laboratory capability with external partnerships, which requires a genuine commitment to mentoring and the patience to support team members stretching beyond their current specialization.

This position reports to the Sr. Vice President, Translational Medicine.

Responsibilities include:

  • Bioanalytical Strategy and Assay Development
    • Define and own the bioanalytical strategy for Borealis' RNA therapeutic programs, from discovery through IND-enabling studies and clinical development.
    • Lead development of fit-for-purpose assays to quantify oligonucleotide therapeutics and relevant metabolites in plasma, urine, and tissues (e.g., hybridization ELISA, LC-MS/MS, LC-HRMS, stem-loop RT-qPCR) to support PK, tissue distribution, and exposure–response analyses.
    • Establish immunogenicity (ADA) strategy and assays where required by modality, conjugate, or regulatory expectations.
    • Ensure method validation and sample analysis meet applicable regulatory expectations (ICH M10, FDA/Health Canada/EMA guidance, GLP, and GCLP).
    • Partner closely with DMPK, Toxicology, Pharmacology, and Chemistry to integrate bioanalytical data into PK/PD modeling, dose selection, and program decisions.
    • Investigate and resolve assay performance issues, and drive continuous improvement of assay robustness, sensitivity, and throughput.
  • Biomarker Strategy and Translational Science
    • Lead development and qualification of assays to measure target knockdown and downstream pathway modulation in accessible matrices (e.g., plasma, urine, urinary extracellular vesicles, kidney biopsy tissue).
    • Evaluate and implement emerging biomarker technologies (e.g., ultrasensitive immunoassay, multiplex proteomics, targeted transcriptomics, spatial and single-cell approaches) where they strengthen program decision-making.
    • Contribute biomarker expertise to clinical protocol design, sampling schedules, lab manuals, and sample handling and logistics plans.
  • CRO and Specialty Laboratory Selection and Oversight
    • Own the outsourcing strategy for bioanalytical and biomarker work supporting GLP toxicology studies and upcoming Phase 1/2 clinical trials.
    • Lead identification, qualification, and selection of bioanalytical CROs, central and specialty laboratories, including scope definition, proposal assessment, and budget review in partnership with Finance and Legal.
    • Lead method transfer from Borealis laboratories to external partners, and provide scientific oversight of method validation, sample analysis, and data reporting.
    • Review and approve validation plans and reports, sample analysis reports, and data packages; ensure data integrity and audit readiness.
    • Set clear expectations, timelines, KPIs, and escalation pathways, and actively monitor partner performance and quality.
  • Regulatory and Cross-Functional Contributions
    • Communicate data, interpretations, and recommendations clearly to project teams, senior leadership, and external partners.
    • Partner with Clinical Operations, Clinical Development, Quality, Data Management, and Biostatistics to ensure seamless sample and data flow across studies.
  • Team Building and Leadership
    • Design the Biomarker & Bioanalytical organization required to support Borealis' evolving portfolio, balancing in-house laboratory capability with CROs, consultants, and academic collaborators.
    • Build and maintain in-house laboratory capabilities, including equipment, SOPs, documentation practices, and quality systems appropriate to an early-stage company.
    • Recruit, onboard, develop, and retain high-performing scientists as organizational needs grow.
    • Coach and mentor team members to expand beyond their existing expertise without compromising on scientific rigor or delivery.
    • Build a culture of ownership, collaboration, transparency, scientific rigor, continuous improvement, and thoughtful urgency.
  • Model Borealis’ values, knowing that Patients are our True North:
    • Act with urgency, resilience and creativity to serve patients;
    • Be open to new ideas, honest conversations and two-way transparency;
    • Stay connected to team members and to science; being kind, humble, and taking risks together.

Location:

This is an on-site position located in Vancouver, BC, Canada. Immigration support and relocation benefits are available.


Education, Experience, and Skills:

Required:

  • PhD in pharmacology, analytical chemistry, molecular biology, immunology, biochemistry, or a related discipline with 10+ years of relevant biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry experience; BS/MS with additional equivalent experience may be considered.
  • Deep hands-on expertise in bioanalytical and biomarker assay development, including ligand-binding assays, LC-MS/MS, and/or molecular (qPCR/RT-qPCR) methods.
  • Demonstrated experience with method validation and sample analysis in regulated environments (GLP, GCLP, and/or CLIA), and a strong working knowledge of ICH M10 and related bioanalytical guidance.
  • Proven success leading outsourced bioanalytical and biomarker work, including selection, method transfer, and scientific oversight of CROs and specialty laboratories.
  • Experience supporting programs through IND-enabling studies and into early clinical development, with contributions to IND/CTA submissions.
  • Demonstrated experience building, leading, coaching, and developing scientific teams combined with the willingness to personally execute critical scientific activities.
  • Strong data interpretation and scientific judgment, with the ability to make timely decisions in environments characterized by uncertainty, evolving scientific data, and changing priorities.
  • Proven ability to work effectively across DMPK, Toxicology, Pharmacology, Translational Medicine, Clinical Development, Clinical Operations, Regulatory, and Quality.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presenting complex data to senior leadership and external partners.

Preferred:

  • Bioanalytical experience with oligonucleotide therapeutics (siRNA, ASO) or other novel modalities, including hybridization-based and LC-MS approaches.
  • Experience establishing or significantly expanding a bioanalytical or biomarker function within an emerging biotechnology company.
  • Experience with kidney-relevant biomarkers and matrices (e.g., urine, urinary extracellular vesicles, kidney biopsy tissue).
  • Experience with ultrasensitive immunoassay, multiplex proteomics, or transcriptomic platforms for biomarker discovery and translation.
  • Strong publication record and external scientific network.

Compensation: The annual salary range is $202,000 to $235,700.

Borealis Bio offers competitive benefits including annual bonus program, equity program, paid time-off, paid parental leave and more. Canada-based employees receive RRSP matching, extended medical, dental and vision and a Wellness Spending Account up to $1,800 per year. Actual base salary and title/level will be determined based on the qualifications of the successful candidate.

Borealis is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we prohibit discrimination or harassment of any kind. We are committed to fostering an environment where ALL people are welcome and supported. We cultivate a culture of inclusion for all employees that respects their individual strengths, views, and experiences. We believe that our differences enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better business results. Creativity and innovation flourish in an environment of openness, inclusion, and mutual respect.

title: Utility Line Clearance Supervisor
description:
Lucas Tree Experts, a leader in the tree care industry, is looking for a Utility Line Clearance Supervisor to join our Management Team in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

A strong supervisory background and valid UTT designation in good standing are required. The ideal candidate will have a minimum of 3 years industry experience or prior supervisory experience in a comparable role, and be comfortable with all aspects of supervision and management including:

  • Employee supervision
  • Safety & performance management
  • Staffing (to include recruiting, interviewing, orienting, and training new hires)
  • Developing growth opportunities and monitoring job success
  • Coaching, counselling, and disciplining employees to accomplish team goals
  • Implementing and enforcing policies and procedures
  • Complete operations by scheduling work, assigning crews, and monitoring work progress
  • Implementing productivity standards to meet operational goals
  • Resolving operational issues and implementing new procedures
  • Providing quality service by enforcing high quality standards with strong customer service

title: Data Scientist, Alexa Connections
description:
As a Data Scientist in Alexa Connections, you will lead the end-to-end development of machine learning and data science solutions that power intelligent communication experiences across channels such as calling, messaging and email. You will partner closely with product, engineering, and business leaders to translate ambiguous problems into scalable ML models, experimentation frameworks, and data-driven product decisions. In this role, you will design and deploy advanced ML and statistical models for capabilities such as prioritization, intent detection, and proactive action recommendations. You will analyze large-scale datasets and run rigorous experiments, including A/B testing and causal analysis, to measure impact and continuously improve customer engagement and product performance. Additionally, you will shape the applied science roadmap and collaborate with global cross-functional teams to deliver AI-driven solutions that scale to millions of Alexa customers.

Key job responsibilities
- Partner with product, engineering, operations, and security teams to translate complex business problems into scalable, production-ready data science and ML solutions.
- Own the full lifecycle of model development, including exploratory analysis, model design, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement.
- Define and track success metrics, conduct rigorous analyses, and provide insights that guide product launches, feature improvements, and data-driven decision-making.
- Build data-driven business cases to prioritize science initiatives and demonstrate measurable impact of ML solutions.
- Develop ML-powered systems supporting key business areas.
- Lead research and analysis to understand customer interactions with Alexa, and enhance overall customer experience.
- Contribute to the broader science community by mentoring analysts, improving data workflows and tooling, and publishing technical work in internal and external forums.

A day in the life
• Deep dive into our business metrics, analyze data, trends, and reviewing dashboards
• Writing code: building packages in Python, writing SQL queries, deploying solutions for Connections experience teams to consume.
• Leading or joining working sessions with Product Managers to refine problem statements new initiatives.
• Exploring new features and model architectures, leveraging AWS services, documentation, and upskilling yourself to the latest technologies.
• Leverage pre-trained LLMs to build applications that solve business problems for Connections experiences.
• Meet with Sr. Engineers/Principal Engineers to align on solution designs.
• Own or co-own MBR, WBR documents that are reviewed with Connections leadership team.

description:

The Commercial Management Coordinator supports the delivery of the Ontario Line Technical Advisory program by integrating commercial management, cost controls, schedule support, risk tracking, and document management. You’ll work closely with HDR’s Project Director & Project Management Lead, Commercial Manager, and Project Managers & Task Leads, coordinating information across HDR disciplines, subconsultants, partner organizations, and Client to help ensure commercial compliance, financial accuracy, and timely reporting in a fast‑paced P3, PDB, and DBB environment.

In the role of Commercial Management Coordinator, we'll count on you to perform the following responsibilities\:

title: Break Press Operator
description:
Job Title: Break Press Operator
Manager Title Production Supervisor
FLSA Status: Non-Exempt, Full-Time
FECON, LLC is a vegetation management equipment manufacturer located in Lebanon, Ohio near Kings Island Amusement Park. FECON is known for having very high-quality products and a team culture – and we are growing! We design, build, test, sell and service our equipment consisting of products such as our well-known “Bull Hog” mulchers, the Stump Ex, our high-quality FTX tractors of varying horsepower, as well as many other attachments. We offer competitive wages, full health care benefits and a continuous learning culture for those who want to grow with the company.
Job Summary:
Uses an electrically powered industrial machine to create, shape and customize metal material into a variety of forms dictated by the manufacturer. Required to read and interpret detailed and complex instructions to produce the desired forms.
Job Duties/Responsibilities:
  • Properly and safely operates CNC power brake press.
  • Works with press programmer to improve setups and processing of materials.
  • Sets stops on machine bed, changes dies, and adjusts components, such as ram or power press, when making multiple or successive passes.
  • Plans sequence of operations, applying knowledge of physical properties of the metal.
  • Inspects workpiece for defects.
  • Measures work piece and verifies dimensions, using micrometer, gauge, straight edge, scale and protractor.
  • Selects and positions flat, block, radius, or special purpose die sets into ram and bed of machine, using hoist, crane, measuring instruments and hand tools.
  • Completes daily workload requirements.
  • Maintains the machinery and keep the work area clean and orderly.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.
Required Skills/Abilities:
  • Understands complex instructions and how schematics work in order to ensure that items are designed and built correctly.
  • Ability to read and understand mechanical blueprints.
  • Ability to use measure tools including protractor, calipers and tape measure.
  • Understands when the machine is not at peak performance, how to increase output, and how to fix errors.
  • Possesses a strong attention to detail. Press brakes are precision equipment and being off by millimeters could create a critical error.
  • Has strong mechanical and technical skills. Machines controlled by computers will need operators who understand technology.
Education and Experience:
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2 years of press break operation required.
Physical Requirements:
  • Ability to safely lift 50 pounds.
  • Use overhead cranes and jib cranes.
  • Most work performed standing at floor level.
  • Ability to do repetitive movements with hands.

title: Systems Engineer

title: Investment & Valuation Analyst
description:
RWE Americas, LLC
To start as soon as possible, full time, permanent

Functional area: Finance / Controlling
Remuneration: Exempt

The Investment & Valuation Analyst will be a key member of the Investment & Valuation (I&V) team at RWE Americas (RWEA), supporting the analysis that underpins the company's strong US growth ambitions. The Analyst’s primary responsibility will be to support the evaluation of solar, wind, and battery storage investment opportunities, including the preparation of final investment decision proposals. The Analyst will learn to work with the team's valuation models and build working relationships across key functions while gaining broad exposure across solar, wind, and battery storage. The I&V team drives value-added growth through critical analysis, strategic guidance, and rigorous governance across a growing pipeline of utility-scale renewable energy and flexible generation investments, supporting approximately $20 billion in planned US investment over the next five years. It is an ideal role for a candidate looking to build foundational power generation market expertise and learn the fundamentals of project finance.

Role Responsibilities:

  • Investment Analysis, Valuation & Structuring:
    Performs quantitative and qualitative analyses of solar, wind, battery storage, and flexible generation investment opportunities using existing models and templates. Collects valuation inputs from internal stakeholders and identifies inconsistencies in assumptions and data

  • Decision Process & Materials:
    Supports the preparation of investment decision materials, including papers and presentations for senior management

  • Stakeholder Leadership & Alignment:
    Collaborates across the I&V team and gathers project inputs from development, commercial, and technical functions, communicating progress clearly. Supports internal analyses and ad-hoc valuation requests while flagging scope or priority ambiguities early

  • Model Quality & Governance:
    Works with existing valuation models to keep inputs complete and consistent within the defined scope and assumptions. Supports quality checks on financial models and analytical outputs, flagging inconsistencies and asking clarifying questions

  • Process & Tools Improvement:
    Shares observations and ideas for improving investment processes, financial models, and templates based on project experience, while learning the team's digital tools

Job Requirements and Experience:

  • Bachelor of Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Engineering, or similar university degree required
  • Previous Finance expereince required
  • Proficiency in Excel; able to run existing financial models, scenarios, and sensitivities with guidance required
  • Foundational knowledge of valuation methodologies, especially DCF
  • Communication and presentation skills
  • Interest in renewable energy or energy markets
  • Knowledge & Application:
    Proficient in Excel and able to run scenarios within financial models with guidance. Understands foundational financial concepts and is able to apply them to valuation, including key drivers such as capex and offtake pricing
  • Complexity & Problem Solving:
    Performs standard scenario analysis under clear direction and begins identifying valuation sensitivities. Demonstrates attention to detail by flagging issues and asking clarifying questions early rather than waiting
  • Collaboration & Interaction:
    Collects inputs from cross-functional teams and communicates clearly. Participates actively in team meetings, demonstrates curiosity, and shares progress in a digestible manner
  • Scope & Ownership:
    Owns discrete tasks within a broader workstream, delivering to expected quality and deadlines, and actively seeks and applies feedback

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. RWE Americas is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time.

description:
PROGRAM MANAGER I

General Responsibilities\:
The Program Manager I will serve as an Expert Inclusion Specialist for the National Center on Health, Physical Activity and Disability (NCHPAD) funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The Program Manager I will respond to inquiries, including a range of content or resource questions received by NCHPAD via telephone, website, email, or personal contact; conduct searches when necessary to answer inquiries, and catalog resources and information on physical activity, nutrition, mental health, outdoor recreation, and other wellness-related topics for people with disabilities and assist with updating NCHPAD directories; serve as a health coach for NCHPAD health promotion programs; and serve as an advocate for people with disabilities and act as a direct liaison between NCHPAD and people with disabilities and their caregivers. The position will work closely with the NCHPAD Call Center, the Participant Engagement Coordinator, and the Community Engagement and Communication teams to facilitate participant communication, resource development, partnership activities, and content development activities for the Center.

Key Duties & Responsibilities\:
1. Responds to inquiries made via the NCHPAD hotline, website, email, or other forms of contact.
2. Conducts necessary searches to address inquiries and catalogs resources and information on various topics related to health, wellness, and disability.
3. Assists with updating NCHPAD directories and identifying resources and opportunities that support participation of people with disabilities in health-enhancing activities.
4. Serves as an advocate for people with disabilities and a direct liaison between NCHPAD and people with disabilities and their caregivers.
5. Serves as a health coach for NCHPAD health promotion programs and helps participants navigate their wellness journey.
6. Works with the Participant Engagement Coordinator, NCHPAD Call Center, and Community Engagement team to strategize and implement participant communication activities across the Center.
7. Works with the Communication and Video team to develop content on various topics related to health, wellness, and disability, with particular emphasis on mental health, outdoor recreation, sport, fitness, and inclusive physical activity.
8. Supports the development and adaptation of health and wellness programs and resources through the GRAIDS process, including resources related to sport, fitness, and inclusive recreation.
9. Develops and supports resources, projects, and partnerships related to sport and fitness, including contributions to the ACSM Certified Inclusive Fitness Trainer (CIFT) initiative. This includes developing resource content and contributing to needs assessments, training, and technical assistance activities as assigned.
10. Supports community partnerships and represents NCHPAD at relevant meetings, conferences, and professional activities that promote disability inclusion in health, fitness, recreation, and wellness. Performs other duties as assigned.
11. Develops and leads NCHPAD's mental health focus area by building and expanding resources, content, partnerships, and programming related to mental health and disability. Integrates mental health considerations throughout NCHPAD's focus sectors and participant engagement activities, ensuring mental health is embedded across relevant health, wellness, physical activity, and inclusion initiatives.

title: H.R. 1 Communications Consultant 4
description:
Description

H.R. 1 Communications Consultant 4

This is a full-time permanent, remote optional position. Employees will be asked to attend in-person meetings or events based on business needs.

All HCA employees are required to be Washington state residents upon their first day of employment.


The Opportunity


Under the direction of the Apple Health Communications Manager, this position manages, plans, coordinates, and implements outreach, communications, and marketing for Washington Apple Health (Medicaid) program clients and stakeholders impacted by the House Resolution One (H.R. 1) bill.


Key Responsibilities Include:


  • Develop, plan, and organize comprehensive H.R. 1-related strategic communications for the statewide Apple Health (Medicaid) program with a focus on external stakeholder and client communications.
  • Provide strategic oversight and governance for the development and lifecycle management of Apple Health H.R. 1 communications assets and marketing—including forms, infographics, publications, fact sheets, FAQs, and client correspondence—by establishing content standards, prioritization frameworks, and quality controls to ensure alignment with program goals, regulatory requirements, and the information needs of external stakeholders and clients.
  • Provide strategic content for Apple Health Granicus Communications bulletins, announcements, blog posts, social media, text messaging, robo calls, video, press releases, publications, web content, talking points, and more.
  • Foster and maintain relationships with the five Apple Health managed care plan communication leads through participation in regular meetings, management of communication and marketing guidelines, and regular content review.
  • Direct reviews of managed care plan web pages and publications related to H.R. 1 content to ensure alignment with HCA Apple Health brand guide, style guide, and managed care marketing and information guidelines.
  • Manage Apple Health H.R. 1-related statewide communications/outreach plan.
  • Manage Apple Health H.R. 1-related program publication processes.

Why You’ll Love This Role:

This high-impact role empowers you to lead statewide communication and outreach strategies that guide vulnerable Washington residents through crucial changes to their Apple Health (Medicaid) coverage. You will shape vital messaging, partner with key state agencies and community leaders, and spearhead data-driven campaigns that ensure equitable access and minimize coverage loss during important legislative transitions.


What You Bring:

A strategic communication leader and compassionate advocate who thrives at the intersection of public policy, health care equity, and data-driven outreach. You excel at translating complex health regulations into accessible, empathetic messaging that resonates with diverse communities, specifically vulnerable populations across Washington state. A natural collaborator, you are adept at building strong, unified networks with state agencies and grassroots community leaders to amplify critical updates.

Required Qualifications

Experience may have been gained through paid or unpaid activities. Please ensure any relevant experience defined below is outlined in your cover letter, resume, and application.

  • Demonstrated ability to successfully perform writing, editing, and planning at an advanced level in communications, journalism, or related community information/relations positions.
  • Demonstrated ability to plan strategically, identify communications needs, and develop goals and comprehensive work plans for achieving those goals.
  • Clearly communicate complex technical information verbally and in writing to a non-technical audience, including the application of plain language principles to legally precise documents.
  • Knowledge of methods of determining needs for public information and education; methods and techniques of evaluating effectiveness of public relations programs; state government and departmental organization, programs, and functions.
  • Excellent writing and proof-reading skills.
  • Demonstrated curiosity about and enthusiasm for telling an organization’s story to internal and external audiences.


Required Competencies:

  • Equity lens – All HCA employees are required to consider equity in their decisions, processes, and day-to-day work, including how their work may affect the people and communities we serve.
  • The ability to take action to learn and grow – You take action to learn and grow by seeking new perspectives, learning from experiences, and using what you’ve learned to continuously improve how you work and serve others.
  • The ability to take action to meet the needs of others – You take action to meet the needs of others by listening, understanding different perspectives, and responding with care, respect, and solutions that support the people of the communities we serve.


Preferred Qualifications

While these are not required, having them may help you stand out as an applicant.

  • Experience with Apple Health (Medicaid) programs or related public-sector, government, or health services programs.
  • Experience in advising top management officials on communications and outreach strategies for programs.
  • Experience in selecting effective methods and techniques of disseminating a variety of information.
  • Knowledge of other state health care programs, commercial health care insurance, and current health care issues.
  • Understanding of health equity principles and how to apply them to communications strategies.
  • Experience working with government agencies, health care providers, health care insurers, and/or public/private health care stakeholders/customers.
  • Demonstrated ability to use social media and video tools to communicate with multiple audiences.
  • Knowledge of human-centered design principles and tactics.
  • Ability to work independently and in groups.
  • Accreditation in public relations.
  • 8 years of demonstrated professional experience in communications, journalism, or related community information/relations positions that include writing, editing, and planning.

OR

  • A bachelor’s degree in communications or journalism AND four (4) years of work experience in communications or journalism.

About the Communications Division


The Communications Division provides strategic leadership and operational support for external and internal communications on agency business and strategic initiatives for HCA.

Supplemental Information

The Washington State Health Care Authority:

Better Health. Better Care. A Healthier Washington.

At HCA, we work to ensure people across Washington have the opportunity to be as healthy as possible. As the State’s largest health care purchaser and behavioral health authority, HCA serves nearly 3 million Washington residents through Apple Health (Medicaid), Public Employees Benefits Board (PEBB) and School Employees Benefits Board (SEBB) programs, and behavioral health services. Through this work, HCA purchases and coordinated care coverage, supports behavioral health prevention, treatment, crisis response, and recovery and helps strengthen access to high -quality care across Washington.

More than a benefits package:

We want our employees to have the support, flexibility, and benefits they need to do their best work and build a career that works for their life. As a Washington State HCA employee, you’ll have access to a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance. Our benefits are designed to support you today while helping you plan for the future. Learn more about why HCA by visiting the Voices of HCA and the "Who we are" section of our website.


Your total compensation is more than your paycheck:

  • Remote work and flexible schedules
  • Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance
  • Paid vacation, sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid Family and Medical Leave (PMFL)
  • Retirement options to plan for the future
  • Training and professional development opportunities
  • Employee wellness programs
  • Learn more about Washington State Employee Benefits


Working Conditions:

Work Location and Schedule:

This is a full-time 40-hour-per-week remote position. You will report to the HCA office located in Olympia, WA for in-person work. Our standard business hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with alternative work schedules considered based on business needs. When working in-person, you will work in a shared space, open office environment. In this role you’ll regularly collaborate with colleagues, agency leaders, state and federal partners, and other external partners or customers. Occasional travel may be required for meetings, training, or other business needs. All employees are required to report to our Olympia office on their first and final day of employment.


Our commitment to an inclusive workplace

The Health Care Authority is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a workplace where employees are respected, included, and supported in bringing their experiences, perspectives, and ideas to work.

Our commitment to inclusion is reflected in how we work together and serve the people of Washington. HCA also supports five voluntary employee led Employee Resources Groups (ERGs), which create opportunities for connection, community, learning, and professional growth.

Application Directions:


To be considered, you must complete the online application in full and submit all required materials. Incomplete applications or applications missing required materials will not be considered. When completing your application, please include the following required materials:


  • Cover letter: describing your qualifications for this specific position
  • Resume: that details your applicable experience and education.
  • Three (3) professional references: References must be entered directly into the designated references section of your application. We require 3 professional references including at least one current or recent supervisor.

We encourage you to apply

If you meet the required qualifications for this position; we want to hear from you. Desired qualifications describe additional experience, knowledge or skills that may be helpful in the role, but they are not required to be considered for the position. We welcome applicants with different backgrounds, experiences, identities, and perspectives.

Veterans

We value the experience and skill veterans bring to the workforce and encourage veterans, transitioning service members, and military spouses to apply. Eligible veterans may qualify for veterans’ preference in accordance with Washington State Law. If you are claiming veterans’ preference, you must attach your applicable DD-214 documentation to your application. Please redact your social security number, date of birth, and any other sensitive information before uploading and attaching the document.

title: (Associate) Operations Officer - Transport Strategy & Knowledge
description: At the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org Infrastructure is central to economic opportunity, competitiveness, resilience, and improved living standards. The Infrastructure Vice Presidency supports countries and clients in developing sustainable infrastructure solutions, mobilizing public and private financing, strengthening institutions, and applying knowledge and innovation to deliver impact at scale. The World Bank Group Transport and Logistics Department supports sustainable, efficient, safe, resilient, and inclusive movement of people and goods. Its work spans roads, railways, urban transport, maritime transport, ports, aviation, logistics, and emerging mobility solutions. The department brings together World Bank and IFC capabilities to support public and private sector transactions, advisory engagements, analytical work, knowledge, and partnerships. The department works across regions and institutions to develop and implement transport solutions, mobilize investment, share operational knowledge, strengthen client capacity, and connect lessons from transactions to future operations. Its multidisciplinary teams collaborate with governments, private sector clients, development partners, industry associations, and technical experts. The (Associate) Operations Officer - Transport Strategy Knowledge will join the WBG Transport and Logistics team and support both IFC and World Bank activities. The (Associate) Operations Officer will work closely with management and technical teams across a broad range of strategic, operational, knowledge, and business development priorities. The role is intended for a highly capable generalist with strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills. The successful candidate will support strategic discussions and departmental priorities by conducting research and analysis, developing strategic narratives and management materials, preparing presentations and knowledge products, and helping senior colleagues communicate complex ideas effectively to internal and external audiences. The (Associate) Operations Officer will support the department in advancing knowledge, learning, business development, and operational priorities through analytical work, strategic messaging, stakeholder engagement, and the development of high-quality products and initiatives. This includes helping synthesize complex information, identify key messages, connect activities to broader institutional objectives, and support discussions involving senior management, regional leadership, clients, development partners, and other strategic stakeholders. The position requires sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to understand both the details and the broader context in which the department operates. The successful candidate should be proactive, solutions-oriented, and comfortable operating in complex environments, with the ability to anticipate needs, identify opportunities, build relationships across teams, and support the development and communication of departmental priorities. The role is well suited to someone interested in developing a deep understanding of World Bank Group operations and growing into broader operational and strategic responsibilities over time. Duties and Accountabilities The (Associate) Operations Officer will support the department across three interconnected areas: 1. Strategic Analysis, Operations and Business Development Support • Support strategic discussions, departmental priorities, and management initiatives through research, analysis, and the preparation of high-quality decision-support materials. • Conduct research and analysis on transport, logistics, infrastructure, private capital mobilization, and related topics, translating complex information into actionable insights and strategic narratives. • Prepare briefing notes, presentations, talking points, pitchbooks, portfolio reviews, management materials, and client-facing products for senior leadership, operational teams, and external stakeholders. • Analyze operational, portfolio, market, and sector information to identify trends, opportunities, lessons learned, and areas for strategic engagement. • Support business development, knowledge, and operational initiatives that require coordination across teams and institutions, helping ensure alignment with broader departmental and World Bank Group priorities. 2. Knowledge, Learning and Communications • Help translate complex technical and operational content into clear, accessible, and compelling messages that support internal learning, external engagement, and institutional visibility. • Support the department's knowledge, learning, and thought leadership agenda by helping capture, synthesize, and disseminate knowledge from operations and strategic initiatives. • Work with technical specialists to turn complex content into clear, accessible publications, notes, learning materials, presentations, newsletters, web stories, and communications for different audiences ensuring usability and visual/style coherence. • In conjunction with Intranet Lead and Intranet Technical Lead, support the maintenance of intranet pages, knowledge hubs, repositories, calendars, and related digital platforms, applying appropriate tagging, metadata, quality assurance, clearance, branding, and accessibility requirements. 3. Events, Stakeholder Coordination and Delivery • Support internal and external conferences, roundtables, client meetings, partner events, and flagship initiatives, including agendas, invitations, logistics, participant coordination, and post-event outputs. • Coordinate internal and external stakeholders across the World Bank Group, clients, partners, industry associations, governments, academia, and technical teams, maintaining clear workplans, deadlines, and follow-up actions. • Quickly learn and navigate relevant WBG processes, systems, templates, and clearance requirements, and maintain practical trackers and project-management tools to keep multiple workstreams on track.

title: Baader Technician
description:
Summary
As a Baader Technician, this role specializes in maintaining and repairing Baader 182, 192, 212, and 427 processing equipment, a crucial component at our Alaska seafood processing facilities, this role involves troubleshooting mechanical and electrical issues, conducting routine maintenance, and performing installations and upgrades. The technician must be proficient in hydraulics, pneumatic, and electrical systems to ensure optimal equipment performance and minimize downtime. Additionally, they may be required to work in challenging environmental conditions, such as cold temperatures and wet environments.

Essential Functions/Qualifications

The responsibilities of the position include the following:
• Conduct routine inspections, cleaning, and lubrication of Baader 182, 192, 212, and 427 processing equipment.
• Diagnose and repair mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and electrical issues.
• Install new equipment or upgrade existing systems.
• Monitor equipment performance and implement adjustments to maximize efficiency and minimize downtime.
• Adhere to safety regulations and industry standards, including lockout-tagout procedures.
• Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, repairs, and spare parts inventory.
• Identify and resolve equipment malfunctions to minimize production disruptions.
• Work closely with production teams to address equipment-related issues and optimize production processes.
• Tests the machines to verify step motors and tooling are set up and running properly.
• Ability to lift heavy equipment, work in confined spaces, and stand for extended periods.
• Other duties are to ensure the facility and organization is fully supported and successful.


Requirements

Competencies
To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following functional and interpersonal competencies:

Functional
• Technical Aptitude: A strong aptitude for learning and understanding technical concepts related to Baader products and systems.
• Manual Dexterity: Skill in using tools and equipment to perform precise tasks.
• Problem-Solving: Ability to identify and troubleshoot technical issues.
• Learning Ability: A willingness to learn and adapt to new technologies and procedures.
• Attention to Detail: Meticulous attention to detail to ensure accuracy and quality in work.
• Safety Awareness: Understanding of safety procedures and practices in a laboratory or manufacturing environment.
Interpersonal
• Communication: Effective communication skills to interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers.
• Teamwork: Ability to work collaboratively with others in a team setting.
• Adaptability: Flexibility to adapt to changing work environments and priorities.
• Reliability: Dependability and trustworthiness in fulfilling job responsibilities.
• Professionalism: Adherence to professional standards and ethics.

Education and Experience
• High school diploma or general education degree (GED); or one to three months related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
• Baader Certificate or equivalent training and experience.
• Seafood or manufacturing experience preferred but not required.
• Proven experience in maintaining and repairing industrial equipment, preferably Baader 182, 192, 212, and 427 processing Baader equipment.

Work Environment and Schedule
As a Baader Technician in a seafood processing plant, this role often works in a demanding and physically challenging environment. Typically, loud, cold, and wet, especially in Alaska processing plants. Technicians may be exposed to moving machinery, sharp objects, and hazardous chemicals. This role often works long hours, including weekends and holidays, to ensure continuous production. The position requires onsite presence at our Alaska Processing Facility, and the ability to travel, spending a significant amount of time during the season at our various locations and processing facilities in Alaska.

Physical Demands
The role requires significant physical strength to lift moderate to heavy equipment, endurance to stand for extended periods in cold, wet environments, and manual dexterity for precise tool usage. Additionally, the technician must be mentally focused to troubleshoot complex issues and work in a noisy environment.

Mental Activities
The employee is frequently required to set an example by consistently modeling high standards of honesty and integrity. Presentation and sharing of information should be handled in a direct, appropriate, and helpful manner. Maintains a reputation for honesty, confidentiality, reliability, and fairness. Is willing to admit mistakes and does not misrepresent him/herself for personal gain. Performs work with energy and drive; values planning, but will take quick, decisive action when an opportunity presents itself.


Benefits

Silver Bay Perks
Benefits and Perks listed below may vary depending on the nature of your employment with Silver Bay and the state where you work.
• Health Insurance: Seasonal Employees, as well as their families, are eligible for health benefits that include medical, dental and vision benefits once the employee meets the required 1560 hours worked to become benefit eligible. Employees are also eligible to receive basic life insurance.
• Employee Assistance Program: Available for employees and their families.
• Other Compensation: Employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus.

Silver Bay Seafood's is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

The IT Technician does not administer core infrastructure and operates under defined access controls to maintain security and compliance.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Provide onsite end‑user support for PCs, label printers, scanners/handhelds, cameras, phones, and production IT stations (OCMs/Bizerba, etc.), following SOPs.

  • Image, deploy, and maintain endpoints using approved tools (e.g., company standard OS images, endpoint protection, asset tagging).

  • Perform break/fix and routine maintenance: cable management, device swaps, peripheral replacement, and basic troubleshooting.

  • Execute ticket work in the Helpdesk system; update status, documentation, and time logs accurately.

  • Support user account lifecycle (create/disable/reset) **only** via approved Active Directory templates/PowerShell forms provided by DBA/IT Manager.

  • Run pre‑approved label and device configurations on production equipment; escalate non‑standard requests to IT Manager/Project Manager.

  • Perform site walk‑throughs to identify issues (loose cabling, hanging cameras, unsafe placements) and remediate or open tickets.

  • Maintain manifest of IT spares at the site; coordinate with IT Manager for vendor RMA and repairs per policy.

  • Escalate incidents per SOP when SLA thresholds or safety are at risk.

  • Assists in onsite projects as defined by the IT Project Manager and IT Manager.

Access & Privilege Constraints

  • Entry level permissions, no administrative access to core network infrastructure: **firewalls, SASE, VPN gateways, routers, core/distribution switches**.

  • No changes to VLANs, routing, firewall rules, NAT, site‑to‑site tunnels, or SSIDs; open a change request for the IT Manager.

  • Limited server access via standard support accounts **only** Tasks restricted to: password resets, enabling/disabling accounts, group membership changes via approved AD tools.

  • No production database or schema access. Report/data requests must be routed to the DBA team.

  • No changes to backups, anti‑virus policies, EDR/SOC configurations, or email security gateways.

  • Configuration of production equipment (e.g., OCMs/Bizerba) limited to documented SOP parameters; firmware/advanced settings require IT Manager approval.

  • All elevated actions require prior written approval (ticket/change record) and supervision by IT Manager or IT Project Manager.

Security, Compliance & Safety

  • Adhere to CP security policies, acceptable use, and respectful workplace standards.

  • Follow change management and incident response SOP; capture evidence in tickets.

  • Protect credentials and PII; use only assigned accounts and MFA as required.

  • Observe food‑production safety rules (PPE, clean‑room practices, equipment lockout/tagout) when working on the floor.

Qualifications

  • Associate degree in IT or related field **or** equivalent experience.

  • 1–3 years in hands‑on endpoint or plant‑floor support (manufacturing preferred).

  • Working knowledge of Windows 10/11, Office 365, Active Directory, printers/scanners, and ticketing systems.

  • Strong documentation habits; ability to follow SOPs precisely.

  • Ability to lift/move equipment (up to 40 lbs), use ladders and scissor lifts at up to 50ft high, and work safely in cold/production environments.

Shift & Coverage

Assigned to a specific site and shift (Day or Evening). Participates in on‑call rotation as defined by IT Manager. Overtime or weekend work may be offered for planned maintenance windows.

Performance Metrics

  • Ticket SLA attainment and MTTR

  • First‑time fix rate

  • Documentation completeness and accuracy

  • Adherence to access constraints and change procedures

title: Zorgassistent | de Posten | Enschede
description:
Op Waterlelie ondersteun je bewoners en collega's bij de dagelijkse gang van zaken op de afdeling. Je helpt waar nodig en draagt bij aan een prettige woonomgeving voor bewoners.

De rol

Als Zorgassistent ondersteun je bewoners en collega's bij verschillende dagelijkse werkzaamheden op de afdeling.

In de ochtend ondersteun je bij de zorg en help je bewoners om de dag goed te beginnen. Je ondersteunt collega's bij het klaarmaken van bewoners voor de dag en helpt waar nodig mee.

Later op de ochtend en in de middag ondersteun je bij de maaltijden. Daarnaast verricht je verschillende praktische werkzaamheden op de afdeling. Denk aan het verzorgen van afwasjes bij bewoners die dit zelf niet kunnen en het legen van prullenbakken op de appartementen.

Je bent zichtbaar aanwezig op de afdeling, maakt gemakkelijk contact met bewoners en ziet wat er nodig is. Juist met die praktische ondersteuning lever je iedere dag een belangrijke bijdrage aan het welzijn van bewoners.

De afdeling en het team

Waterlelie is een afdeling binnen Bloemenhof waar ongeveer 30 bewoners wonen. De afdeling heeft van oorsprong een somatisch karakter. Tegelijkertijd ontstaat er steeds meer een mix van somatiek en PG. Bewoners verhuizen binnen de Posten namelijk niet onnodig door wanneer hun zorgvraag verandert.

Dat maakt het werk afwisselend. Je hebt contact met bewoners met verschillende ondersteuningsvragen en draagt bij aan een prettige en verzorgde woonomgeving.

Je werkt samen met ongeveer 20 collega's, waaronder Verzorgenden IG, Helpende, Zorgassistenten, Huishoudelijk Medewerkers en Medewerkers Woonplezier. Vanuit ieders eigen rol zorgen jullie ervoor dat bewoners de ondersteuning krijgen die bij hen past.

Wie ben jij?

  • Je werkt graag met ouderen;

  • Je bent behulpzaam en toegankelijk;

  • Je ziet werk liggen en pakt dit op;

  • Je kunt goed samenwerken;

  • Je werkt zorgvuldig en betrouwbaar;

Wat bieden wij?

  • Salaris volgens cao VVT;

  • Een jaarcontract voor een afgesproken aantal uren;

  • Ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen;

  • Vertrouwen en verantwoordelijkheid in je werk;

  • Korte lijnen en betrokken leidinggevenden;

  • Pensioenopbouw en deelname aan de FiscFree-regeling.

Nieuwsgierig

Voor algemene vragen of vragen over de sollicitatieprocedure kan contact worden opgenomen met onze recruiter Leoni 06 27146488 of mail naar solliciteren@deposten.nl.

Ben je benieuwd naar de mogelijkheden bij de Posten? Kom gezellig langs voor een kop koffie bij één van onze recruiters tijdens het ontmoetingsmoment Bakkie en Baan en ontdek wat wij voor jou kunnen betekenen!

Wanneer: Elke woensdag van 10:00 tot 11:00 uur

Waar: De Posten 135 in Enschede (bij binnenkomst kan je je melden bij de receptie)

About the position:
The Forms and Public Records Specialist plays a key administrative role in ensuring the agency’s documents, forms, and records are managed efficiently, compliantly, and securely. In collaboration with other relevant positions, this role provides administrative support and executes actions related to public records requests, in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements. The role typically involves collaborating with employees and leadership members to ensure that records and forms systems align with CDHY’s operational and legal compliance needs.

Duties

Records Management and Retention:

  • Schedules and coordinates manual and electronic forms and/or records management services including files consulting, records retention scheduling, essential records scheduling, and similar services, in one or a group of organizational units and communicates record management needs with department personnel.
  • Reviews records retention schedules to ensure conformance with legal requirements and state and agency standards, procedures and policies.
  • Manages manual and/or electronic records retention, disposition, transfer, and storage systems and programs.
  • Designs and develops electronic forms, layout and screens; analyzes work plan and/or process to determine required data elements, screen and automation concepts; determines audit requirements.
  • Reviews and processes public record requests; assists in the development of public disclosure guidelines and training.
  • Develops and maintains forms web repository and web links.

Public Records Management and Response:

  • Receives public records requests, assists requestor in defining the scope of records requested, assists staff in identifying records responsive to a request, identify and redact information exempt from disclosure, provides records to requestor, and retains records related to requests in accordance with records retention requirements.
  • Provides consultation and determinations on responses to discovery records requests.
  • Conduct records management workshops and similar instructional sessions and assists in the development of instructional materials.
  • Review, determine, and analyze potential applications of electronic, automated, micrographics and/or imaging technology and assist in performing analysis to determine the feasibility and/or benefits of converting information to alternative formats.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Records Management – Ability to independently manage records throughout their lifecycle by organizing, categorizing, retrieving, securing, and disposing of complex paper and electronic records to maintain.
  • Retention & Governance – Ability to independently apply retention schedules, laws, and agency policies to organize, preserve, or dispose of records so the program stays fully compliant, and records remain accessible, protected, and legally managed throughout their lifecycle.
  • Policy & Legal Application – Ability to apply agency policies and state laws to ensure all records and disclosure work is fully compliant.
  • Training & Guidance – Ability to explain procedures, advise staff and managers to promote consistent records and forms practices.
  • Electronic Records Search – Ability to use advanced search methods across Laserfiche, program databases, shared drives, Outlook email, and other systems to find records for complex tasks.
  • Critical Thinking & Problem Solving – Ability to analyze complex records situations, system inconsistencies, and process gaps, and develop practical solutions or recommendations to ensure records are accurate, accessible, compliant, and support program decision-making.
    • Ability to communicate professionally in writing and in-person
    • Ability to manage multiple projects concurrently to achieve required timelines.
    • Ability and willingness to work with diverse groups of people.
    • Ability and willingness to work within a school environment serving students from grade Pre-K to post high school ages.
    • Ability and willingness to serve as a mandated reporter of child abuse and/or neglect.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Proficiency in American Sign Language (must be willing to learn).
  • Three or more years of working experience with records management, records retention, public records and/or electronic filing system management.
  • Professional working experience using Laserfiche systems.
  • Professional experience developing and providing training to employees.
  • Washington State Public Records Certification.
