title: Store Implemenation Coordinator - 532
description:
The In-Store Implementation Coordinator is responsible for leading the end-to-end execution of in-store partner activations across David’s Bridal’s retail footprint. This role serves as the central project management lead responsible for translating partnership concepts and commercial agreements into successful, scalable in-store experiences.
From shop-in-shops and product installations to take-sale programs, displays, signage, fixtures, events, and other partner activations, this individual will own the implementation process from kickoff through launch and post-launch stabilization.
Success in this role requires exceptional project management, strong cross-functional leadership, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple complex implementations simultaneously. The ideal candidate is highly organized, solutions-oriented, comfortable operating in a fast-moving retail environment, and able to drive accountability across teams without necessarily having direct authority over them.
Key Responsibilities
In-Store Activation & Implementation

Own the end-to-end implementation of in-store partner activations across the David’s Bridal store network.
Translate partnership agreements and activation concepts into detailed implementation plans, timelines, milestones, dependencies, and deliverables.
Coordinate launches including shop-in-shops, displays and fixtures, product placement, take-sale programs, signage, collateral, events, and other physical retail experiences.
Develop repeatable implementation playbooks that allow successful concepts to scale from pilot locations to broader store rollouts.
Ensure each activation is operationally ready before launch, including product, fixtures, signage, training, technology, inventory, store communication, and supporting processes.
Conduct post-launch validation to ensure activations were implemented as designed and identify issues requiring remediation.

Project Management

Serve as the central owner and source of truth for all assigned in-store implementations.
Build and maintain comprehensive project plans, launch calendars, workback schedules, RACI frameworks, risk logs, and status reporting.
Manage multiple concurrent implementations at different stages of development without sacrificing execution quality.
Establish clear owners, deadlines, dependencies, and escalation paths for every activation.
Proactively identify risks, blockers, and resource constraints and drive issues to resolution before they impact launch dates.
Lead recurring implementation meetings and provide concise, actionable status updates to stakeholders and leadership.
Create visibility into the overall activation pipeline, including upcoming launches, at-risk projects, decisions needed, and completed implementations.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Act as the connective tissue between Enterprise Partnerships, Account Management, Store Operations, Marketing, Creative, Merchandising, Technology, Supply Chain, Finance, and other internal stakeholders.
Partner closely with Enterprise Account Managers to transition signed partner opportunities from commercial agreement into implementation.
Coordinate directly with external partners and vendors on implementation requirements, deliverables, shipping, installation, creative assets, fixtures, and timelines.
Partner with Store Operations to ensure activations are executable at the store level and that field teams have clear instructions, training, and support.
Drive accountability across cross-functional stakeholders while maintaining strong, collaborative working relationships.

Operational Excellence & Scalability

Build standardized processes, templates, checklists, and documentation for in-store implementations.
Identify opportunities to improve launch speed, reduce friction, eliminate recurring implementation issues, and create greater consistency across stores.
Establish launch-readiness criteria and ensure required deliverables are completed before activation.
Maintain documentation and historical learnings to improve future launches.
Support the development of scalable operating models as David’s Bridal expands its portfolio of in-store partnerships and alternative revenue programs.

Performance & Post-Launch Support

Partner with Account Management and business stakeholders to validate that activations are functioning as intended following launch.
Establish processes for collecting store feedback, implementation photos, operational issues, reporting and other launch validation.
Track implementation KPIs including on-time launch rate, implementation cycle time, outstanding blockers, store readiness, and issue resolution.
Lead implementation retrospectives for major activations and incorporate learnings into future rollout plans.

Qualifications

5–6+ years of experience in project management, retail operations, implementation, store development, visual merchandising operations, partner operations, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross-functional projects from concept through execution.
Strong project management experience is required.
Experience supporting multi-location retail environments, physical store activations, installations, or large-scale rollouts strongly preferred.
Proven ability to manage multiple projects, timelines, stakeholders, and competing priorities simultaneously.
Strong understanding of dependencies, critical paths, risk management, and launch readiness.
Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate clearly with both executives and frontline teams.
Ability to influence and drive accountability across teams without direct reporting relationships.
Comfortable operating in an evolving environment where processes may need to be built while the work is underway.
Experience with project management and collaboration platforms such as Jira, Monday.com, Asana, Smartsheet, Confluence, or similar tools preferred.
Retail, bridal, fashion, marketplace, shop-in-shop, or partnership experience is a plus.

What Success Looks Like
Within this role, success means that every in-store partnership has a clear path from signed agreement → implementation → store readiness → launch → validation.
The In-Store Implementation Coordinator creates the operational discipline necessary to ensure:

Activations launch on time and as designed.
Stores understand exactly what is expected of them.
Partners have clear visibility into implementation.
Cross-functional owners understand their responsibilities and deadlines.
Risks and blockers are surfaced early rather than at launch.
Successful pilots can be quickly and consistently scaled.
Leadership has clear visibility into the status and health of the in-store activation portfolio.

Ideal Candidate Profile
You are a highly organized individual who thrives on turning ideas into execution. You naturally create structure around ambiguity, anticipate what could go wrong, and follow through until every detail is complete.
You are equally comfortable building a project plan, working through an operational issue with a store team, coordinating deliverables with an external partner, and providing an executive-level status update.
Most importantly, you take ownership. When an activation is handed to you, you become accountable for getting it across the finish line.

title: Multiplatform Content Scheduler
description:
Division: Programming & Multi-platform
Work Status: Full-time
Location: Toronto, Ontario (Hybrid)

About the Role
We are looking for a highly organized and detail-oriented Multi-platform Content Scheduler to support the scheduling and operational management of content across our on-demand and FAST channel platforms.

Passion for television and digital content.

FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS

ADVERTISING/WORKING TITLE: SENIOR CLASSIFICATION OFFICER

This open competitive advertisement is for a Career Service position located at the Charlotte Correctional Institution in the Classification Department.

Our mission in the Classification Department is to accurately assess and classify inmates based on their needs, risks, and behaviors. We ensure appropriate housing and program placements within the correctional system. Our goal is to enhance safety and security while promoting effective rehabilitation, ultimately aiding in the successful reintegration of inmates into society.This position is not a telework position and is required to report to the FDC office in the area it serves.

• Planning and coordinating targeted referrals for treatment, programs, work, and services to meet both inmate and departmental needs. Collaborate with various areas for optimal outcomes.

• Evaluating diverse information sources, such as reports, interviews, and observations, to make informed decisions on inmate management.

• Maintaining accurate and detailed inmate records in the Offender Based Information System (OBIS) and other necessary applications. Compile and develop records as needed.

• Leading disciplinary hearings, making custody and reclassification recommendations, and handling special status inmate reviews. Ensure all eligible inmates receive appropriate gain time awards.

title: Spa Supervisor
description:
The Spa Supervisor supports daily operations at the resort’s 15-treatment-room spa, helping deliver a smooth, welcoming experience for guests and a well-organized work environment for the team. This is a hands-on, guest-facing role that provides on-shift direction, supports the Spa Assistant Manager with staffing and service standards, and helps coordinate the spa’s front-of-house and treatment operations.

The Spa Supervisor handles routine operating decisions and guest concerns during assigned shifts, escalating significant staffing, financial, safety, or service issues to the Spa Assistant Manager. The Spa Assistant Manager leads day-to-day department management; the Area Director of Spa provides broader direction and oversight.

The pay rate for this position is $21.00 - $23.00 hourly. This is the pay rate for this position that the Grand Hyatt Indian Wells reasonably expects to pay. Decisions regarding individual salaries will be based on a number of factors, such as experience and education.

Key responsibilities

Responsibilities include, but not limited to\:

  • Lead assigned shifts, helping the spa open, operate, and close according to resort standards.
  • Welcome guests and support a calm, polished arrival and departure experience, including clear communication about appointments, spa services, and resort policies.
  • Monitor the daily appointment schedule and coordinate with reception, therapists, and other spa team members to keep service flow on track.
  • Help assign and adjust work during the shift based on bookings, staffing, and guest needs.
  • Coach team members in the moment on hospitality, communication, presentation, and service standards; share follow-up coaching needs with the Spa Assistant Manager.
  • Respond to routine guest questions and concerns, resolve issues within established guidelines, and promptly escalate matters requiring management attention.
  • Inspect treatment rooms, relaxation areas, locker rooms, and other guest spaces for cleanliness, readiness, supplies, and presentation.

  • Support consistent pre- and post-treatment room procedures and help the team follow sanitation, safety, and resort operating protocols.

  • Communicate with hotel departments, including housekeeping, front office, concierge, and food and beverage, to coordinate guest needs and resort service.
  • Help maintain accurate shift notes, incident reports, attendance records, and other operational documentation.
  • Support onboarding and training for new team members and reinforce established procedures.

  • Assist with weekly payroll processing by reviewing timecards, monitoring attendance, identifying discrepancies, and ensuring payroll information is submitted accurately and on time.

  • Stay informed about spa services, packages, promotions, and resort offerings so guest questions can be handled accurately.

  • Maintain inventory controls, oversee supply replenishment, and help ensure operational readiness across all spa areas.

  • Foster retail success by coaching associates on product knowledge, recommendations, and guest education.

  • Support the implementation of spa promotions, seasonal offerings, and resort marketing initiatives.

  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Success in this role

Success means guests feel welcomed and well cared for, spa spaces and schedules are ready for service, team members receive reliable on-shift support, and operational issues are communicated to the Spa Assistant Manager promptly and clearly.

Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance

401k Retirement Savings Plan with Company Match

Free Room Nights at Hyatt Hotels and Friend & Family Discounts

Paid Vacation, Paid Sick Days

Free Lunch Meals during shift

title: Verzorgende IG | de Posten  | Enschede
description:
Als Verzorgende IG op Bloesem bied je bewoners de zorg, begeleiding en ondersteuning die zij nodig hebben. Samen met je collega's zorg je ervoor dat bewoners hun leven zoveel mogelijk kunnen blijven invullen op een manier die bij hen past.

De rol

Als Verzorgende IG ondersteun en begeleid je bewoners bij de dagelijkse zorg. Daarnaast verricht je verpleegtechnische handelingen die horen bij jouw deskundigheid.

Je observeert, signaleert en bespreekt veranderingen in de gezondheid of het welzijn van bewoners. Daarbij werk je nauw samen met collega's, behandelaren en familieleden.

Doordat je bewoners goed leert kennen, merk je vaak snel wanneer er iets verandert. Je denkt mee over passende ondersteuning en draagt bij aan de kwaliteit van leven van bewoners.

Geen dag is hetzelfde. Juist de combinatie van zorg, contact met bewoners en samenwerking met collega's maakt het werk veelzijdig en betekenisvol.

De afdeling en het team

Bloesem is een afdeling binnen Bloemenhof waar ongeveer 30 bewoners wonen. De afdeling heeft van oorsprong een somatisch karakter. Tegelijkertijd ontstaat er steeds meer een mix van somatiek en PG. Bewoners verhuizen binnen de Posten namelijk niet onnodig door wanneer hun zorgvraag verandert.

Dat maakt het werk afwisselend. Je ondersteunt bewoners met verschillende zorgvragen en blijft meebewegen met wat bewoners nodig hebben.

Je werkt samen met ongeveer 20 collega's, waaronder Verzorgenden IG, Helpende, Zorgassistenten, Huishoudelijk Medewerkers en Medewerkers Woonplezier. Vanuit ieders eigen rol zorgen jullie ervoor dat bewoners de ondersteuning krijgen die bij hen past.

Medewerkers waarderen de warme sfeer, het fijne team en het persoonlijke contact met bewoners. Samen werken jullie aan een omgeving waar bewoners zich thuis voelen.

Wie ben jij?

  • Je bent gediplomeerd Verzorgende IG;

  • Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor de zorg die je levert;

  • Je kunt zelfstandig werken en maakt gemakkelijk contact met bewoners;

  • Je signaleert veranderingen en onderneemt actie wanneer dat nodig is;

  • Je werkt graag samen met collega's en andere disciplines;

Wat bieden wij?

  • Salaris volgens cao VVT, schaal 35;

  • Een jaarcontract voor 30 uur per week;

  • Ruimte om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen;

  • Vertrouwen en verantwoordelijkheid in je werk;

  • Korte lijnen en betrokken leidinggevenden;

  • Een prettige werkomgeving waarin collega's voor elkaar klaarstaan;

  • Pensioenopbouw en deelname aan de FiscFree-regeling.

Nieuwsgierig

Voor algemene vragen of vragen over de sollicitatieprocedure kan contact worden opgenomen met onze recruiter Leoni 06 27146488 of mail naar solliciteren@deposten.nl.

title: Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services, State and Local Government and Higher Education
description:
Are you passionate about helping State and Local Government and Higher Education institutions unlock the transformative power of cloud technology? Amazon Web Services is seeking a Solutions Architect to serve as a trusted technical advisor to customers across the Maryland region. In this role, you'll combine your communication skills, problem-solving abilities, and eagerness to learn new technologies to guide diverse organizations through their cloud journey.

This is more than a typical technology consulting role. You'll work at the intersection of innovation and public service, helping government agencies and universities architect solutions that modernize their operations, improve citizen and student experiences, and achieve mission-critical outcomes. Your ability to understand complex technical challenges and translate them into actionable solutions will help grow our State and Local Government and Higher Education businesses while making a meaningful impact on communities across the region.



Key job responsibilities
- Design and deliver cloud architecture solutions that meet infrastructure and application requirements for State and Local Government and Higher Education customers, incorporating best practices for security, scalability, and performance
- Lead architecture reviews, technical workshops, and proof-of-concept projects that demonstrate innovative cloud solutions and help customers envision transformative possibilities for their organizations
- Serve as a trusted technical advisor by taking the time to understand each customer's unique business context, technology challenges, and long-term goals, then translating those needs into technical requirements
- Collaborate with account teams, professional services, and AWS engineering groups to scope customer engagements with clear objectives, drive timely delivery of value, and ensure customer success throughout their cloud adoption journey
- Educate customers and internal teams by developing and delivering technical content such as presentations, workshops, and best practice guidance, while capturing and sharing knowledge that advances the broader Solutions Architecture community

A day in the life
Your day might begin with an architecture review session with a state agency exploring modernization options, followed by leading a hands-on workshop that demonstrates serverless computing for IT team. After collaborating with your account team to develop a migration strategy, you'll build a proof-of-concept that illustrates the art of the possible with analytics and AI/ML services. You'll wrap up by joining a strategic planning discussion with a state agency CIO about how cloud technology can drive their agency's digital transformation objectives.

title: Helpende | de Posten | Enschede
description:
Voor veel bewoners ben jij één van de eerste gezichten die zij zien wanneer de dag begint. Je ondersteunt bij de dagelijkse verzorging en begeleiding en zorgt ervoor dat bewoners de dag prettig en op hun eigen manier kunnen starten. Je werkt voornamelijk dagdiensten die beginnen om 07.30 uur.

De rol

Als Helpende ondersteun je bewoners bij de dagelijkse verzorging en begeleiding. Je helpt bij het opstaan, wassen, aankleden en andere dagelijkse activiteiten.

Je kijkt naar wat iemand zelf kan en ondersteunt waar dat nodig is. Omdat je bewoners regelmatig ziet, leer je hun gewoonten, voorkeuren en dagelijkse ritme kennen. Daardoor merk je vaak snel wanneer er iets verandert en kun je daar samen met collega's op inspelen.

Je draagt niet alleen bij aan goede zorg, maar ook aan een prettige dag voor bewoners. Soms zit dat in de ondersteuning die je biedt, soms in een gesprek of juist in het herkennen van wat iemand nodig heeft.

De afdeling en het team

Waterlelie is een afdeling binnen Bloemenhof waar ongeveer 30 bewoners wonen. De afdeling heeft van oorsprong een somatisch karakter. Tegelijkertijd ontstaat er steeds meer een mix van somatiek en PG. Bewoners verhuizen binnen de Posten namelijk niet onnodig door wanneer hun zorgvraag verandert.

Dat maakt het werk afwisselend. Je ondersteunt bewoners met verschillende zorgvragen, waardoor geen dag hetzelfde is.

Je werkt samen met ongeveer 20 collega's in verschillende functies, waaronder Verzorgenden IG, Helpende, Zorgassistenten, Huishoudelijk Medewerkers en Medewerkers Woonplezier. Vanuit ieders eigen rol zorgen jullie ervoor dat bewoners de ondersteuning krijgen die bij hen past.

Praktisch

· Je werkt voornamelijk dagdiensten;

· De diensten starten veelal om 07.30 uur;

· Je bent bereid om ook weekenden te werken.

Wie ben jij?

  • Je bent gediplomeerd Helpende Zorg & Welzijn niveau 2;

  • Je werkt zelfstandig en neemt verantwoordelijkheid;

  • Je kunt goed samenwerken en zoekt collega's makkelijk op;

  • Je hebt oog voor de bewoner achter de zorgvraag;

  • Je vindt het prettig om onderdeel te zijn van een team waarin collega's elkaar ondersteunen.

Wat bieden wij?

  • Salaris volgens cao VVT, schaal 25;

  • Een jaarcontract voor een afgesproken aantal uren;

  • Ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen;

  • Vertrouwen en verantwoordelijkheid in je werk;

  • Korte lijnen en betrokken leidinggevenden;

  • Een organisatie waar aandacht voor bewoners én collega's centraal staat;

  • Pensioenopbouw en deelname aan de FiscFree-regeling.

Nieuwsgierig

Voor algemene vragen of vragen over de sollicitatieprocedure kan contact worden opgenomen met onze recruiter Leoni 06 27146488 of mail naar solliciteren@deposten.nl.

Ben je benieuwd naar de mogelijkheden bij de Posten? Kom gezellig langs voor een kop koffie bij één van onze recruiters tijdens het ontmoetingsmoment Bakkie en Baan en ontdek wat wij voor jou kunnen betekenen!

Wanneer: Elke woensdag van 10:00 tot 11:00 uur

Waar: De Posten 135 in Enschede (bij binnenkomst kan je je melden bij de receptie)

title: Spring 2027 DNC Technology Internship
description:
Welcome to the DNC Technology Internship Application!


The DNC Technology department is accepting applications for our Spring 2027 Internship Program! This is a separate application from the DNC General Internship Application because it requires specific experience.


Interning with DNC Tech is a unique opportunity for future leaders to gain real life, hands-on experience in Democratic political technology, learn and experience industry data & analytics processes, strengthen their understanding of the political process, and prepare them for future political opportunities.


The program will run from January 11, 2027 - March 19, 2027 and will be conducted in an in-person, hybrid, or remote format. Interns who are based in the Washington D.C. area will have an opportunity to perform in-person work for the DNC at the Democratic National Committee Headquarters and DNC events. You must be located in the United States to apply for this internship.


The DNC Internship Program provides a stipend of $3,700. Housing is not provided. During the upcoming term, interns are expected to work 20 hours per week.


The deadline for applications is November 27, 2026.


Position Summary:

As an intern with DNC Tech, you will work on a project or projects designed to support the work of the overall Tech team and your own skills and experience. You will build your skills as a technology professional, in data analytics, engineering, or data science; software engineering; product; or supporting users of data and technology products, or cybersecurity. You will participate in team meetings and work closely with mentor(s). In addition to working on project/s, you may work on a variety of additional tasks relevant to the team you’re interning with. As an intern with DNC Tech, you’ll learn a lot about the interesting ways in which technology intersects politics.


As part of the internship program, you will also be expected to assist the DNC Operations team by attending weekly phone shifts and any mandatory onboarding/offboarding sessions.


In addition, through the internship program, you will have opportunities to participate in grassroots organizing, assist at DNC functions, receive personal development training, and network with DNC leadership and staff.


NOTE: The Data team at the DNC are fully remote teams. Tech interns may work from any contiguous US time zone. If working from AK or HI, you must be able to do work during either Pacific, Mountain, Central, or Eastern time working hours. You will arrange a schedule with a supervisor. Technology interns still have the opportunity to choose among in-person, hybrid, or remote work like every DNC intern, but be aware that your supervisor and mentors will likely be remote.


An internship at DNC Tech may be a great fit for you if:

  • You’re willing to learn new things, and you feel comfortable learning and problem-solving on your own, with guidance from a mentor.
  • You enjoy problem-solving and have strong communication skills.
  • You are excited to learn about the ways that tech can support Democratic politics, and to work on things that help others.
  • You have previous experience in politics, e.g. using Votebuilder, or volunteering for a Democratic campaign. (This is NOT required.)


For the data internship, we recommend:

  • You have completed at least a semester, ideally two semesters, of computer programming-related courses, OR have equivalent experience. We expect interns on the Data team to have done some computer programming or data manipulation / analysis previously
  • Our team uses a lot of SQL, Python, and R but it is okay if you’ve never used one of those before, as long as you have some familiarity with programming or spreadsheet software including Excel or Google Sheets. If you’ve used one of those languages or software, or something else similar to one of those, we encourage you to apply!


For the cybersecurity internship, we recommend:

  • You have at least an entry-level skill-set in using MacBooks and Google Suite applications
  • Our team constantly has to adapt to industry changes that happen almost daily – therefore, having a passion for technology and learning new things is required
  • Basic Scripting: Ability to write entry-level scripts in Python, Bash, or PowerShell to automate simple tasks or parse data.
  • Security Core Concepts: Understanding of fundamental principles such as the CIA triad, authentication mechanisms, common threats (phishing, malware), and industry recognized security frameworks (CIS, NIST, etc.).
  • AI Security & Tool Awareness: Familiarity with basic AI security concepts such as prompt injection and data privacy risks.


Include in your application for a DNC Tech internship:

  • In your cover letter, tell us why do you want to intern here, specifically? Tell us about a time you solved a problem or learned something new. (Briefly - 1 paragraph or less is fine!)
  • Share in your resume and/or cover letter what software / technology / programming skills, and experiences you have. What are the titles of a couple relevant classes you’ve taken? What technology related project /s (ex. an assignment from a class) have you worked on? This information helps us determine whether we have a project that will match your experience and interest.


About the team:

  • The DNC Technology department (aka DNC Tech) is a small, collaborative, multi-disciplinary tech team – we provide the tech foundation for Democratic politics. You can learn more about the team here. We build tools and applications that help elect Democrats year over year. Our work is an incredibly important background part of running successful Democratic campaigns around the country, including:
  • Ensuring permissions and onboarding/offboarding work properly and that our data tools are secure,
  • Ensuring we have accurate, accessible data,
  • Building tools so that people working hard on campaigns and in other political roles can save time and energy,
  • Making it possible for those with voter protection expertise to share accurate information about how to vote,
  • Supporting people throughout the Democratic ecosystem with secure hardware, software, device management, and other technology problems,
  • … and much more.


Eligibility Requirements:

Applicants must be 18 years of age on or before the first day of the internship and meet at least one of the following criteria:

  • Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a college, community college, or university (two-to-four year institution). It is highly recommended that applicants complete at least one full term prior to submitting an application.
  • Graduated from an undergraduate or graduate program at a college, community college, or university (two-to-four year institution) no more than two years before the first day of the internship.
  • A veteran of the United States Armed Forces who possesses a high school diploma or its equivalent and has served on active duty, for any length of time, in the two years preceding the first day of the internship.


Applicants must meet all of the following criteria:

  • Commitment of 20 hours per week during the program
  • Physically present in the United States to participate in this internship program


Required Application Materials:

  • Resume
  • Cover letter
  • References


SECTION: CLOSING

Due to the volume of applications, we cannot review materials submitted outside the application form. All applicants must complete the application to be considered. To ensure you have the most up-to-date information, we recommend reading our FAQ page before contacting us with questions. If you have a specific question, please email us at internapp@dnc.org.


The Democratic National Committee (DNC) is committed to diversity among its staff, and recognizes that its continued success requires the highest commitment to obtaining and retaining a diverse staff that provides the best quality services to supporters and constituents. The DNC is an equal opportunity employer and it is our policy to recruit, hire, train, promote and administer any and all personnel actions without regard to sex, race, age, color, creed, national origin, religion, economic status, sexual orientation, veteran status, gender identity or expression, ethnic identity or disability, or any other legally protected basis. The DNC is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities in the hiring process and on the job, as required by applicable law. The DNC will not tolerate any unlawful discrimination and any such conduct is strictly prohibited.

SCHEDULE: Monday - Friday Hours, 9am-5pm

LOCATION: Manhattan

WORKPLACE FLEXIBILITY: In Person, 1 day remote

POSITION SUMMARY

This position is responsible for conceptualizing and executing AFC’s special events, fundraising efforts and client events. This position will work closely with the Chief Development Officer to meet the fundraising goals of the organization with a focus on fundraising through special events and management of existing signature events and other third party events. Overall, this position is responsible for managing and growing the revenue from our signature events and building a vision of how we can continue to grow the scope and impact of our revenue generating events.

The focus of this role is taking our events to the next level. Knowledge of scaling the fundraising prowess while reducing expenses is critical. This individual will mobilize lay leadership and community to prospect leadership, co-chairs, host committee and multipliers who can bring in new sponsors and ticket buyers. This role will collaborate closely with the Directors on the team to integrate events and attendees into overall fundraising strategies.

This role will be strategy based, analyzing the revenue and expenses of our existing events and identifying ways to significantly increase revenue.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Event Vision, Strategy, and Growth

  • Lead the vision, strategy, and execution of AFC's signature events, fundraising events, and client-centered events, ensuring each event aligns with organizational priorities, mission, and revenue goals.
  • Develop and implement a long-term strategy to grow event revenue, strengthen return on investment (ROI), and elevate the quality and overall experience of AFC's event portfolio.
  • Independently assess event performance, revenue, expenses, audience engagement, and pipeline potential to identify opportunities for optimization, cost management, and revenue growth.
  • Develop new event concepts, formats, and partnership opportunities that expand AFC's reach, diversify revenue opportunities, and strengthen the donor and supporter pipeline.
  • Establish event goals, timelines, priorities, and success measures and independently drive projects from concept through completion.

Revenue Generation and Expansion

  • Lead revenue-generation strategies related to events, including sponsorships, ticket sales, tables, donations, and other event-related opportunities.
  • Establish revenue targets and develop strategies and systems to meet or exceed established goals.
  • Grow and deepen revenue generated through AFC's existing signature events and identify new event opportunities that contribute to the organization's financial sustainability.
  • Collaborate with the Chief Development Officer to integrate event donors, attendees, and sponsors into broader fundraising strategies, including cultivation, engagement, and stewardship.
  • Identify and pursue opportunities to develop corporate partnerships, sponsorships, in-kind support, and other strategic revenue relationships.

Leadership Mobilization and Community Engagement

  • Recruit, mobilize, and empower volunteer leadership, including event co-chairs, host committees, table captains, prospectors, and community ambassadors, to expand each event's reach and impact.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with supporters who can connect AFC to new sponsors, donors, corporations, foundations, community partners, and prospective event participants.
  • Serve as a key connector between AFC and the broader community, positioning events as opportunities for meaningful engagement and long-term philanthropic support.
  • Represent AFC professionally and authentically with external stakeholders, community leaders, corporate partners, donors, and supporters.
  • Foster inclusive and culturally responsive event experiences that reflect AFC's mission and the communities it serves.

Event Production and Project Management

  • Independently oversee all aspects of event production from concept through execution, including timelines, budgets, venues, vendors, contracts, communications, collateral, program development, guest experience, and run-of-show.
  • Manage event budgets with discipline, ensuring appropriate expense control, strategic investment, and strong ROI.
  • Negotiate vendor contracts and manage vendor relationships to secure high-quality services, control costs, and maximize value.
  • Anticipate operational and logistical challenges and develop solutions and contingency plans to ensure successful event execution.
  • Ensure events reflect AFC's mission, values, and culture, including appropriately uplifting client voices and showcasing AFC's impact.

Cross-Department Collaboration

  • Partner closely with Development leadership and directors across the organization to ensure events support donor cultivation, institutional giving strategies, communications goals, and community engagement.
  • Work closely with Communications to ensure consistent branding, messaging, creative assets, marketing, and promotion across all events.
  • Coordinate with Program teams to create meaningful client-centered events that honor youth experiences and strengthen community connection.
  • Maintain proactive communication with internal stakeholders while independently managing day-to-day event responsibilities and decisions.
  • Provide leadership with timely updates regarding progress, revenue performance, risks, challenges, and matters requiring organizational input.

Data, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement

  • Use event, donor, audience, and financial data to sharpen event strategy and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.
  • Track progress toward revenue goals and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including revenue, expenses, attendance, sponsorships, engagement, and ROI.
  • Provide timely and accurate reporting to Development leadership and Executive Leadership.
  • Evaluate each event following completion, documenting outcomes, lessons learned, challenges, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Create and maintain systems, processes, and feedback loops that improve event planning, execution, accountability, and organizational knowledge.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to improve efficiency, strengthen revenue performance, and enhance the overall event experience.

title: Refrigeration Piping / Low Voltage Foreman
description:
Refrigeration Piping / Low Voltage Foreman

New Construction HVAC Division

Reports To: HVAC Superintendent

Location: Greater Phoenix, AZ. Corporate Office: 303 W Elliott Rd, Suite 101, Tempe, AZ 85284

Compensation: $35.00 - $40.00 hourly

POSITION SUMMARY

The Refrigeration Piping / Low Voltage Foreman is a supporting field leadership role within the new construction HVAC division. This is a working foreman position that leads and works hands-on alongside the self-perform refrigeration piping crew and owns the field execution of low voltage systems, equipment start-up, and commissioning support. The Foreman is the field-level owner of making the mechanical system run, and proving that it runs: refrigerant piping installed to specification, low voltage controls terminated and functional, factory and equipment start-ups completed and documented, and commissioning checklists tracked and closed out. The Foreman also coordinates and quality-checks the controls subcontractor to keep the mechanical system on schedule and functionally complete.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Refrigeration Piping (Self-Perform)

  • Lead installation of refrigerant piping systems, including brazing, pressure testing, evacuation, and charging, to specification, code, and manufacturer requirements.
  • Manage crew productivity, layout, material staging, and daily manpower loading against the project schedule.
  • Enforce clean, code-compliant, inspection-ready workmanship and correct deficiencies before they reach punchlist.

Low Voltage & Controls Support

  • Install and terminate low voltage wiring, thermostats, relays, sensors, and functional control components for HVAC equipment.
  • Verify point-to-point functionality of low voltage devices prior to start-up and commissioning.
  • Troubleshoot low voltage faults during start-up and functional testing.

Controls Subcontractor Oversight

  • Coordinate the controls subcontractor's field sequencing, access, and readiness against the mechanical schedule.
  • Quality-check controls subcontractor work for completeness and functional readiness; flag deficiencies to the Project Manager and Superintendent.
  • Coordinate, schedule, and inspect the controls subcontractor in the field; route all scope direction, contractual instruction, and change-generating decisions through the Project Manager.

Equipment & Factory Start-Up

  • Perform and lead equipment start-ups and verify systems operate to design and manufacturer specifications.
  • Schedule, host, and oversee manufacturer and factory start-up technicians; confirm all pre-start prerequisites are complete before the factory representative arrives.
  • Capture and resolve start-up deficiencies before turnover.

Commissioning

  • Own the field commissioning process for assigned scope, including building and tracking commissioning checklists, schedules, and functional test readiness.
  • Complete and maintain commissioning documentation in Facility Grid and other required software, keeping status current and defensible.
  • Serve as the field point of contact for the commissioning agent, general contractor, and owner's representative on functional performance items.

Documentation, Field Leadership & Safety

  • Submit accurate and timely daily field reports; maintain start-up records, test reports, and commissioning logs for the turnover package.
  • Set the pace, quality standard, and safety expectation for the crew; participate in daily safety huddles and hazard analysis.
  • Enforce Tempe Mechanical safety policies and maintain compliance with EPA, OSHA, and local regulations.
  • Support scheduling, look-ahead planning, and coordination with other trades and the general contractor.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Journeyman-level refrigeration and HVAC piping experience on commercial projects.
  • EPA Section 608 Universal certification (refrigerant handling) - required.
  • Demonstrated brazing proficiency.
  • Working knowledge of low voltage HVAC controls, thermostats, relays, and sensor wiring.
  • Ability to read and execute mechanical drawings, control diagrams, and equipment submittals.
  • Valid Arizona driver's license and clean driving record.
  • Preferred: prior commissioning experience and familiarity with Facility Grid or comparable software, manufacturer start-up certifications (e.g., VRF, chiller, or rooftop unit platforms), experience coordinating controls or BAS subcontractors on new construction, and OSHA 30; bilingual (English/Spanish) a plus.

BENEFITS

  • Medical Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • Company Events & Team Culture
  • Profit Sharing Retirement Plan
  • ZayZoon - Wages on Demand
  • 6 Paid Holidays
  • 48 Hours of Paid Time Off
  • 40 Hours of Sick Time

OUR PROMISE

Tempe Mechanical is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

title: Inventory and Systems Leader
description: Job Title: Inventory Systems Lead Salary Range: CAD$82,447 – CAD$103,059 Working Type: On-Site PURPOSE OF ROLE The Inventory Systems Leader owns end-to-end inventory accuracy, warehouse systems performance, and automation reliability within an automated food production environment. The role ensures alignment between physical inventory and system records, stable and effective use of warehouse and material handling systems (e.g., WCS and ERP), and uninterrupted operational flow. This role acts as the single operational authority bridging inventory control, system governance, and on-floor execution, driving strong team performance, system discipline, and continuous improvement. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES Inventory Control Accuracy Hold full accountability for inventory accuracy across all stock types and systems Lead cycle counts, reconciliations, adjustments, and investigations of inventory discrepancies Ensure proper stock rotation (FEFO), expiry management, and traceability Minimize shrink, write-offs, and obsolescence through robust controls and root cause analysis Maintain inventory accuracy during peak demand, system changes, and operational disruptions Understand and consider inventory valuation, write-offs, and working capital impacts when managing inventory accuracy and corrective actions. Systems Ownership Governance Own the performance, governance, stability and effective operational use of warehouse IT and automation systems, including ERP, WCS and associated system interfaces. Act as the operational system subject matter expert, supporting issue triage, detailed diagnostics, root cause analysis and resolution of recurring system faults. Review system logs, alarms, event histories, transactions and other diagnostic information to identify failure points and support fault investigation. Establish and maintain system monitoring and diagnostic routines, using system and performance data to identify emerging and recurring issues. Ensure accurate, real-time transactions and data integrity across inventory and automation systems. Monitor operational system usage and identify behaviours, process gaps or recurring failures that negatively affect system performance. Maintain clear records of system incidents, known problems, RCA findings, corrective actions and system performance trends. Act as the principal operational and technical interface with IT, engineering, supplier help desks and automation vendors during incidents and technical investigations. Raise and manage system incident and problem tickets, providing appropriate logs, evidence and operational context, and following actions through to resolution. Support system changes, fixes, upgrades and deployments through impact assessment, testing, validation and operational feedback. Validate technical SOPs, recovery procedures and system operating practices, ensuring lessons from incidents and system changes are embedded into operational processes and key-user training. Ensure appropriate system access controls, user discipline and data governance standards are maintained in line with site and corporate requirements. Support major system incidents, including investigation, recovery, documentation and post-incident review. Use incident trends, operational observations and system data to identify improvement opportunities and reduce recurring failures. Support service reviews with system and automation vendors, providing evidence on reliability, recurring faults, responsiveness and service levels. Team Leadership Capability Development Lead, coach, and develop the inventory and systems team and other operational teams where required. Set clear expectations, drive accountability, and monitor performance, productivity, and accuracy Ensure training completion and system competency across the team and key operational users Lead teams effectively through periods of change, disruption, and peak operational demand Operational Cross-Functional Coordination Partner with inbound, outbound, and production teams to ensure smooth operational flow Minimize operational disruptions linked to system issues Support production, shipping, and customer service through accurate inventory and reliable systems Process Improvement Capability Building Drive continuous improvement using system data and operational insights Identify gaps in inventory and system processes and lead sustainable improvements Develop, validate, and maintain SOPs related to inventory and system use Train and coach key users to build strong system and inventory capability across the operation Safety, Quality Compliance Ensure inventory and system operations comply with food safety, quality, and regulatory requirements Support audits, investigations, and corrective actions related to inventory accuracy, traceability, or system integrity Maintain audit readiness and accurate documentation at all times Support product holds, quarantines, recalls, and escalations in line with site procedures KEY EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND WORKING CONDITIONS Essential 3+ years’ experience in leading inventory operations within warehouse, manufacturing, or food production environments Strong knowledge of inventory control processes including cycle counts, reconciliations, discrepancy investigation, and root cause analysis Experience with warehouse automation and a strong understanding of automation and ERP systems, with a focus on inventory transactions, data integrity, and system diagnostics Ability to understand and interpret technical specifications, interface definitions and communication protocols. description:
Job Title: Helpdesk Specialist (Aqualab)

Department: Revenue Ops - Client Success

Reports To: Helpdesk Manager

Location: Pullman, WA or Remote (US)

Compensation: $60,000 - $70,000


Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Addium, Inc. does not sponsor employment visas now or in the future.


About Addium

Addium is a leading ag-tech company uniting science, sensors, and software to deliver end-to-end solutions in agriculture and food safety. Serving 34,000+ global clients with 60M+ daily sensor readings, we turn raw data into actionable insights that conserve resources, improve food safety, and drive measurable impact. Our mission is to make the invisible visible—transforming data into clarity, action, and automation. Trusted by partners like Mondelez, PepsiCo, Ferrero, and Green Thumb Industries, we stand for innovation, reliability, and a bold commitment to the future of agriculture.


Position Summary

The Helpdesk Specialist is the first point of contact for AQUALAB customers who need technical help with their instruments, software, and service requests. This role resolves support cases quickly and accurately, coordinates with internal teams when issues need escalation, and helps customers get the most out of our products and self-service tools. Above all, the Helpdesk Specialist represents AQUALAB's commitment to customer service as a differentiator, treating every customer interaction with the professionalism and care our customers expect.


Key Responsibilities

Case Management and Customer Support

  • Manage and resolve technical support cases in Salesforce, keeping customers informed from first contact through resolution.
  • Troubleshoot instrument, software, and connectivity issues by phone, email, and video, escalating complex issues to the appropriate team when needed.
  • Communicate clearly and professionally with customers, setting accurate expectations and following through on every commitment.
  • Document case details, actions taken, and root causes accurately so the team can track trends and improve service.


Self-Service Portal Support

  • Guide customers through registering for and using the self-service portal, including calibration and service requests.
  • Resolve account setup issues and create missing instrument assets on customer accounts so customers can request service without delays.


Cross-Departmental Coordination

  • Support the onboarding calendar for Vapor Sorption Analyzer (VSA) customers in collaboration with Sales Engineering and Laboratory Sciences.
  • Coordinate with the Repairs Manager on loaner instruments, follow-ups, and escalations.
  • Work with the Shipping Manager to address urgent shipping concerns.
  • Partner with the Receiving Team to resolve issues with incoming instruments.


Continuous Improvement

  • Share feedback on recurring customer issues and suggest improvements to support processes in Salesforce and NetSuite.
  • Participate in ongoing technical training to build deeper troubleshooting expertise across AQUALAB's product lines.


Who We're Looking For?

We are looking for the right person more than the perfect résumé. The ideal candidate has an outstanding, customer-first personality and genuinely enjoys helping people solve problems. You bring positive energy to every call, stay calm and confident under pressure, and take ownership until the customer's issue is fully resolved. You understand that every interaction shapes how customers feel about AQUALAB, and you hold yourself to a high standard of service every time.
Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field is preferred; equivalent technical certifications or relevant experience will be considered.
  • Minimum of 5 years in technical support, customer support, or another customer-facing technical role.
  • Experience with case management systems is preferred; hands-on experience with Salesforce and NetSuite is highly desirable.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to customers.
  • Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities.
  • Strong organizational and multitasking skills, with the ability to stay composed in high-pressure situations.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with internal teams and external customers.


Preferred:

  • A background in food science, including experience in food manufacturing, R&D, or product formulation.
  • A degree or coursework in food science.
  • Familiarity with laboratory instruments or quality control processes.


What We Offer

  • Competitive salary
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan with a company match (up to 4% after your first year)
  • Paid Time Off, Sick Leave, and 11 Paid Holidays
  • Company-paid life and disability insurance
  • HSA with company contribution and FSA options
  • A small, focused team that moves fast and gives you the room to actually build something

All qualified applicants are considered regardless of ethnicity, nationality, gender, veteran or disability status, religion, age, sexual orientation or gender identity, or other protected status.

title: FT - Human Resource Business Partner
description:
ROLE PURPOSE
Connective is a non-profit organization delivering a range of social services, with over 1,300 employees, the large majority members of one of three bargaining units (CUPE, BCGEU, and the Yukon Employees Union). Connective is committed to providing high-quality, person-centred programs and services to the communities we serve.
People are at the core of Connective's success. The HR Business Partner is the primary HR resource for the Service Delivery VP and their leadership team. This is not a generalist role and it is not a service desk. It is a strategic partnership — the HRBP works alongside operational leaders to understand their people challenges, anticipate workforce needs, and deliver HR solutions that enable the region to achieve its service delivery objectives.
The HRBP operates within Connective's three-pillar HR model. Transactional HR work is handled by Shared Services. Specialist programs and policies are owned by Centers of Excellence. The HRBP's role is to bring those resources to bear on the strategic people needs of their region — translating organizational priorities into workforce plans, coaching leaders through complex people situations, and ensuring HR activity in the region is aligned with Connective's overall direction.
Success in this role requires seasoned HR experience, strong business judgment, and the ability to build genuine credibility with operational leaders. The HRBP must be equally comfortable advising on a sensitive employee relations matter and contributing to a regional workforce planning conversation. Independence of judgment, proactive thinking, and a high degree of discretion are essential.
STATUS AND CLASSIFICATION
Exempt. This position is open to applicants of all genders.
HOURS
40 hours per week; Monday to Friday, 0830-1630.
This position requires the ability to work flexible hours based on operational needs.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
Strategic HR Partnership

  • Serve as the primary HR resource for the VP, Service Delivery and their leadership team, providing proactive and responsive strategic HR advice across all people matters
  • Partner with the regional VP to assess short and long-term workforce needs and develop HR strategies that support operational objectives
  • Contribute to regional workforce planning — headcount forecasting, succession considerations, capability gaps, and organizational design
  • Translate Connective's organizational priorities into regional people strategies, ensuring alignment between HR activity and service delivery goals
  • Advise on organizational structure and role design as the region evolves, including in the context of Connective's provincial expansion plans

Employee Relations and People Management Support

  • Provide advice and guidance to managers on complex employee relations matters including performance management, misconduct, attendance management, conflict resolution, and terminations
  • Conduct or oversee workplace investigations into allegations of employee misconduct, providing written reports and recommendations to management
  • Coach managers to build their people management capability — helping them handle situations independently over time, not creating dependency on HR
  • Support leaders in applying Connective's HR policies consistently and in compliance with the BC Employment Standards Act, Human Rights Code, WorkSafeBC requirements, and other applicable legislation
  • Advise on sensitive and confidential employee situations with discretion, sound judgment, and a clear understanding of legal risk

Talent and Workforce Planning

  • Partner with the Talent Acquisition Business Partner to identify regional hiring needs, contribute to sourcing strategy, and support hiring manager capability in the region
  • Identify and advise on retention risks within the region, working with leaders and CoE colleagues to develop targeted responses
  • Support succession conversations and talent identification within the regional leadership team
  • Contribute to onboarding effectiveness for new managers and key hires in the region

Change Management and Organizational Effectiveness

  • Partner with Learning & Development and Change Management Lead to design and support change management approaches for organizational changes, restructures, or strategic initiatives within the region
  • Develop targeted communication plans to support employees through change, in alignment with Connective's broader communications and change strategy
  • Identify organizational effectiveness issues — team dynamics, structural friction, manager capability gaps — and partner with Learning & Development and Change Management Lead to develop approaches to address them •

Contribute to building a healthy, engaged, and high-performing regional workforce culture
Policy, Compliance and HR Excellence

  • Interpret and advise managers on Connective's HR policies, ensuring consistent application across the region
  • Ensure HR activity in the region complies with applicable employment legislation — BC Employment Standards Act, Human Rights Code, WorkSafeBC, and any relevant legislation in other provinces as Connective expands
  • Collaborate with the ER & Compliance Lead on complex compliance matters, investigations, and policy development
  • Partner with the Total Rewards Lead to ensure compensation decisions in the region are consistent with Connective's framework and internally equitable
  • Use HR data and people analytics to identify trends, inform decisions, and report on regional people metrics to the VP

HR HR Function Contribution

  • Operate as an active member of the HR Business Partner team — sharing knowledge, calibrating approach, and contributing to consistent HR practice across all regions
  • Contribute to the development and refinement of HR programs, policies, and tools in collaboration with CoE colleagues
  • Participate in the broader HR transformation — this role is part of building a new function, not maintaining an existing one

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Function independently, while remaining a crucial member of the support team
  • Adhere to Connective policies and procedures
  • Be available to work flexible hours as needed. May include some evenings/weekends, as determined by the regional office needs and schedules

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS
Required

  • Minimum seven years of progressive HR experience as a generalist or HR business partner, with demonstrated experience advising operational leaders on complex people matters
  • Proven ability to build trusted relationships with business leaders and influence decisions without formal authority
  • Solid working knowledge of BC employment legislation including the Employment Standards Act, Human Rights Code, and WorkSafeBC requirements
  • Experience supporting employee relations matters end to end — from initial advice through to investigation, outcome, and documentation
  • Demonstrated experience with performance management, attendance management, and workplace conflict resolution • Strong written and verbal communication skills — able to translate complex HR concepts into clear, actionable advice for operational leaders
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and exercise independent judgment in a fast-paced, multi-site environment
  • Post-secondary degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field, OR demonstrated equivalency through progressive experience and professional development

Preferred

  • Chartered Professional in Human Resources (CPHR) designation or active pursuit
  • Experience working in a social services, healthcare, community services, or similarly mission-driven non-profit organization
  • Familiarity with multi-province employment obligations — particularly BC, Alberta, and Yukon
  • Experience supporting organizational change or restructure • Experience working in or alongside a unionized environment

Competencies

  • Business acumen — understands how the organization works, not just how HR works. Asks the right questions before offering solutions.
  • Trusted advisor — builds credibility quickly with operational leaders. Respected for judgment, not just knowledge.
  • Execution and follow-through — does what they say they will do. Manages multiple relationships and priorities without dropping the ball.
  • Judgment in complexity — comfortable operating in ambiguous, sensitive situations. Knows when to escalate and when to resolve.
  • Proactive thinking — anticipates people issues before they become crises. Brings solutions, not just analysis.
  • Commitment to equity and inclusion — ensures HR advice and practice is fair, consistent, and free from systemic bias.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to successfully complete a Vulnerable Persons Criminal Records Check
  • Ability to successfully pass a reference check

COMPENSATION
The salary range for this position is $87,000 to $108,700. Annual salary will be negotiated based on experience and qualifications. This role will also be eligible for Connective's comprehensive benefits package.

Important: Candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada, observe their weekly hours limit if under a temporary or study visa, and provide proof of eligibility if selected for the role.

The role serves as the technical intake point between users and Tier 2/3 teams, ensuring issues are accurately diagnosed, reproducible, and fully documented prior to escalation.

  • Perform structured troubleshooting using documented workflows and root-cause isolation techniques
  • Resolve Windows OS issues including profile corruption, OS configuration, patching, and driver-related problems

  • Administer Active Directory objects (users, groups) following least-privilege standards
  • Create, modify, disable, and audit Microsoft 365 user accounts, mailboxes, licenses, and group memberships
  • Troubleshoot Microsoft 365 services (Outlook connectivity, Teams issues, OneDrive sync, SharePoint access)
  • Perform basic network diagnostics (IP configuration, DNS resolution, gateway reachability, latency symptoms)
  • Use RDP and approved remote support tools for endpoint and application troubleshooting
  • Deploy and image workstations using standard build procedures and deployment tools
  • Install, update, and license approved software packages
  • Maintain accurate CMDB/asset records and ticket documentation
  • Identify recurring incidents and potential systemic issues and escalate with supporting evidence

title: Director of Membership
description:
Director of Membership

Hiring Range: $66,550 - $76,000

On-site in Lake Worth, FL

Girl Scouts of Southeast Florida has a fantastic opportunity available for a Director of Membership!

The Director of Membership leads the Council's strategy for growing and retaining membership across Southeast Florida. This role is responsible for understanding where our greatest opportunities exist, developing strategies to reach and convert prospective members, strengthening troop formation and placement, and improving renewal and retention throughout the membership lifecycle.

As our Director of Membership, you will use data, community insights, and membership trends to identify priority markets, set goals, develop recruitment and retention strategies, and evaluate what is working. You will help shape how GSSEF attracts girls and adult members, converts interest into membership, creates sustainable troop opportunities, and keeps members engaged year after year.

Reporting to the Vice President of Mission Design, you will serve as the Council's functional leader and subject-matter expert for membership growth, recruitment, conversion, troop formation, renewal, and retention.

You will work closely with Mission Delivery to turn membership priorities into actionable initiatives, providing the strategy, goals, target audiences, measures of success, and functional direction needed for effective execution. You will also collaborate across departments to identify and remove barriers throughout the member journey, from initial interest and registration through placement, participation, renewal, and retention.

On any given day, you may be:

  • Analyzing membership trends and identifying communities, schools, or geographic areas with growth potential
  • Developing Council-wide recruitment, conversion, renewal, and retention strategies
  • Designing membership campaigns in partnership with Marketing, and defining target audiences, goals, timelines, and measures of success
  • Evaluating the membership pipeline to identify where prospective members are getting stuck or disengaging
  • Building community partnerships that create new pathways to membership
  • Using CRM, pipeline, and performance data to recommend changes in strategy
  • Establishing and monitoring Service Unit membership goals
  • Working across departments to improve the overall experience for our members

Who are we seeking?

  • Someone with strong knowledge of membership development, recruitment, customer acquisition, retention, and relationship-management strategies.
  • A strategic thinker who can translate organizational goals and market opportunities into clear membership priorities, initiatives, and measurable outcomes.
  • Someone who understands the relationship between recruitment, conversion, member experience, engagement, renewal, and retention.
  • A data-driven leader who can interpret membership trends, pipeline data, performance indicators, and operational information and turn those insights into action.
  • A strong problem solver that can collaborate with others to develop practical solutions.
  • An experienced leader who can provide functional direction, influence outcomes, and drive execution across teams without direct supervisory authority.
  • Strong project-management and organizational skills, including the ability to establish priorities, define outcomes, manage multiple initiatives, and evaluate results.
  • A relationship builder who can develop productive partnerships with schools, community organizations, volunteers, funders, and other stakeholders.
  • Strong judgment, problem-solving, critical-thinking, and decision-making skills.
  • Experience with customer relationship management systems and the effective use of technology and data to support growth and retention. Salesforce or similar CRM experience is strongly preferred.

What else will you need?

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in membership development, recruitment, sales, customer acquisition, nonprofit growth, or a related field.
  • Experience working in a nonprofit, membership-based, youth-serving, or mission-driven organization is preferred.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience working in a goal-oriented, outcome-driven recruitment, sales, membership growth, or comparable environment.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and implementing strategies tied to measurable recruitment, growth, conversion, retention, or customer/member outcomes.
  • Demonstrated experience using data, performance measures, and CRM or pipeline information to evaluate results and inform strategy.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives or teams is strongly preferred.
  • Bilingual proficiency in Spanish or French is preferred.
  • Ability to work in person at our Lake Worth Administrative Headquarters and work additional hours, including evenings and weekends, as required to meet business needs.
  • Access to reliable transportation and a valid Florida driver's license with a satisfactory driving record and eligibility for coverage under applicable Council insurance.

What will you get?

  • We are an energetic group that works really hard, but we also like to have lots of FUN! We're building future leaders of tomorrow, so we provide development opportunities that foster both professional and personal growth and an exceptional benefits package that includes paid holidays; a summer shut-down and a winter break!
  • We provide an exceptional work environment; vacation and sick time; subsidized medical and dental insurance; free Teladoc, employee assistance program access, life and disability insurance; and offer for employees to fund through payroll deductions additional life insurance, an FSA, a pre-paid legal plan, and vision coverage. Team members also receive discounts at our Council shop and are eligible to participate in a 401-K plan with employer match from day one with no vesting period!
  • In addition, all team members are invited to join our Culture and Inclusion in Action team, participate in Dog Days of Summer, Health & Wellness challenges, and enjoy a 4-day work week with remote Mondays after an introductory period!

How do you apply?

Complete our online application in consideration for an opportunity to begin your career in Girl Scouting today!

If you are ready to turn data, community insight, and strategy into meaningful membership growth, apply today to become our Director of Membership and help more girls and families find their place in Girl Scouts.

Girl Scouts of Southeast Florida, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States for any employer. Girl Scouts of Southeast Florida does not sponsor applicants for work visas. Note: This posting may be closed or canceled at any time based on business needs.

title: Associate II - Facilities
description:

Computer Skills (Word, Excel, Asana).

Employee Assistance Program

This role is based in our San Francisco location.

title: Senior Data Architect
description:
Senior Data Architect – Digital Regulatory Assurance System (DRAS)

Client: Government of Alberta (GoA) – Environment & Protected Areas
Position: Data Architect
Location: Remote – Canada
Work Location: Remote; resource must work from within Canada
Maximum Rate: $100 CAD/hour
Contract Hours: 739.5 hours
Hours: 36.25 hours/week
Work Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:15 AM–4:30 PM Alberta Time, with a 1-hour lunch
Expected Interview Dates: October 20–23, 2026
Travel: None

About the Role
The Government of Alberta is modernizing how it regulates and assures environmental outcomes across the province through the Digital Regulatory Assurance System (DRAS).
DRAS supports applications, approvals, compliance, and monitoring activities that protect Alberta’s air, land, water, and biodiversity.
The Government of Alberta is seeking an experienced Data Architect to design and lead data integration between DRAS, the Databricks-based Data Management Platform, and the Alberta Geospatial Platform.
The successful candidate will define how regulatory, environmental, and spatial data is modeled, integrated, governed, secured, and delivered across these platforms. The objective is to provide trusted, timely, high-quality, and reusable data for regulators, decision-makers, and Albertans.
The Data Architect will work within a multidisciplinary Agile team consisting of data engineers, developers, GIS specialists, business analysts, and product owners.
Key Responsibilities
Data Architecture & Design
  • Define and maintain the target-state data architecture for integrating DRAS, Databricks Data Management Platform, and the Alberta Geospatial Platform.
  • Design conceptual, logical, and physical data models for regulatory, environmental, and geospatial data.
  • Define enterprise integration patterns including:
    • Batch processing, Near-real-time integration, Event-driven architecture, REST/API-based integration, Change Data Capture (CDC)
  • Design Databricks Lakehouse architecture using:
    • Bronze/Silver/Gold medallion architecture, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Apache Spark, PySpark, SQL
  • Architect spatial data flows while preserving geometry, coordinate reference systems, spatial accuracy, and data integrity.
Data Integration & Delivery
  • Lead the architecture and design of data pipelines and interfaces between enterprise systems.
  • Work closely with data engineers, developers, GIS specialists, and technical teams during implementation.
  • Define data contracts, API specifications, interface agreements, and integration standards.
  • Resolve complex integration challenges involving:
    • Data quality, Schema changes, Latency, Data dependencies, System interoperability
  • Translate architecture into actionable requirements and user stories within an Agile/Scrum environment.
  • Participate in sprint planning, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, and other Agile ceremonies.
Data Governance, Security & Quality
  • Establish and apply data governance practices covering:
    • Metadata management, Data lineage, Data classification, Master data, Reference data, Data quality
  • Ensure architecture aligns with Government of Alberta security, privacy, information management, and records-management standards.
  • Apply appropriate role-based access controls (RBAC) and data-sharing policies.
  • Define data-quality rules, validation frameworks, monitoring approaches, and controls.
  • Perform and support threat and risk assessments and provide recommendations.
Leadership & Stakeholder Collaboration
  • Act as a trusted Data Architecture advisor to program leadership, product owners, business stakeholders, and technical teams.
  • Translate complex regulatory and business requirements into effective data architecture solutions.
  • Collaborate with Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, GIS, platform teams, and other Government of Alberta ministries.
  • Ensure architecture aligns with Government of Alberta standards, enterprise roadmaps, and technology strategies.
  • Produce high-quality:
    • Architecture documents, Data models, Architecture diagrams, Decision records, Technical recommendations
  • Provide technical leadership, mentoring, planning, estimating, and presentations.
  • Explain complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.


Requirements

Mandatory Qualifications
Education
  • College or bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering, Geomatics, or a related field.
Required Experience
The candidate must demonstrate the following experience within specific jobs/projects:
  • 8+ years designing, planning, implementing, and supporting enterprise solutions.
  • 8+ years documenting enterprise solution databases within an enterprise IT environment.
  • 6+ years performing threat and risk assessments and presenting recommendations.
  • Demonstrated experience providing leadership, planning, estimating, and presentations.
  • 8+ years of experience applying enterprise architecture principles and associated best practices.
  • 8+ years working as a Data Architect in an enterprise IT environment.
  • 7+ years progressive experience in data architecture, data engineering, or data integration, including at least 3 years in a Data Architect role.
  • Hands-on experience designing solutions using Databricks, including:
    • Delta Lake, Apache Spark, PySpark, SQL, Unity Catalog
  • Strong experience with:
    • Relational data modelling, Dimensional data modelling, Lakehouse architecture
  • Enterprise integration experience with:
    • REST APIs, ETL/ELT, Event streaming, Change Data Capture (CDC)
  • Experience with cloud data platforms, preferably Microsoft Azure, including:
