title: Employment Coach - Antioch and Concord
description:
Location: Concord,California,United States

EMPLOYMENT COACH

Economic stability through immediate employment is a primary concern and priority for a vast majority of Rubicon participants. Within the Pathways phased service approach, the Employment Coach works within the Employment Services component and provides the first phase of services by focusing on securing immediate short-term employment and/or income support to stabilize participants’ lives. The Employment Coach provides job readiness training and support through group and individualized support services designed to help participants develop essential skills (job readiness, resume, cover letter, and reference list development, master application completion, internet job search skills, etc.) needed to successfully identify and secure immediate employment. The Employment Coach integrates technology into the job search and job readiness programming to help participants build their digital literacy skills.

To help build participant self-efficacy and higher order thinking skills, Pathways is designed as an intentionally self-driven employment and career services model. The Employment Coach works dynamically and collaboratively with participants using employment coaching, job search assistance, and project-based learning tools and strategies to prepare participants for a successful job search. Additionally, the Employment Coach understands the unique challenges faced by individuals from socially and economically marginalized backgrounds and knows how to adapt and apply established, as well as innovative, employment coaching and job search strategies to meet their needs. To be effective in this approach, the Employment Coach maintains consistent engagement with the participant’s Impact Coach and the Business Services Representative/Employer Relations Specialist to ensure the participant feels supported throughout the process.

This position is part of a program pilot with responsibilities and program delivery strategies anticipated to evolve over time; in addition to the competencies detailed below, innovation, initiative and a tolerance for ambiguity will therefore be critical competencies for success. Researching, developing and applying innovative job search tools and strategies will be required to prepare participants for a successful job search within the Pathways model.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Assist participants in identifying, selecting, and applying for open positions matching their qualifications. This involves sharing timely employment information and resources and promoting Rubicon’s Job Connect for access to employer job orders and leads.
  • Provide individual and group employment readiness workshops, discussion groups, and/or classes based on participant needs, including resume development, interviewing skills, and online job search resources and strategies.
  • Provide participants with ongoing coaching and support throughout the job search process; collaborate with the Impact Coach and Workforce Liaison for service coordination as needed; motivate participants to achieve goals and provide participants with honest, productive feedback.
  • Coordinate employment readiness workshops and oversight of the computer lab and lab volunteers; assess participant level of computer proficiency and assist them in the use of the computers including accessing MS Word, Excel, and Outlook in support of their job search activities.

COMPETENCIES

  • Strong experience and expertise with employment readiness training and/or effective job search strategies.
  • Solid workshop facilitation skills and abilities, computer and internet proficiency.
  • Teamwork, interpersonal flexibility, excellent organization and communication skills, and the ability to inspire others.
  • Cultural responsiveness and an alignment with our values and commitment to equity and inclusion.
  • If you don't currently possess Rubicon's organizational core competencies of Trauma Informed Care, Motivational Interviewing, and Coaching, Rubicon provides necessary training.

This position requires travel between Antioch and Concord and to other Rubicon meetings. If the employee opts to meet these travel requirements by driving, proof of a valid and current driver's license, current auto insurance, and an acceptable Motor Vehicle Report are required.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

  • $23-25/hour.
  • Medical, Dental and Vision health plans. .
  • 3 weeks paid vacation and sick leave, 13 paid holidays.
  • 4 days paid restorative holiday between Christmas and New Years.
  • Employer sponsored retirement plan.

Rubicon is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and values diversity of culture, thought, and lived experiences. We seek talented, qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, marital status, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, conviction history, uniform service membership/veteran status, physical or mental disability, protected medical conditions, genetic characteristics, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression regardless of physical gender, or any other consideration made unlawful by federal, state, or local laws.

Rubicon uses E-Verify to validate the eligibility of our new employees to work legally in the United States.

About Rubicon

An $18M non-profit Rubicon, provides direct services at eight locations in Alameda and Contra Costa counties and operates a growing commercial landscape social enterprise program that is a leader in sustainable practices. Rubicon transforms East Bay communities by equipping people to break the cycle of poverty. Recognized as a national leader in workforce development, Rubicon provides individualized one-on-one career advising, job search support, financial education, wellness and legal services, to very low-income people who face significant barriers to achieving economic mobility.

Rubicon is a 2022 Great Place to Work, on a journey towards becoming a high-road employer and an anti-racist organization. We are committed to systems change and advocacy through efforts like expanding and deepening Employee Resource Groups; the launch of an internal Racial Justice Task Force; and implementation of talent and culture supports that acknowledge and facilitate healing from the direct and indirect effects of racial trauma.

Rubicon actively recruits staff members with a diversity of culture, thought, and lived experiences who are not only highly skilled, but who consistently demonstrate a commitment to our vision of an East Bay without poverty and are passionate about this work.

title: Staff Scientist/Engineer - Acoustics
description:
ABOUT EPSILON

Epsilon is one of the best known and most respected environmental consulting firms in the northeast United States. Epsilon’s client base includes major energy, commercial real estate, aviation, institutional and residential developers, as well as local and state public agencies. As a well-established, mid-sized firm, we are large enough to support our team members professionally and personally, and small enough to keep our focus on project successes and client satisfaction. Epsilon is privately held by its Principals, who are experts in their fields and work side-by-side with staff of all levels on complex, high-profile and interesting projects.


POSITION SUMMARY

Epsilon is seeking a full-time staff scientist or engineer to work as part of the Epsilon team on a wide range of environmental licensing, permitting and compliance projects. This hybrid position will encompass work primarily in the Acoustics Group in our Maynard, MA office.


In the Acoustics Group, the successful candidate will assist with community sound level measurement programs, meteorological data collection, data analysis, shadow flicker analyses for wind turbines, sound level modeling, and report preparation. This position requires periodic field work as well as overnight, out-of-state travel.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS

The ideal candidate will have:

· 0-3 years of experience in a consulting environment,

· B.S. or B.A. in Acoustics, Engineering, Environmental or Physical Sciences, or Physics,

· Experience in using sound level measurement and meteorological equipment,

· Experience with ISO 9613-2 sound modeling software (i.e. CadnaA, SoundPLAN)

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office

· Superior written and verbal communication skills, and

· Ability to work cooperatively as part of a multidisciplinary project team.


In addition to the Preferred Qualifications, the Candidate must have a valid driver’s license to operate a motor vehicle for business travel, including proper insurance and registration, and have all necessary paperwork to work in the USA.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR THE JOB

The Candidate must:

· Be able to work safely outside in variable weather conditions for an extended period of time, as necessary,

· Work on a computer for extended periods of time,

· Be able to travel outside of the state via plane or car, for extended period of time, and

· Be able to carry approximately 50 pounds on either paved paths, trails, or in fields.


SALARY RANGE

Epsilon's pay range for this position is $60,000-$80,000 USD per year. Pay is commensurate with experience and other job-related factors including but not limited to credentials, skill, and geographic location.


WORKING CONDITIONS IN WHICH THE DUTIES ARE PERFORMED

Epsilon maintains a professional office located in an historic mill in Maynard, MA. Office space is recently renovated, clean, quiet, and friendly.


Our team members enjoy regular opportunities for professional growth, a relaxed and flexible work environment, a competitive base salary, a 401k plan with a generous company match, profit sharing, an annual performance bonus program, and a full benefits package.


Epsilon is an equal opportunity employer that recognizes the value of a diverse workforce. All qualified individuals will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, gender identity or expression, national origin, sexual orientation, disability and/or protected veteran status in accordance with governing laws.

title: Assistant Director
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:
This position serves as the back-up for the Economic Development Director. This position will coordinate with the Director to manage all aspects of the office to include developing a cutting-edge marketing program, plan and develop economic development product, recruit new business and industry, retain existing industry and manage the day-to-day operations of the office.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
This class specification lists the major duties and requirements of the job and is not all-inclusive. Incumbent(s) may be expected to perform job-related duties other than those contained in this document and may be required to have specific job-related knowledge and skills.
  • Serve as back-up for the Economic Development Director on economic development projects to include: attending prospect meetings, attending and presenting at County Council meetings, and coordinating and/or making presentations to other project- related stakeholders.
  • Supervise staff’s day-to-day operations, including coaching new skills, implementing processes and procedures and conducting reviews.
  • Create and implement policies and procedures that increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the office. Evaluate existing processes and programs and make recommendations to the Director.
  • Represent the office at county, community or other stakeholder meetings.
  • Develop, implement and manage the county’s economic development strategy that is continuously reviewed for effectiveness, accuracy and relevancy.
  • Develop, implement and oversee an existing industry program to include: reviewing program for effectiveness, making ongoing program enhancements and coordinating the collection of data that can be used to enhance marketing efforts.
  • Conduct marketing trips to industries/site selection consultants in targeted markets, and attend industry and other tradeshows as needed.
  • Coordinate with Director and other team members to evaluate and follow-up on leads generated by various marketing channels.
  • Manage all aspects of the office’s product development efforts to include: ensuring that all due diligence needed to have an in-depth understanding of Chester County’s unique products has been performed; master plan, evaluate and make recommendations on existing properties; pursue funding and relevant certifications to increase the marketability of properties; and coordinate with the Director to identify and research new potential industrial sites.
  • Manage economic development projects from inception to completion, as needed.
  • Manage all economic development grants, including the identification, application and administration of grant funding opportunities.
  • Understand developing trends in this market, research opportunities and launch new marketing and other economic development recruiting initiatives as determined by trend and research analyses.
  • Creates and fosters an environment of inclusion and cooperation between economic development allies, Chester County leadership, local stakeholders and office staff. Serves on relevant boards and/or committees to encourage economic development and growth in Chester County.

  • Maintains accurate records and files.
  • Manage the office’s finances to include: monitoring expenditures to ensure the office has the financial wherewithal to undertake and complete projects, provide information to the Director for annual/biennial budgeting, serve as the department’s liaison on finance and budgeting related items.
  • Manage CCED’s fall and spring internship program, providing oversight and mentorship.

QUALIFICATIONS:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:
Bachelor's degree in business administration, or a closely related field, AND ten (10) years of professional experience in economic development, business development, business management, regional economic analysis, marketing, land development, redevelopment, or financial analysis; OR an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:
Knowledge of:
  • Principles, practices, and techniques of marketing, public information and education.
  • Research and statistical analysis techniques.
  • Pertinent federal, state and local laws, regulations and codes.
  • Real estate and business law principles.
  • Principles of economic and industrial development.
  • Record keeping principles and practices.
  • Correct business English, including spelling, grammar and punctuation.
  • Principles and techniques of preparing effective written informational materials.
  • Techniques of making effective oral presentations to large and small groups.
  • Techniques for dealing with a variety of individuals from various socio-economic, ethnic and cultural backgrounds.

Skill in:
  • Planning and administering economic development services and programs.
  • Interpreting and applying methods, practices, procedures, and regulations, related to economic development benefits.
  • Developing strategies and implementing tactics for optimal economic vitality, branding, marketing, special events and business relationships.
  • Interpreting, applying and explaining complex federal, state and local laws related to the areas of responsibility.
  • Preparing clear and concise reports, correspondence and other written materials.
  • Using initiative and independent judgment within general policy guidelines.
  • Using tact, discretion and prudence in dealing with those contacted in the course of the work.

REQUIRED CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, AND REGISTRATIONS:
Continued employment is contingent upon all required licenses and certificates being maintained in active status without suspension or revocation.
  • Driver’s license
  • CEcD (Certified Economic Developer) and/or SCCED (South Carolina Certified Economic Developer) preferred

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORKING ENVIRONMENT:
The physical demands described herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Mobility to work in a typical office setting and use standard office equipment; stamina to sit for extended periods of time; strength and agility to lift and carry up to 20 pounds; vision to read printed materials and a computer screen, and hearing and speech to communicate over the telephone, radio and in person.

title: Project Go, Program Manager
description:
Position: Project Go, Program Manager
Unit: Youth Justice Division
Supervisor: Project Go, Program Director
Company Description
The Philadelphia District Attorney’s Office is committed to delivering justice and providing vital support to victims of crime. Our Victim Services Unit plays a critical role in guiding victims through the legal process and ensuring they receive the necessary support and resources. We are dedicated to enhancing the quality of victim services and fostering a supportive environment for both victims and staff.
**Please note that effective September 1, 2021, the City of Philadelphia requires all new employees to present proof of vaccination against COVID-19. **
To attain a job with the city, you must be a city of Philadelphia resident within 6 months (180 days) of hire and able to work completely in the office.
Summary of Job
As the Program Manager, you will lead and oversee partnerships with schools, students, and caregivers to identify barriers to consistent school attendance and drive the development and implementation of strategic action plans to address them. In this role, you will evaluate school-based attendance improvement plans, determine eligibility for further intervention through Project Go, and manage escalation to the Regional Truancy Court when appropriate.
You will be responsible for onboarding and managing school partners each academic year, designing and delivering ongoing professional development and training opportunities, and ensuring program fidelity and effectiveness. Using a healing-centered, trauma-informed, and evidence-based approach, you will support whole-child outcomes while guiding cross-functional collaboration among internal teams and external stakeholders.
Additionally, you will leverage program data and stakeholder insights to assess the broader social, institutional, and environmental inequities impacting attendance, inform continuous program improvement, and contribute to systems-level change and the redevelopment of Project Go.
The ideal candidate is a mission-driven, strategic, and resourceful leader with a strong commitment to improving outcomes for youth in Philadelphia. The Program Manager excels in stakeholder management, conflict resolution, and collaborative leadership, empowering school staff, partners, students, families, and team members through inclusive and affirming practices.
Duties & Responsibilities
Stakeholder Engagement and Capacity-Building
  1. Lead trauma-informed, healing-centered engagement (presentations and informational sessions) with school personnel, students, and families on truancy prevention and youth-centered topics to identify systemic and individual barriers to consistent school attendance.
  2. Annually develop and facilitate orientation sessions for school personnel on PA truancy law, program policies, and best practices. Manage onboarding of school personnel, including review and verification of MOUs and Regional Truancy Court documentation.
  3. Instruct orientation sessions with school personnel and represent Project Go at school open houses, truancy prevention meetings, and attendance summits to strengthen partnerships, establish intervention strategies, and promote program visibility.
  4. Implement targeted family outreach initiatives to reduce chronic absenteeism and improve attendance compliance.
  5. Act as a primary point of contact for students and families through meetings, phone communication, and written correspondence, ensuring clear, timely, and supportive engagement.
  6. Interface with the Regional Truancy Court hearings as a Project Go representative, and coordinate court-related case management activities.
  7. Participate in monthly court huddles with DHS TIPS staff and hearing officers to coordinate case management and advocate for partner schools.
Program Oversight and Outcomes
  1. Review and evaluate School Attendance Improvement Plans, providing feedback to ensure quality, alignment, and program compliance before referral acceptance.
  2. Oversee and monitor individualized and school-level action plans in collaboration with school personnel to address attendance barriers and improve outcomes.
  3. Manage referrals to partner schools, ensuring alignment with action plans and continuity of care.
  4. Monitor, reduce, and sustain low Family Court referral rates by implementing proactive, data-informed truancy intervention strategies through early intervention, family engagement, and school collaboration.
  5. Track and analyze student progress data in close coordination with partner schools to support sustained attendance improvement. Oversee accurate data entry and quality-control processes that inform the timely preparation of warning letters to families regularly, family conference documentation, and court referrals.
  6. Generate and distribute Family Conference Reports and Court Satisfaction surveys to partner schools that assess outcomes, ensure timely follow-up, and improve referral and court processes.
Program Operations and Administration
  1. Partner with the Project Director and Project Go team to evaluate program effectiveness, analyze trends, and develop strategic improvement initiatives.
  2. Ensure accurate and compliant documentation by maintaining comprehensive physical and electronic case files.
  3. Develop, revise, and manage program materials, including training curricula, presentations, handouts, and resource guides.
  4. Manage program calendars, meetings, and operational timelines to support efficient program execution.
Skills & Qualifications
  • 2- 3 years of relevant experience working with youth and families in education, social work, case management, behavioral health, or other relevant field in an urban environment; non-profit/government experience is a plus. All qualified candidates must have earned a bachelor’s degree from an accredited university.
  • Must have demonstrated experience interacting with diverse groups of people and mediating conflicts.
  • Must be knowledgeable of services for youth and families in Philadelphia.
  • Possesses a high level of technical proficiency (Microsoft suite and etc.) with the desire to improve or continuously develop their skills.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills, including group facilitation skills; Comfortable speaking in small and large group settings.
  • Possesses a high level of problem-solving skills.
  • Uses appropriate discretion in handling confidential information.
  • Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team.
  • Possess a valid driver’s license and reliable access to transportation.
  • Previous knowledge of PA truancy law, IDEA, FERPA, and the McKinney-Vento Act is a plus.
  • Candidates must be organized, flexible, and capable of working under pressure.
  • Ability to develop and cultivate effective internal/external working relationships is essential.
  • Understanding of the uniquely sensitive and confidential nature of the professional services provided by the Office.
Applications will be active for one year from the date of receipt by the Office.
All exempt employees of the District Attorney’s Office are at-will employees and serve at the pleasure of the District Attorney. The at-will relationship shall not be modified for any employee and no agreement, oral or written, shall be entered into that changes the at-will relationship.

Become our next Aquatics Director - Building Safe Swimmers and Strong Teams! We are hiring a Director for both our Hammond and Gary branches.

Position Summary

At the YMCA, we believe strong communities are built through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. As the Program Director, you will lead the daily operations, growth, and quality of assigned programs, with a primary focus on aquatics and member engagement. This role is ideal for a leader who enjoys developing people, creating exceptional participant experiences, managing operations, and ensuring safety and compliance. You will oversee program development, staff recruitment and supervision, budgeting, risk management, and community partnerships while fostering a welcoming and inclusive environment for all.

What Success Looks Like

Successful Program Directors:

  • Build strong, engaged teams through hiring, training, coaching, and accountability.
  • Create high-quality programs that meet community needs and achieve participation goals.
  • Maintain a safe environment through risk management, emergency preparedness, and regulatory compliance.
  • Develop meaningful relationships with members, participants, community partners, and volunteers.
  • Manage budgets responsibly while supporting program growth and sustainability.
  • Lead with the YMCA's mission, values, and cause-driven culture.

What You'll Be Doing

Leadership & Staff Development

  • Recruit, hire, onboard, train, and supervise program staff.
  • Provide ongoing coaching, performance feedback, and professional development.
  • Establish department goals and measure team performance against key objectives.
  • Foster a positive, inclusive, and accountable team culture.

Program Management

  • Develop, coordinate, market, and evaluate program offerings and services.
  • Monitor participant satisfaction and implement improvements based on feedback.
  • Support member engagement and retention initiatives.
  • Ensure programs meet YMCA quality standards and community needs.

Safety & Risk Management

  • Implement and maintain risk management practices.
  • Conduct emergency drills, staff trainings, and preparedness assessments.
  • Ensure staff certifications remain current.
  • Maintain compliance with licensing, OSHA, and aquatics safety requirements.
  • Monitor and maintain equipment through preventive maintenance schedules.

Financial Management

  • Develop and manage annual department budgets.
  • Monitor revenue and expenses, prepare variance reports, and provide accurate forecasts.
  • Ensure programs operate within approved budgets while maintaining quality standards.

Community Engagement

  • Build relationships with schools, agencies, community organizations, and program partners.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to member and community inquiries.
  • Support YMCA fundraising initiatives, including the Annual Campaign.

Administrative Responsibilities

  • Complete payroll, recordkeeping, reporting, scheduling, and other administrative duties.
  • Attend and participate in required meetings, trainings, and association initiatives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Aquatics-Specific Responsibilities

  • Lead and model a high-quality swim lesson program.
  • Maintain Lifeguard and Swim Instructor certifications (Instructor/Trainer certification preferred).
  • Obtain and maintain Certified Pool Operator (CPO) certification within 90 days of hire.
  • Conduct monthly lifeguard in-service trainings.
  • Maintain compliance documentation, including:
    • Pool chemistry records
    • Patron load records
    • Staff certification tracking
    • Emergency drill documentation
    • OSHA compliance records

What You Should Know Before Applying

This is a highly visible leadership role that combines people management, customer service, program operations, and safety oversight.

You May Enjoy This Role If You:

  • Enjoy mentoring and developing staff.
  • Thrive in a fast-paced environment with varied responsibilities.
  • Are comfortable making decisions and solving problems independently.
  • Have strong organizational and communication skills.
  • Value community impact and mission-driven work.
  • Enjoy balancing administrative responsibilities with direct program involvement.

Challenges of the Role

  • Managing multiple priorities, schedules, and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Responding to unexpected staffing, facility, or participant issues.
  • Working occasional evenings, weekends, and special events based on program needs.
  • Maintaining high safety standards while delivering exceptional member experiences.
  • Balancing budget expectations with program growth and service quality.

Qualifications

  • Associate degree in a related field or equivalent experience.
  • Three years of related supervisory or program leadership experience.
  • Ability to respond effectively during emergencies.
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ability to learn new software systems.
  • Ability to effectively engage with individuals from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
  • Lifeguard and Swim Instructor certifications.
  • Maintains current technical and industry knowledge.

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to stand, walk, sit, bend, and move throughout the workday.
  • Visual, auditory, and verbal ability to communicate effectively.
  • Ability to maintain focus, alertness, and sound judgment in a busy environment.
  • Ability to work in both office and aquatic settings.
  • Must maintain a professional appearance and demeanor.

Our Benefits Include

  • Health care medical coverage
  • Dental and vision insurance
  • Employer-paid Long-Term Disability (LTD) and Life Insurance
  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • 12% employer retirement contribution
  • Complimentary YMCA family membership
  • 50% discount on most YMCA programs
  • Ongoing professional development and leadership development opportunities

We encourage our staff to take full advantage of YMCA programs and facilities to support their own health, well-being, and work-life balance.

Our Mission

To put Christian principles into practice through programs that build healthy spirit, mind, and body for all.

title: Power BI Business Intelligence Analyst and Developer
description:
We are seeking a detail-oriented and growth-minded Power BI Business Intelligence Analyst and Developer (Junior-to-Mid level) to join our team. In this role, you will focus on turning well-structured datasets and business requirements into clear, impactful, and high-performance visual dashboards and reports. You will work closely with pre-modeled data sources, utilizing advanced DAX and Power Query to build complex calculations and dynamic data transformations. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to leverage modern AI coding assistants (such as Claude, GitHub Copilot, and Codex) to accelerate your development workflows for DAX optimization and Power Query scripting.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Report & Dashboard Development: Design, build, and deploy intuitive, interactive Power BI reports and dashboards that effectively communicate key business metrics.
  • Advanced Calculation & Transformation: Write efficient DAX expressions for complex measures, calculations, and data aggregations, and use Power Query to refine and shape data inputs.
  • AI-Assisted Development: Integrate AI tools (Claude, GitHub Copilot, Codex) into your daily workflow to accelerate report building, troubleshoot DAX queries, and streamline Power Query transformations.
  • Data Collaboration: Collaborate closely with data engineering/modeling peers who provide core datasets, ensuring your semantic layers and visual outputs meet user requirements.
  • Optimization & Maintenance: Monitor report performance, optimize DAX and visual rendering times, and maintain existing reporting assets as business needs evolve.
  • User Enablement: Gather requirements from business stakeholders and translate them into actionable, visually compelling solutions.

Requirements:

  • Proven experience developing production-ready dashboards and reports in Power BI, with a strong command of Power Query.
  • Solid experience writing DAX measures, calculated columns, and managing row-level security (RLS) or complex evaluation contexts.
  • Strong foundational knowledge of SQL for data extraction and validation, alongside scripting familiarity (Python or PowerShell) for data pipeline tasks or automation.
  • Strong capability to translate raw business metrics and requirements into clean, user-friendly visual narratives.
  • Openness and enthusiasm for leveraging AI development assistants (such as Copilot, Claude, or Codex) to boost productivity and code quality.

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
  • 1–3 years of hands-on experience focused specifically on Power BI report development and business intelligence analysis.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
About the role:

At the heart of our offering is a versatile software platform for orchestrating complex robotic systems, from industrial robot arms and mobile manipulators to humanoids. Our Forward Deployed engineers bring it into real production environments with international customers and delivery partners.

As Senior Project Manager, you help steer that work. You keep projects on track from POC to production, give team leads a clear picture to decide which projects to take on, and ensure that what we build for one customer flows back into the platform. You work at the staff level alongside product management and technical leadership, and take on whatever else the department needs as it grows. Expect a fast-moving environment where the processes are still being shaped, and you help shape them.

Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate the Forward Deployed project landscape, and prepare prioritization decisions with the team leads by strategic value, technical risk, and commercial return
  • Plan scope, milestones, and engineer allocation together with the team leads, and make the trade-offs visible when capacity is tight
  • Drive engagements from POC through pilot to production, including on-site commissioning and acceptance
  • Act as a key point of contact for customers and delivery partners, with a clear interface between their scope and ours
  • Support Sales and Pre-Sales with feasibility assessments and effort estimates
  • Coordinate across product teams and AI research without direct line authority
  • Make sure features built for customer projects are fed back into the platform as standard capabilities
  • Set up lightweight ways of working for planning and reporting that fit how the teams actually work

Essential Skills:

  • Degree in Computer Science, Mechatronics, Electrical, Mechanical or Industrial Engineering, or a comparable field
  • 5+ years of project management, including meaningful time in a startup, scale-up or other fast-growing tech environment
  • Experience with customer-facing projects in robotics, AI or software-heavy automation, and with taking new technology from pilot to production
  • Comfortable with immature products and changing requirements: you make progress without waiting for perfect specs
  • Solid technical understanding of robotic systems and how mechanics, controls, software and AI work together
  • Pragmatic, agile-first project management, with tools such as Jira and Confluence
  • Ability to lead through influence and make trade-offs under ambiguity
  • Fluent English; willingness to travel around 30% of the time, including on-site customer phases

Beneficial Skills:

  • Fluent German; Mandarin is a plus
  • Experience in a product company where customer projects drive platform development
  • Experience with humanoid or mobile robot deployments
  • Familiarity with machinery and functional safety (ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066, ISO 3691-4)

What we offer

  • A dynamic high-tech company, combined with financial soundness and world-class investors.
  • Join an interdisciplinary, international team with 60+ different nationalities in a collaborative work environment.
  • Lots of development opportunities as we continue to grow.
  • Challenging tasks and impactful projects alongside experts that enable professional and personal growth.
  • Corporate Benefits Program covering health, mobility, and learning for 100€ net per month.
  • Modern office facilities with a rooftop terrace overlooking Munich, free drinks & fruits, and regular company events contribute to a good working environment

About us

Agile Robots SE is an international high-tech company based in Munich, Germany with a production site in Kaufbeuren and more than 3500 employees worldwide. Our mission is to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and robotics by developing systems that combine state-of-the-art force-moment-sensing and world-leading image-processing technology. This unique combination of technologies allows us to provide user-friendly and affordable robotic solutions that enable intelligent precision assembly.

This is made possible by our employees, who bring out the best in each and every day with creativity and enthusiasm. Become part of this team and shape the future of robotics with us!

We are proud of our diversity and welcome your application regardless of gender and sexual identity, nationality, ethnicity, religion, age, or disability.

title: SAP DRC / E-Invoicing Delivery Lead / Scrum Master
description:
For a large-scale international SAP S/4HANA transformation program, we are looking for an experienced SAP DRC / E-Invoicing Delivery Lead / Scrum Master to support the coordination of the e-invoicing workstream.

The role sits at the intersection of Business, Tax, Finance, Procurement and IT and requires someone who can bring together different functional and technical teams around the SAP DRC and e-invoicing activities.

description:

Job Summary
JCS Solutions' C5ISR Center CSSP Cloud Operations Team is seeking an Elastic Data Engineer to support enterprise cybersecurity operations within a Department of Defense environment. In this role, you will design, maintain, and optimize data-ingestion, analytics, and monitoring capabilities using the Elastic Stack to help drive threat detection, incident response, compliance reporting, and operational visibility.
You will work with cybersecurity and operational telemetry from multiple sources, ensuring data quality, platform performance, and actionable insights for security analysts and stakeholders.

Salary Range: $135,000 to $162,000

What’s in it for you:
  • Join a premier technology firm specializing in innovative solutions.
  • Be part of a collaborative, inclusive, and innovative work culture.
  • Enjoy tremendous growth potential in a high-performing team environment.
  • A robust benefits package:
    • Health, dental, and vision insurance
    • Life insurance
    • Short-and-long term disability
    • Paid time off (PTO)
    • 401k retirement plan with employer match
    • Annual Professional Development Reimbursement Program
    • And more!

What you will do:
  • Design and maintain data pipelines for cybersecurity, cloud, network, endpoint, application, identity, and infrastructure telemetry.
  • Collect, ingest, transform, normalize, enrich, and route structured and unstructured data from enterprise sources.
  • Develop and maintain data schemas, mappings, standards, and models, including Elastic Common Schema (ECS) alignment.
  • Parse and process complex log formats, including JSON, XML, CSV, syslog, Windows Event Logs, and custom application data.
  • Implement data quality controls, validation, cleansing, reconciliation, deduplication, and enrichment processes.
  • Build reusable parsing, transformation, and enrichment workflows and integrate data from APIs, databases, cloud services, message queues, files, and security platforms.
  • Support high-volume, near-real-time data ingestion and event processing while troubleshooting ingestion, mapping, parsing, and data-quality issues.
  • Analyze data flows to identify gaps, bottlenecks, inconsistencies, and source-system issues.
  • Collaborate with cybersecurity analysts, detection engineers, and infrastructure teams to onboard data sources and support threat hunting, alerting, incident response, and reporting.
  • Document data sources, schemas, lineage, dependencies, governance, retention, classification, and onboarding procedures.
  • Use Python, SQL, PowerShell, Bash, Git, and testing practices to support data engineering, automation, validation, and troubleshooting.
  • Maintain expertise in cybersecurity telemetry, ETL/ELT processes, APIs, and large-scale event-data management.

What you will bring:
  • Strong experience with the Elastic Stack, including Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana, Elastic Agent, Fleet, and Beats.
  • Experience designing and supporting high-volume logging, cybersecurity telemetry, and data-ingestion pipelines.
  • Knowledge of Elasticsearch architecture, including clusters, indices, shards, mappings, templates, data streams, and lifecycle management (ILM).
  • Experience processing JSON, XML, CSV, syslog, Windows Event Logs, and other log sources using Logstash filters and ingest pipelines.
  • Experience implementing data retention, rollover, and tiered-storage strategies.
  • Linux administration and scripting experience using Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar languages.
  • Knowledge of REST APIs, Git, networking, TLS/certificates, and access-control mechanisms.
  • Understanding of security monitoring, threat detection, incident response, vulnerability management, with strong troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills.
  • BS degree with 4-8 years of relevant experience, or MS degree with 2-6 years of relevant experience.
  • Active DoD TS/SCI clearance or ability to obtain one.

How will you wow us:
  • Experience supporting SOC, CSSP, SIEM, or enterprise observability platform.
  • Experience with Elastic Security, AWS, AWS GovCloud, Kafka, Docker, or Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with Zero Trust, RMF, DISA STIGs, and federal logging requirements.
  • Elastic, AWS, Security+, GIAC, or CISSP certification.

title: Associate Product Manager
description:
About the role:

We're looking for an Associate Product Manager to be Rezdy's dependable NA presence — covering the hours our Sydney/Melbourne-based PM and dev team aren't online. This is a strong fit for someone energized by operational rigor and real-time problem-solving: comfortable triaging under pressure, translating between technical and commercial audiences, and building product judgment by working closely alongside a senior PM rather than owning a roadmap from day one. Pacific timezone

What you'll do:

  • Connect the time zones. Be the dependable daily link between North America stakeholders — support and account management teams — and the Sydney/Melbourne-based PM and dev team, flagging decisions and blockers in real time rather than letting them wait for the next overlap window.
  • Be the NA distribution conduit for Commercial leads and distribution partners (Viator, GYG, etc) and Distribution Resellers
  • Keep incidents moving and visible during NA hours. Triage escalations that occur in NA working hours against a defined severity framework, looping in the senior PM and dev lead when judgment calls exceed current scope, and making sure NA support and AM teams get clear, live updates rather than waiting for the next AU working day.
  • Surface and track AM churn risk. Own intake of NA account-manager-flagged churn risk — capturing impact and urgency the moment it's raised — so it's framed and ready to compete fairly when the senior PM and dev lead plan the sprint.
  • Answer for what's in flight. Be NA's go-to for "is this expected / is this known / what's the status" questions on Booking Manager and Distribution, working from close sync with the senior PM's roadmap and known-issues context rather than independent authority over it.
  • Share release communication in NA hours. Help execute the existing release process — communication and post-release follow-up specifically during NA hours — rather than owning release planning or prioritization.
  • Partner with Engineering at a working level. Build enough fluency in our data architecture to relay NA-side context accurately to engineering, without owning technical trade-off decisions.
  • Put AI tools to work. Use AI tools to speed up research, troubleshooting, and day-to-day tasks — a lever for moving faster, not a replacement for judgment.

What you'll bring:

  • 2+ years of experience in product management, product operations, or a closely related operational/customer-facing role, ideally in B2B SaaS.
  • Comfort working within another PM's priorities and roadmap — bringing your own judgment and context to how that work gets executed
  • Experience with incident or issue management processes, and communicating through them clearly under time pressure.
  • Comfort working with legacy technology systems and the teams that maintain them — able to translate between legacy constraints and current product priorities for both engineering and commercial audiences.
  • Strong written communication skills — able to adjust tone and depth for audiences ranging from support and account management teams to engineering.
  • Ease operating in process-driven environments (Jira, Slack, or equivalent).
  • Comfort picking up domain concepts across different product types — e.g., transactional booking flows versus distribution/channel connectivity — without needing deep expertise in both on day one.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in the travel, tours, or activities booking software space.
  • Familiarity with multi-brand or multi-product portfolios (Expedition Software operates Checkfront, Rezdy, and Regiondo).
  • Prior experience in a support, account management, or customer-facing product role.
The salary range for this position is $85,000-$100,000, commensurate with years of experience, skillset, and qualifications.

title: Change Management Lead
description:
Position:

Change Management Lead

Reports to:

Principle Advisor, Enterprise Digital Strategy

Position Term:

Full Time Permanent

Primary Location:

Mississauga, Ontario, Canada

Workplace Type:

Hybrid

Job Purpose
The Change Management Lead is responsible for the change management side of organizational digital transformation at World Vision Canada. The role plays a key part in helping the organization successfully implement digital transformation, ensuring that employees adopt and sustain new systems and ways of working so that the organization realizes the full value of its investment.

The role sits at the intersection of business transformation and employee experience. The incumbent partners with executives, business leaders, technology teams and end users to develop and execute change strategies that accelerate adoption, support value realization and deliver lasting outcomes.

Reporting to Principal Advisor, Enterprise Digital Strategy and working closely with People, Culture & Connection, the incumbent is the primary point of accountability for adoption across the organization. This position has no direct reports; results are achieved through enablement, measurement and influence rather than line authority.

Responsibilities

Develops and executes the change management strategy and plans. Creates comprehensive change management strategies and plans for large-scale business and technology initiatives, applying a structured methodology such as ADKAR and maintaining the supporting deliverables: change strategy, sponsor roadmap, communication plan, training plan, coaching plan and resistance management plan.
Conducts change impact, readiness and risk assessments. Carries out stakeholder assessments, change impact analyses, readiness assessments and change risk evaluations, identifying the groups affected and the extent of change for each. Directs support, training and communication effort to where it is most needed.
Defines and implements change interventions. Designs targeted interventions that address organizational barriers and accelerate adoption and establishes the governance structures and change networks required to sustain change over time.
Builds and leads the change champion network. Selects, trains and supports champions embedded in business and delivery teams who act as early adopters, local training facilitators, the feedback route to this role, and reporters of adoption at team level. Maintains recognition and development pathways that sustain participation.
Engages and influences senior stakeholders. Builds trust relationships with executive sponsors and senior business leaders and advises them on carrying out the sponsorship role. Develops executive communication strategies and stakeholder engagement plans, facilitates leadership workshops, steering committees and decision-making sessions, and aligns stakeholder groups around objectives and expected outcomes.
Equips managers and leaders to lead change. Prepares department leaders and middle managers to lead their own teams through transition, and to understand and apply new decision rights and governance arrangements in their areas.
Designs and delivers learning and adoption programs. Creates and oversees the training, communication and adoption activity accompanying each release of capability. Collaborates with Learning and Development to build scalable learning pathways ranging from foundation-level capability for all staff to expert level for change champions, covering data and AI literacy, as well as new digital ways of working. Sustains a fixed communication cadence of leader briefings, all-leader forums, written communication, readiness surveys and recognition, and refines programs continuously based on employee feedback and adoption insight.
Measures, publishes and reports adoption. Scores and measures adoption effectiveness through defined performance indicators, organizational behavioral agility, usage analytics and business outcomes, and publishes an adoption dashboard covering extent of use, engagement and sentiment, depth of feature use, and business value delivered. Incorporates adoption trajectory into digital transformation program and executive leadership reporting on cadence. Prepares the readiness evidence on which phase decisions depend, providing recommendations where readiness is not evidenced.
Manages resistance, adoption risk and change capability. Identifies resistance through periodic surveys that map teams by level of resistance and enthusiasm, apply targeted intervention where resistance is high, and monitors organizational capacity to absorb change and identify adoption plateaus. Builds internal change management capability, mentoring colleagues and embedding change practice so that it endures beyond the current program of work.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Organizational Development, Human Resources, Business Administration, Communications or equivalent professional experience.
Change management certification, Prosci, CCMP or ACMP. Preferred.
7+ years of experience leading organizational change management initiatives.
Experience supporting enterprise digital transformations, technology implementations or business transformation programs.
Experience designing stakeholder engagement, communication, training and adoption strategies.
Experience establishing and leading a champion or change agent network.
Experience defining adoption measures and reporting them to executive and board audiences.
Experience delivering within a scaled agile environment, including planning across multiple teams and increments.
Strong understanding of change management frameworks and methodologies.
Change impact assessment, stakeholder analysis and readiness assessment.
Design and analysis of readiness and sentiment surveys, including interpretation of resistance data.
Definition of adoption measures and the construction and maintenance of reporting dashboards.
Workshop facilitation and presentation skills.

Preferred:

Experience working with data and analytics transformation initiatives.
Experience leading geographically dispersed or cross-functional teams.
Experience working with delivery vendors in a distributed environment.
Experience in a nonprofit or mission-driven organization.

Ability to read, write and speak business French.

Why Consider Us?

Our competitive compensation & benefits include:

Health Spending Account
Up to 6% matched pension contributions
Parental leave top-up
Generous paid vacation, sick days, wellness and personal days
Office closed extra days before long weekends (6x/year)

World Vision Canada has consistently been awarded Canada and GTA top employer awards.
We are Canada’s largest development, relief, and advocacy non-profit organization.

description: Position Summary Reporting to the Vice Provost for Global Engagement (VPGE), the Executive Director, Office of International Services provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for all immigration-related services across the University of Illinois Chicago (UIC), including regional campuses and instructional sites. The Executive Director serves as the University's principal authority on immigration regulations affecting international students, scholars, faculty, researchers, and visiting exchange participants. This position ensures institutional compliance with federal immigration regulations and provides expert guidance to senior university leadership on immigration policy, risk management, and regulatory matters. Essential Responsibilities Immigration Leadership and Compliance Direct all immigration services and compliance functions for international students, scholars, faculty, researchers, and exchange visitors. Interpret, implement, and monitor complex federal immigration regulations, policies, and procedures related to F-1, J-1, and other employment-based immigration categories. Ensure institutional compliance with regulations administered by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Department of State (DOS), U.S. Department of Labor (DOL), and other federal agencies. Collaborates with University Counsel with regard to representing the university in communications concerning immigration regulations, compliance matters, audits, and problem resolution. Maintain productive relationships with governmental agencies and professional organizations to support effective immigration services and regulatory compliance. Establish priorities and performance standards for immigration services operations. Direct the development, implementation, and assessment of programs supporting international student and scholar orientation, transition, retention, and cultural adaptation. Supervise, mentor, and evaluate professional staff responsible for immigration advising, case management, and compliance functions. Ensure staff maintain current knowledge of immigration regulations, procedures, and best practices. Institutional Service Serve on university and system-wide committees addressing immigration, compliance, international education, and risk management issues. Lead special projects and initiatives related to immigration services and international student and scholar support.

title: Director of Quality Control - Construction
description:
Key Responsibilities:

Develop, implement, and continuously improve the company's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring alignment with organizational objectives, industry standards, and regulatory requirements.
Establish and maintain quality policies, procedures, standards, inspection protocols, and reporting systems to ensure consistent quality practices across all projects.
Define quality objectives, key performance indicators, acceptance criteria, and inspection and testing requirements to support project success and continuous improvement.
Provide leadership and oversight of project quality control activities, including inspections, testing, material receiving processes, and verification of compliance with drawings, specifications, codes, and contract requirements.
Monitor and evaluate quality performance across projects, reviewing inspection results, testing reports, deficiencies, and corrective actions to ensure quality standards are achieved.
Lead root cause analysis investigations and implement corrective and preventive measures to reduce deficiencies, rework, and quality-related risks.
Support project teams in identifying, assessing, and mitigating quality risks throughout the project lifecycle.
Evaluate subcontractor and supplier quality performance and recommend improvements to ensure compliance with company standards and project requirements.
Support commissioning, functional performance testing, and project turnover activities to ensure completed work meets quality expectations and contractual obligations.
Conduct project quality assessments and audits to evaluate the effectiveness of quality control processes and identify opportunities for improvement.
Analyze trends in deficiencies, failures, and quality metrics, and provide recommendations to leadership to improve project outcomes and operational performance.
Develop and deliver quality-related training, coaching, and resources to project teams to promote consistency, accountability, and best practices.
Foster a quality-focused culture throughout the organization by promoting continuous improvement, proactive problem-solving, and operational excellence.
Collaborate with internal departments, consultants, subcontractors, and clients to support quality objectives and successful project delivery.
Lead ongoing development of Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), quality checklists, audit processes, and quality documentation standards.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives through lessons learned, root cause analysis, and process optimization.
Establish and maintain standardized quality management workflows within Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), ensuring consistent use of inspections, deficiencies, forms, checklists, Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), issue tracking, document control, and reporting processes across all projects.
Drive company-wide adoption and continuous improvement of ACC quality management tools by developing standards, templates, dashboards, and reporting metrics that enhance visibility, accountability, consistency, and quality performance across the organization.
Collaborate with Operations, Construction, IT, and project teams to optimize ACC quality processes, ensuring accurate quality records, real-time reporting, effective deficiency management, and the capture of lessons learned to support continuous improvement initiatives.
Establish quality planning requirements that align inspections, testing, deficiency management, and verification activities with project sequencing and construction milestones, ensuring quality activities are proactively planned rather than reactively managed.
Assume other related duties and responsibilities consistent with the scope and level of the position.

Skills and Experience:

Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible construction experience, including at least 5 years in a quality management, quality assurance, or quality control leadership role.
Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and managing Quality Management Systems (QMS) within the construction industry.
Proven leadership experience with the ability to build, coach, mentor, and develop high-performing teams while fostering a collaborative and accountable work environment.
Extensive experience managing quality programs on large-scale commercial, institutional, industrial, multi-family residential, or infrastructure projects.
Strong understanding of construction methods, materials, building systems, and industry best practices.
Experience working collaboratively with owners, consultants, regulatory authorities, subcontractors, and project teams.
Thorough knowledge of contract documents, drawings, specifications, shop drawings, and project quality requirements.
Strong understanding of quality management principles, continuous improvement methodologies, root cause analysis, and corrective action processes.
Familiarity with commissioning, functional performance testing, project turnover requirements, and deficiency management processes.
Excellent communication, problem-solving, and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Quality management certifications, such as ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or equivalent, are considered an asset.

title: Authorizations Coordinator
description:
About the Role

The Authorizations Coordinator is responsible for managing the end-to-end prior authorization and referral process for patient services. This role ensures that authorization requests are accurately initiated, tracked, followed up on, and completed in accordance with payer requirements, medical policies, and client expectations.

The ideal candidate has experience in prior authorizations, medical billing, or revenue cycle management, with strong attention to detail, excellent communication skills, and the ability to manage a high-volume workload in a remote environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Receive, review, and process prior authorization and referral requests accurately and in a timely manner.
  • Initiate, track, and follow up on authorization requests from submission through final determination.
  • Review patient cases, medical documentation, CPT codes, ICD-10 diagnosis codes, and payer requirements to determine authorization needs and likely outcomes.
  • Verify patient demographics, insurance eligibility, benefits, referral requirements, and coverage details.
  • Obtain, review, and enter insurance authorizations and referrals prior to patient services.
  • Work within EMRs, payer portals, and authorization platforms such as Availity or similar systems.
  • Communicate with provider offices, physicians’ offices, insurance representatives, and internal teams to gather required documentation and resolve authorization issues.
  • Assist patients, when appropriate, with collecting supporting documents needed for authorization processing.
  • Maintain accurate logs of open cases, pending documents, payer follow-ups, action items, and case outcomes.
  • Monitor authorization status and follow up with insurance companies to prevent delays in patient care or claim processing.
  • Identify and escalate issues related to denials, missing documentation, payer discrepancies, or authorization delays.
  • Respond to emails, phone calls, and internal messages in a timely and professional manner.
  • Support benefit verification tasks for patients and clients as needed.
  • Assist with customer service calls and route inquiries appropriately.
  • Maintain productivity expectations, including daily or weekly case submission and follow-up targets.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • 1–3+ years of experience in prior authorizations, medical billing, revenue cycle management, or a related healthcare administrative role.
  • Strong knowledge of insurance verification, benefits, referrals, payer requirements, and authorization workflows.
  • Experience using EMRs, payer portals, and authorization platforms such as Availity or similar tools.
  • Familiarity with CPT coding, ICD-10 diagnosis codes, and medical documentation review.
  • Understanding of payer policies, authorization requirements, denial scenarios, and follow-up processes.
  • Ability to accurately verify patient demographics, insurance eligibility, benefits, and required documentation.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools, including Excel, Outlook, and Teams.
  • Comfortable working with general workflow tools, web browsers, softphone systems, and healthcare technology platforms.
  • Ability to manage high-volume case loads while meeting submission targets and deadlines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to assess problem areas, identify root causes, and resolve issues effectively.
  • Strong time management and prioritization skills, especially when handling urgent versus routine cases.
  • Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment.

title: Director, Portfolio Controlling
description:
RWE Americas, LLC
To start as soon as possible, full time, permanent

Functional area: Finance / Controlling
Remuneration: Exempt

The Director, Portfolio Controlling will be part of the Controlling team in the rapidly growing renewables business of RWE Americas (RWEA). The Director role is a highly skilled finance leadership role overseeing a portfolio of renewable energy assets. The Director will manage a team responsible for administering financing agreements (tax equity, debt/loan, joint-venture partnership) including complying with all covenants and compliance obligations, providing external financing parties with required reports and deliverables, and consulting with internal stakeholders and external financing parties to achieve strategic and commercial business objectives. The ideal candidate has deep knowledge of financing agreements, tax equity structures and modeling, is familiar with commercial and operational performance metrics for renewable energy assets and is customer-service minded with strong communication and collaboration skills.

Role Responsibilities:

  • Execution: Lead a team responsible for administering and complying with financing agreements (tax equity, debt/loan, joint-venture partnerships) for a significant portion of RWEA’s operating portfolio, including driving completion of reports/deliverables (monthly operating reports, PAYGO calculations, cash distributions, tracking/flip models, annual operating budgets), tracking project and investor returns, and responding to questions and issues raised by external financing parties
  • External Stakeholder Management: Lead engagement with external financing counterparties, serving as the organization's principal liaison and driving collaborative relationships that support strategic objectives and business outcomes
  • Collaboration: Manage cross-functional relationships with Legal, Accounting, Tax, and Asset Management to timely deliver all financing obligations, analyze and solve complex strategic topics, and optimize asset-level financial and operational performance
  • Strategic Steering: Advise Origination and M&A teams on deal structuring and financing agreement language to steer decisions so the Portfolio Controlling team can effectively administer financing agreements post-closing
  • Financial Optimization: Oversee project and investor returns in order to make recommendations to Senior Leadership to optimize financing agreements, including modeling tax equity buyout or restructuring transactions, leading negotiations with external financing parties, and executing transaction agreements
  • Team Development & Management: Lead and manage direct reports as well as others within the Portfolio Controlling team, including review of work product, setting clear expectations, building succession depth, and scaling team capabilities in line with portfolio growth and evolving business needs
  • Process Optimization: Drive continuous improvement across processes, including implementing standardized templates, assumptions, and dynamic modeling approaches
  • Change Management & Integration: Support evolving company priorities, special projects, and integration efforts related to structural changes and accelerated growth targets

Job Requirements and Experience:

  • BA/BS in Finance / Accounting / Economics / Business (required)
  • Advanced degree is a plus, but not required
  • Minimum 12 years of experience in Finance, Accounting, Financial or Management Consulting, or other finance-related fields
  • Experience with tax equity financing, loan financing, origination/structured finance transactions required.
  • Minimum 4 years leading functional teams and or transactions
  • Proven experience leading teams of three or more, with demonstrated strength in people leadership, development, and accountability
  • Experience within the renewable energy sector preferred
  • Expert understanding of tax equity structures and modeling and financing agreements
  • Leads with expert analytical and conceptual thinking; solves complex problems; crafts clear, strategic visualizations, anticipates stakeholder dynamics and their needs in analyses.
  • Fosters a high-performance problem-solving culture within the team through guidance and development.
  • Collaborates across business units, teams and senior leadership; presents to senior leadership and external financing counterparties on complex matters.
  • Outstanding communication skills (written and verbal), comfortable interfacing with senior management and external financing parties.
  • Persuasive communicator who establishes feedback culture and drives consensus building across teams.
  • Demonstrated leadership and people-management experience.
  • Manages cross-functional, corporate wide processes, new initiatives or tools.
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • CPA is preferred, but not required
  • Minimum 4 years of relevant experience
  • Experience in an FP&A role and/or within the renewable energy sector preferred, but not required
  • Basic knowledge of the core accounting concepts and principles; advanced knowledge is a plus
  • Strong communication skills (written and verbal) and comfortable interfacing with senior management
  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Actively drives collaboration across functions; explains findings clearly to internal stakeholders; acts as finance partner with asset managers and technical teams
  • Proven ability to empathize, build relationships, and effectively communicate with people from a diverse set of backgrounds
  • Focuses on building relationships to standardize processes and solve problems
  • Applies strong conceptual and analytical thinking; independently runs forecasts and builds models; explains financial trends effectively to business partners; interprets financial data in light of business dynamics
  • Proficient understanding of forecasting, variance analysis, asset performance metrics and systems/reporting tools (e.g., Power BI)
  • Strong technical background, with advanced proficiency in Excel, SAP, SAC, PowerBI, and/or Tableau a plus
  • Detail-oriented, has strong business acumen and analytical mindset, and a sound understanding of business concepts
  • Motivated self-starter, goal-oriented, and strong problem-solving abilities
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to coordinate multiple tasks and deliverables
  • Identifies issues and modifies processes and methods as needed
  • Demonstrated desire to learn about the Company and the renewables space
  • Responds well to direction, is easy to challenge and develop, and is coachable
  • Leads assigned tasks with management direction/guidance
  • Guides interns/graduates/new joiners

Work Environment:

This position is a hybrid role with an expected 3 days in the Chicago office each week with some travel <10% to other RWEA offices. The employee must be able to sit, walk, or stand for long durations of time.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. RWE Americas is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time.

Pay range: The annual base salary range for this position in Illinois is $178,000 - $240,000. The listed salary range represents our good faith estimate for this position and represents the range for new hire salaries across all U.S locations. Please note that the salary information is a general guideline only. RWE considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s education & work experience, training & certifications, and key skills as well as market and business considerations at the time of the offer.

Benefits offered: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability, 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, EAP, Education Assistance, Parental Leave, Paid time off, and Holidays. Eligible employees also participate in short-term incentives, in addition to salary.

title: Mechatronic Apprentice I
description:
Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!

As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement.

You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
• You will perform preventative/predictive maintenance of conveyance equipment using the appropriate job plans, procedures, and manuals.

• You will conduct maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells.

• You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components.

• You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc.
• You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head
