title: Planner I,II,III
description:
Position Profile

The Planner series consists of three levels (I, II, III), each with progressively increasing responsibility in land use planning, zoning, and community development. Planners perform professional and technical duties to support the development and implementation of zoning ordinances, land-use policies, and urban planning initiatives.

Serving as key administrators of the County's zoning, subdivision, solid waste, and nuisance ordinances, Planners play a critical role in enforcing regulations and advancing the County General Plan. They provide staff support to the County Commission, Planning Commission, Public Lands Committee, and Trails Committee, ensuring that land development aligns with county policies and long-term strategic goals.

Planners conduct research, review applications, enforce ordinances, and provide recommendations on zoning and land use matters. They actively engage with residents, developers, government agencies, and community stakeholders to promote resilient planning practices and responsible development that supports the County's growth and vision.

Compensation

  • Planner I: $22.00 - $26.00 per hour
  • Planner II: $27.00 - $32.00 per hour
  • Planner III: $32.00 - $36.00 per hour

BENEFITS

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance: We pay 80% to 95% of your premiums.
  • Retirement Contributions: The County contributes to your Utah Retirement Systems (URS) account.
  • Paid Time Off (PTO): Start earning PTO immediately upon hire.
  • Annual Paid Holidays: Enjoy 108 hours of paid holidays each year.

Essential Functions

  • Assists with the management of daily department operations, including land use studies, ordinance development, business regulations, and permit review. Monitors or leads projects to ensure compliance with the County General Plan.
  • Provides interpretations of county zoning, planning, nuisance, solid waste, and related ordinances to ensure regulatory compliance.
  • Serves as an administrative advisor and liaison to the Board of County Commissioners, Public Land Committee, Trails Committee, and Planning Commission. Offers technical insights, policy recommendations, and implementation strategies for county development initiatives.
  • Conducts public meetings and hearings to solicit feedback and educate the public on planning policies and projects.
  • Identifies funding sources, applies for grants, and ensures compliance with grant conditions for projects, including trails development and land use initiatives.
  • Develops, organizes, and facilitates comprehensive planning processes for current and future county development needs. Assists in maintaining the County General Plan and converting policies into action plans.
  • Coordinates planning research and program development with other county departments and governmental agencies. Conducts feasibility studies, updates zoning ordinances, and ensures compliance with land-use regulations.
  • Engages with the public, developers, contractors, and entrepreneurs to discuss planning, zoning, and development concerns. Provides guidance on county regulations and requirements.
  • Oversees subdivision development, zoning proposals, land acquisitions, and building permits to ensure compliance with county codes and ordinances.
  • Represents County interests in discussions with federal, state, and local agencies that own or control land within the County. Prepares reports and recommendations for County Commissioners regarding public land issues.
  • Performs other related duties as required.

Planner I (Entry-Level Professional Planner)

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Provides public assistance on planning matters such as zoning, site plan reviews, and conditional use permits.
  • Conducts field studies and surveys to collect data for planning projects.
  • Gathers and analyzes statistical data related to zoning and land use.
  • Acts as a technical assistant to various boards and commissions.
  • Designs and drafts maps, charts, graphs, and other illustrative materials for planning projects.
  • Conducts site visits and zoning variance investigations.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Urban Planning, Public Administration, Geography, Environmental Studies, Landscape Architecture, or a related field.
  • 1-2 years of experience in urban or regional planning, zoning administration, or related work.
  • An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Planner II (Intermediate-Level Professional Planner)

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Implements department work plans and programs and monitors compliance with planning, zoning, and development ordinances.
  • Conducts research on policy and zoning regulations, presents findings to the Planning Commission, and prepares reports.
  • Prepares draft proposals for zoning ordinance amendments and planning policies.
  • Conducts feasibility studies and prepares progress reports on land use projects.
  • Reviews and updates ordinances affecting zoning, development, and planning.
  • Coordinates planning projects with other county departments and government agencies.
  • Engages with the public to address land use concerns and follow up on policy decisions.
  • Participates in project review meetings with developers to negotiate zoning compliance.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Urban Planning, Public Administration, or a related field.
  • 3-5 years of progressively responsible experience in planning, zoning, or a related field.
  • An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
  • AICP Certification, if degree held is from an accredited planning program.

Planner III (Senior-Level Professional Planner/Project Lead)

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Serves as a team leader or project manager, supervising lower-level planners.
  • Assists in performance evaluations for junior staff.
  • Conducts in-depth research on planning, zoning, and community development issues.
  • Prepares and presents written reports and zoning recommendations to commissions and elected officials.
  • Develops proposals for zoning and planning policies.
  • Conducts feasibility studies and monitors project progress.
  • Ensures public engagement in land-use planning through hearings and meetings.
  • Collaborates with government agencies and developers on regulatory compliance.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Urban Planning, Public Administration, or a related field.
  • 5-7 years of progressively responsible experience in planning, zoning, or related fields.
  • Experience in leading projects and mentoring junior staff preferred.
  • An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
  • AICP Certification.

Skills & Abilities

  • Extensive knowledge of:
    • Urban and rural planning principles, zoning regulations, and land use policies.
    • Economic, political, and sociological factors affecting planning decisions.
    • Research methods, statistical analysis, and ordinance compliance.
  • Strong ability to:
    • Analyze planning and development issues, propose solutions, and implement regulations.
    • Utilize ArcGIS Pro, MS Word, Excel, Gmail, OnBase, and other planning tools.
    • Communicate effectively with public officials, stakeholders, and the general public.
    • Foster collaboration between county departments and outside agencies.

title: Antenna & RF Engineer, Amazon Leo Antenna Development
description:
Amazon LEO is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon LEO will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.

As an Antenna & RF Engineer supporting the development, test, and design of antenna and RF Front-End, you will design, integrate, and characterize antennas and arrays across multiple domains (phased arrays, reflectors, aperture antennas, and other relevant topologies). You will own “ADC-to-antenna” RF performance, collaborating with RF, systems, and calibration teams to deliver high-performance RF systems and links for both space and ground segments.

You’ll split your time between EM design tools, RF system analysis, and lab validation, working on high volume antenna design from concept to deployment.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


Key job responsibilities
- Design and optimize antenna and array architectures (element selection, lattice, feeding networks, beam-forming strategies) to meet RF system goals.
- Own end-to-end RF performance from ADC/DAC through RF front-end to antenna radiation, working closely with RFIC, PA/LNA, and system teams.
- Use EM and RF design tools (e.g., HFSS, CST, AWR, or similar) to simulate element/array performance, mutual coupling, scan loss, and pattern characteristics.
- Collaborate with calibration, software, DSP, ASIC, and validation teams to define system strategies (array calibration, beam equalization, phase/amplitude error mitigation, IFFT gains, and more) and measure on-bench and in-chamber performance.
- Define and maintain antenna specifications and requirements at the module, aperture, and system level.
- Support prototype builds, bring-up, and test campaigns for active antennas, including chamber testing and over-the-air validation.
- Provide DFM and DFT feedback for antenna boards, modules, and test fixtures.
- Write design reports, test summaries, and present results to leadership and cross-functional partners.
- Develop and deploy code to support testing, simulation, and validation of antenna systems.

Here’s Where You’ll Make An Impact:

xCures is deepening its work with chronic care programs and telehealth channel partners, and this role puts a clinician at the center of it. Reporting to the Vice President of Scientific and Medical Affairs, you will be the clinical voice in those partner relationships. You will speak directly with clinicians and clinically trained leaders on the partner side, peer to peer. You will translate what their care teams need into what the xCures Clinical Clarity Engine can deliver, then carry it back to the platform teams. The reach goes well beyond any single clinic.

The platform supports care for thousands of patients across the country every day, and your judgment shapes how that history reaches decision-makers. If you want your clinical experience to influence care at that scale, this is where you will make that impact.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the clinical liaison across chronic care and telehealth channel partner relationships, defining data needs, setting expectations, and translating clinical and operational requirements into workable plans that fit platform capabilities.
  • Act as the subject matter expert on chronic disease management and clinical data during partner meetings and external engagements.
  • Lead partner conversations on data quality and extractor validation, explaining how the Clinical Clarity Engine surfaces the chronic disease history a care team needs (diagnoses, medications, labs, comorbidities), with every data point traced to its source document.
  • Support partner programs by advising on the interpretation, provenance, and internal use of the clinical data the platform produces through its validated extractors.
  • Bring partner requirements to internal Product, Engineering, and Data Science teams to shape chronic care features and data offerings.
  • Collaborate with channel partners on case studies of new and emerging health technology, and lead joint publications and thought leadership with partners and external clinicians.
  • Represent xCures at conferences and health tech venues, presenting how the platform advances chronic care through emerging health technology, in support of the business development team.

Qualifications:

Required:

  • Active clinical licensure as a Nurse Practitioner (NP) or Physician Assistant (PA); an MD, DO, or other advanced clinical degree also qualifies.
  • Superior written and verbal communication, with the credibility to lead the conversation when presenting to senior executives at health systems and technology companies.
  • Working knowledge of chronic disease management across common conditions (e.g., diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease).
  • 4+ years of combined clinical practice and stakeholder-facing experience (medical affairs, clinical liaison, or clinical program roles).
  • Ability to translate complex clinical and scientific concepts into clear, actionable guidance for diverse audiences.
  • Working knowledge of electronic medical records and the healthcare data landscape (e.g., HIE, QHIN, TEFCA).
  • Understanding of data quality principles, validation processes, and how to assess the provenance and limits of clinical data.
  • Proven ability to build and maintain relationships with diverse stakeholders, including clinical leaders, executives, and internal cross-functional teams (e.g., Product, Engineering, Business Development).
  • Track record of managing multiple complex, unrelated projects at once, with strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Comfort working remotely and with virtual collaboration platforms.
  • Ability to thrive in a dynamic, growth-phase startup environment.


Bonus Points:

  • Direct clinical experience caring for patients with chronic conditions.
  • Experience working with structured clinical data.
  • Experience supporting telehealth or virtual care organizations, or working within a channel partner model.
  • Familiarity with value-based care, population health, or chronic care management programs.
  • Familiarity with the regulatory landscape governing clinical data use in healthcare.

Location

xCures operates in a distributed, remote-first environment. This role includes up to 10% travel for conferences, partner meetings, and company events throughout the year. Candidates may be located anywhere in the United States. The successful candidate must already have authorization to work in the United States. At this time, xCures does not offer sponsorship. All candidate information will be held in confidence and in accordance with EEOC guidelines.


Additional Considerations

We recognize that people bring a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the requirements listed in a job description. Diversity of experience and skills, combined with a shared passion for healthcare, is what drives us to innovate. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification listed. xCures is an equal opportunity employer, committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Benefits


Great work deserves great support. We believe our people are our greatest asset, and we’re committed to supporting them with a strong, competitive benefits package. Our goal is to be a place where people genuinely want to build their careers, and our benefits are designed to support our team in the ways that matter most.

  • Remote-First
  • Paid Time Off and 13 Company Holidays
  • Equity Package
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Medical, Vision, and Dental
  • Employer HSA Contribution
  • Employer 401(k) Match
  • STD, LTD, Life Insurance and Critical Illness Plans
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Adoption Assistance
  • Company Offsites
  • Monthly Internet Allowance
  • Professional Development Funds
  • And more!


Compensation

The anticipated salary range for this role is $150,000 to $180,000.

Agency Notice: xCures does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies, search firms, or other third-party recruiters. Any resumes submitted without a signed, active agreement with xCures will not be considered, and no fee will be paid in the event of a hire.

JOB SUMMARY

This opportunity is for Military personnel participating in the Department of Defense SkillBridge Program. Ideally, the SkillBridge will be a minimum of 90 days in length. DLB is able to accommodate up to the full 180-day program and we will consider durations less than 90 days. For more information and to speak with our SkillBridge Specialist, please submit your application and we will be in touch with you within 24 hours to schedule time to connect on the opportunities we have available, the geographic area that you are looking for and your time frame.


The SkillBridge - Data Center Commissioning Field Technician is an entry-level role that builds upon foundational commissioning knowledge while introducing more independent troubleshooting, testing, and reporting responsibilities. This role provides technical support in the inspection, validation, and functional testing of electrical, mechanical, and control systems.


The SkillBridge - Data Center Commissioning Field Technician will develop a deeper understanding of commissioning procedures, engage with vendors and project teams, will rely on instructions and take ownership of specific testing tasks under immediate supervision. They are expected to demonstrate increasing autonomy, problem-solving skills, and initiative in executing commissioning tasks.


The SkillBridge - Data Center Commissioning Field Technician will rely on instructions and pre-established guidelines to perform the functions of the job. Works under immediate supervision.


This person will communicate and operate in line with organizational goals and values, as well as departmental objectives.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Perform On-site Inspection, Validation, Testing and Verification of Electrical and Mechanical Equipment (50%)

  • Participate in factory witness testing
  • Observe startup activities
  • Use technical equipment to perform testing
  • Perform functional testing of equipment and electrical, mechanical and controls systems
  • Troubleshoot system components


Develop Testing Plans and Procedures (20%)

  • Assist in the development of commissioning plans
  • Prepare pre-functional checklists
  • Prepare functional performance test scripts


Review Construction Related Design Documents, Drawings and Specifications (15%)

  • Review shop drawings and submittals
  • Review sequence of operations
  • Assist in commissioning focused design reviews

Reporting (10%)

  • Prepare project progress reports for internal and external stakeholders
  • Assist in preparation and contributes to final commissioning report
  • Manage personal hours using company tools

Technology, Digital Tools & AI-Enabled Efficiency (5%)

  • Leverage AI-enabled and digital tools to enhance efficiency, reduce manual effort, and support consistent, high-quality work output.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes and demonstrate a continuous learning mindset, seeking out new technologies, skills, and methods that elevate individual and team performance.
  • Adapt to emerging technologies and evolving digital workflows, actively supporting the integration and adoption of innovative tools across the organization.


Completion of Assigned Tasks and Deliverables on Time and on Budget

Performs Other Related Duties as Assigned


POSITION REQUIREMENTS (BEGINNER LEVEL FOR ALL THE FOLLOWING UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED)

  • Must be a current participant of the Department of Defense SkillBridge Program
  • Knowledge of electrical, mechanical and controls system principles
  • Skilled at using MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams), along with exceptional organizational skills for file management
  • Skilled in completing assignments accurately and with attention to detail
  • Ability to leverage AI and emerging technologies to streamline workflows, optimize operational processes, and contribute to company-wide innovation
  • Ability to work successfully in a remote environment thru effective communication and organizational skills, self-motivation, proactiveness and resourcefulness in a distraction free workspace
  • Ability to follow company and site safety requirements
  • Ability to analyze and prepare documents, reports and correspondence
  • Ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written form (technical and non-technical information)
  • Ability to work successfully as a member of a team and independently with supervision
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet close deadlines
  • Ability to achieve certification for NFPA70E and / or OSHA training as / if required
  • Organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously


PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The following physical demands must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


While performing the duties of this job, the employee is

  • Frequently manipulating, moving or grasping small parts, devices or tools
  • Frequently required to remain in a stationary position
  • Frequently moving through office, critical facility and other environments (such as low temperatures, high temperatures and outdoor elements such as precipitation and wind), including tight and confined spaces

TRAVEL / RELOCATION REQUIREMENTS

  • Must be located near a major airport.
  • Effective May 7, 2025, and in accordance with U.S. federal regulations for domestic air travel, a valid REAL ID (or an acceptable alternative, such as a passport) is required for travel associated with this position.

OR

Technician III (Level 3, Step 1-4) – increased level of independent work and technical problem-solving.

title: Transportation Planner
description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves\: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story\:' https\://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

We believe transportation is more than movement, it’s the foundation of connected, thriving communities. As part of HDR’s Transportation Business Group, you’ll help shape the systems that move people and goods safely, efficiently, and sustainably. From designing resilient highways and iconic bridges to advancing transit, passenger and freight rail, aviation, federal transportation ports and marine infrastructure, your work will directly support economic vitality, public safety, sustainable and resilient communities and quality of life. We bring together planners, engineers, architects, construction management staff, environmental, strategic communications, economists, management consultants and specialists across disciplines to solve complex mobility challenges with innovation, technical excellence, and a deep understanding of community needs. Whether you're modernizing aging infrastructure or pioneering next-generation transportation solutions, your contributions will help define the future of mobility. This isn’t just a job, it’s a chance to lead progress, drive meaningful impact, and leave a legacy of smarter, more connected transportation networks. We are all employee-owners at HDR, which is the foundation of our collaborative culture that connects employees around the world.

In the role of Transportation Planner, job responsibilities will vary depending on the strengths of the potential candidate and opportunities available, but will generally include\:
  • Supporting transportation master plans, secondary plans, and environmental assessments
  • Macroscopic travel demand modelling and analysis of model outputs
  • Supporting the development of multimodal transportation options
  • Transit planning studies, business cases development
  • Transportation best practice and emerging trends research and report development
  • Data processing, analytics, and visualization
  • Preparing materials for and attending client, public and stakeholder meetings
  • Technical report writing
  • GIS / mapping
  • Traffic and microsimulation analysis (Synchro/Vissim/Aimsun)
  • Field Surveys / Observations

Job Skills

  • A self-starter, comfortable working in a team environment, with a strong interest in transportation and developing transportation solutions.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • Fluency with MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, and PowerPoint).
  • Working knowledge with EMME, VISUM, Synchro, Vissim, or similar demand modelling and traffic simulation platforms, is an asset.
  • Working knowledge in ArcGIS is an asset.
  • Programming skills in languages such as Python and R, is an asset
  • Progressive and innovative approach to problem-solving is an asset.
  • Knowledge of travel demand modeling, geometric roadway design, traffic engineering, transit service planning, active transportation, and an understanding of the current transportation planning context is an asset.
  • Knowledge and application of the Municipal Class Environmental Assessment Process (MCEA), Transit Project Assessment Process (TPAP), TAC Manual, MTO or BC Geometrics Design Manual are assets.
Preferred Qualifications
  • One to two years of experience in transportation planning and engineering including master and secondary plans, highway and transit infrastructure projects, environmental assessments, traffic operations studies, macro/meso/microsimulation modelling, transportation business cases, traffic impact studies, traffic safety, pedestrian and cycling studies, and traffic management plans.
  • Familiarity with planning policies and guiding documents in the BC, ON, or AB is an asset.
  • Experience working on projects with public agencies in British Columbia, Ontario, or Alberta (such as Translink, BC MoTT, MTO, Metrolinx, TTC, York Region, Peel Region, City of Toronto, or City of Calgary) preferred.
  • Masters degree is an asset.
  • Eligible for future engineering licensure in Canada.

title: Senior Full Stack Developer – Java & Angular
description:
Company: International Organization
Position: Senior Full Stack Developer
Work Model: Hybrid 50/50
Industry: Financial Services / Mobility

About the Organization

The organization operates internationally in the financial services and mobility sector. Its technology teams develop digital platforms supporting quotation, customer self-service, fleet processes, connected services, and asset lifecycle management across multiple markets.

The Senior Full Stack Developer will join an international agile team building applications used by internal teams and external customers.

Job Summary

The Senior Full Stack Developer will be responsible for designing, developing, and supporting secure, scalable, and maintainable applications, with a strong focus on Java and Angular development.

The role covers the full software lifecycle, from clarifying requirements and designing solutions to development, testing, deployment, documentation, and ongoing application support.

Mission of the Role

To deliver reliable digital solutions that support business operations and customer services across multiple markets, while improving application quality, security, maintainability, and service continuity.

Key Performance Objectives

1. Translate business needs into clear technical solutions

Typical tasks include clarifying and qualifying business and technical requirements, collaborating with stakeholders and team members, and contributing to technical studies before project launch.

The Senior Full Stack Developer will help establish a shared understanding of the required functionality and design solutions aligned with business needs and technical standards.

2. Build secure, scalable, and maintainable applications

Typical tasks include designing and developing backend services and frontend functionality using Java, Spring Boot, Angular, Node.js, and TypeScript.

The developer will deliver production-ready applications that meet agreed requirements and follow development, data, and security standards.

3. Deliver effective integrations and reliable data flows

Typical tasks include developing integrations using HTTP/REST, SOAP, and Kafka; working with Oracle SQL and Redis; and supporting software package integration and configuration.

The developer will ensure that application components and connected systems exchange data reliably and support the required business processes.

4. Improve existing code and verify software quality

Typical tasks include optimizing existing code, improving maintainability, creating or implementing testing strategies, and resolving issues identified during testing.

The developer will help ensure that new functionality and changes work as intended and maintain the quality of existing applications.

5. Support reliable deployment across environments

Typical tasks include supporting deployment tooling, working with automated delivery pipelines, and using technologies such as Jenkins, GitLab CI, Maven, Docker, and Kubernetes.

The developer will contribute to consistent, repeatable releases and help resolve integration, configuration, and deployment issues across environments.

6. Maintain application reliability and service continuity

Typical tasks include providing application support, investigating technical issues, implementing fixes, and collaborating with relevant teams to restore functionality when problems occur.

The developer will support stable application operation and help maintain continuity for internal users and external customers.

7. Maintain technical documentation and contribute to team improvement

Typical tasks include creating and updating technical documentation, sharing development best practices, and continuously developing technical expertise.

The developer will make applications easier to understand and maintain, support collaboration across functions, and contribute to improvements in the team’s engineering and delivery practices.

Core Technology Stack

Languages and build tooling: Java 17–21, Python 2.x/3.x, Node.js, TypeScript, Webpack
Frameworks: Spring Boot 3.x, Angular 16/17
Data: Oracle SQL, Redis
Integration: HTTP/REST, SOAP, Kafka
CI/CD: Jenkins, GitLab CI, Maven
Containers and orchestration: Docker, Kubernetes
Tools: Git, IntelliJ, VS Code, Jira, Confluence
Security: OWASP awareness

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Minimum of 5 years of professional software development experience.
  • Strong commercial experience with Java, Spring Boot, Angular, Node.js, and TypeScript.
  • Hands-on experience with Oracle SQL, Redis, REST services, and Kafka.
  • Good knowledge of Git, automated delivery pipelines, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • Experience working in Agile, Scrum, Kanban, and DevOps-oriented environments.
  • Ability to design, develop, test, document, and support high-quality software solutions.
  • Understanding of secure development practices and OWASP principles.
  • English proficiency sufficient for effective collaboration in an international environment.
  • Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, creativity, and adaptability.
  • A collaborative approach, focus on delivery, and willingness to share knowledge and support change.

Compensation and Opportunities

Compensation details will be discussed during the recruitment process.

The role offers the opportunity to:

  • Develop digital platforms used across multiple markets.
  • Work across backend, frontend, integration, and deployment activities.
  • Collaborate with an international agile technology team.
  • Contribute to applications supporting customer services and core business processes.
  • Develop technical expertise and share knowledge within the engineering community.

Hiring Process

Applications are managed through the recruitment agency handling the search. Selected candidates will receive further information about the organization, project, and interview stages during the recruitment process.

title: Mission Delivery Coordinator
description:
Mission Delivery Coordinator

Part-Time | Hiring Range: $20-22/hour, up to 24 hours per week

Girl Scouts of Southeast Florida has a fantastic opportunity available for a part-time Mission Delivery Coordinator!

If you enjoy working with people, being out in the community, and having a job where your day-to-day work changes throughout the year, this may be the role for you.

As a Mission Delivery Coordinator, you will provide hands-on support for programs, events, recruitment activities, campaigns, and other priorities across Girl Scouts of Southeast Florida. Rather than working within just one department, you will support different Council initiatives throughout the year based on organizational needs, seasonal demands, your availability, and your individual strengths.

You may find yourself:

  • Helping facilitate a Girl Scout program or activity
  • Supporting a signature event like Mall Madness, STEAMapalooza, or Rock the Noc
  • Representing Girl Scouts at a school or community recruitment event
  • Supporting membership recruitment and troop formation
  • Preparing materials, supplies, and activity stations for an event
  • Supporting Product Program initiatives, including the Cookie Sale
  • Working to prep for summer camp and more!

You will have the opportunity to work alongside a variety of staff members, volunteers, and departments to help bring the plans to life. Your responsibilities may include facilitating activities, assisting girls and families, preparing and transporting materials, setting up and breaking down events, capturing prospective member information, providing customer service, completing administrative tasks, and helping ensure programs and events run smoothly.

Reporting to the Director of Mission Delivery, you will have the opportunity to learn about many different areas of Girl Scouts while building hands-on experience in programs, events, recruitment, community engagement, and Council operations.

Because this is a flexible, community-based role, your schedule and work location will vary depending on the initiatives you support. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys variety, is dependable, and is comfortable jumping in wherever an extra set of capable hands is needed.

Who are we seeking?

  • Someone who enjoys working directly with girls and is comfortable facilitating activities and engaging groups in program, event, and community settings.
  • A friendly and confident communicator who can engage effectively with children, families, volunteers, colleagues, and community members.
  • Someone who provides great customer service and can represent Girl Scouts professionally and enthusiastically in the community.
  • A dependable team member who arrives prepared and on time, follows through on commitments, and communicates proactively about scheduling and availability.
  • Someone who can follow established plans, instructions, procedures, and safety requirements while using good judgment in day-to-day situations.
  • An organized person who can manage their time, keep accurate records, and reliably complete assigned responsibilities.
  • Someone who can work independently when needed while staying connected with the appropriate project lead and knowing when to ask questions or escalate an issue.
  • A flexible learner who can move between different types of assignments and quickly learn new processes, responsibilities, and areas of Council work.
  • Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office 365 and the ability to learn Council technology and systems used for communication, registration, data collection, and reporting.

What else will you need?

  • High school diploma or equivalent required. Additional education or coursework in youth development, education, recreation, community engagement, sales, marketing, communications, or a related field is preferred.
  • At least one (1) year of relevant work or volunteer experience is strongly preferred. Relevant experience may include youth programs, camps, education, childcare, recreation, community engagement, customer service, events, sales, or membership organizations.
  • Experience working directly with children or youth is strongly preferred.
  • Prior Girl Scout experience or familiarity with the scouting program and troop model is preferred.
  • Bilingual proficiency in Spanish, French, Haitian Creole, or another language commonly spoken within our service area is a plus.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule based on assigned initiatives, including daytime, afternoon, evening, and weekend hours as needed.
  • Ability to travel regularly throughout the Council's service area and work in a variety of settings, including schools, community locations, Council facilities, offices, and indoor and outdoor environments. GSSEF makes every effort to assign employees to locations close to home when possible, though some assignments may require travel to other areas within the Council's service territory.
  • Access to reliable transportation and a valid driver's license with a satisfactory driving record and eligibility for coverage under applicable Council insurance.

What will you get?

  • The opportunity to do meaningful, hands-on work that directly supports girls and families throughout Southeast Florida.
  • A role with variety, where you can build experience across programs, events, community engagement, membership recruitment, and other areas of Girl Scouts.
  • Opportunities to learn new skills through cross-training and exposure to different areas of Council operations.
  • An energetic, mission-driven team that works hard, has fun, and is committed to building the future leaders of tomorrow.

How do you apply?

Complete our online application in consideration for an opportunity to begin your career in Girl Scouting today!

If you are looking for a flexible, hands-on role where you can work with girls, connect with your community, and contribute to a variety of Girl Scout experiences throughout the year, apply today to become a Mission Delivery Coordinator!

Girl Scouts of Southeast Florida, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States for any employer. Girl Scouts of Southeast Florida does not sponsor applicants for work visas. Note: This posting may be closed or canceled at any time based on business needs.

title: Field Technician for Water Filtration - 4 Hours Monthly
description:
Get Paid to Drive Your Route. Work When It Works for You.

Field Technician — National Water Services, LLC. Water Machines

1099 Independent Contractor | $27/hr | Chicago, IL

If you like working independently, hate being stuck at a desk, and want a consistent route you can count on — this might be exactly what you’re looking for.

NWS operates water vending machines in retail stores across the country. We’re building a team of Field Technicians in Chicago, IL, to keep those machines clean, stocked, and running right. It’s straightforward work, it pays well, and you’re in charge of your own time.

What You’ll Actually Be Doing

Each week (or every two weeks, depending on the location), you’ll visit your assigned stores and:

• Clean and disinfect the water vending machine inside and out

• Take meter readings and log the data on your service report

• Snap photos of the machine condition at every visit

• Submit your completed report to the home office when you’re done

• Call in anything that looks off — damage, mechanical issues, anything unusual

That’s it. Each stop takes about an hour. Your total hours per week depend on how many stores are on your route.

What Makes This Different from Other Gig Work

• Consistent, scheduled route — not random job pickups

• Same stores every week, so you know exactly where you’re going

• $27/hr all-in — your mileage and travel are already baked into the rate

• Supplies provided — we give you everything you need to do the job

• Real support — a home office contact you can actually reach

This Is NOT a Repair Job

You’re not expected to fix anything. If a machine has a mechanical or technical issue, you flag it and we send a Service Technician. Your job is to keep things clean, documented, and reported — that’s where your value is.

What You Need to Get Started

• A reliable vehicle and a valid driver’s license

• A smartphone with a camera for photo submissions

• Attention to detail — you follow the checklist, every time

• You show up when you’re scheduled. That’s the most important thing.

No experience in water systems required. If you’ve done field services, retail merchandising, delivery routes, janitorial work, or anything similar — you’ll hit the ground running.

Who Thrives in This Role

This is a great fit if you’re already doing gig work and want something more predictable layered in, or if you’re looking for flexible part-time income that fits around your schedule. People who do well here tend to be:

• Self-starters who don’t need someone looking over their shoulder

• Detail-oriented — you notice things other people miss

• Reliable — your stores count on you showing up

• Good communicators — you keep the home office in the loop

How to Apply

Click “Apply Now” to be directed to our application. It only takes a few minutes to complete.

If we’re moving forward, you’ll hear from us by email. Interviews are conducted virtually via Microsoft Teams — we’ll send you a calendar invite with everything you need.

You can also view all open positions across our locations at:

freshpure.com/careers

title: Production Controller
description:
FII USA, Inc., a Foxconn Technology Group Company, is seeking a Production Controller that will work as part of a team to assist in planning and controlling production related activities. Once a part of the team, you will be responsible for a wide variety of tasks within the Supporting Quality Department in a manufacturing environment and have the opportunity to display critical thinking skills to expand your career in Smart Manufacturing.

The Production Controller will keep track of all open work orders and WIP to ensure timely work order closure, as well as monitor production schedules and assist their department as needed.
  • Schedules coordinates flow of work within or between departments of manufacturing plant to expedite production.​
  • Reviews master production schedule work orders, establishes priorities for specific customer orders and revises schedule according to work order specifications, established priorities and availability or capability of workers, parts, material, machines and equipment. ​
  • Reschedules identical processes to eliminate duplicate machine setups. ​
  • Distributes work orders to departments, denoting number, type, and proposed completion date of units to be produced. ​
  • Confers with department supervisors to define progress of work to provide information on changes in processing methods received from methods or engineering departments. ​
  • Compiles reports concerning progress of work and downtime due to failures of machines equipment to apprise production planning personnel of production delays. ​
  • Maintains inventory of materials parts needed to complete production. ​
  • May expedite material ​
  • May use computer system to track locate production units.
  • Other Duties as assigned
  • Associates Degree in Supply Chain Management. Bachelors Preferred.
  • 1-2 years of relevant working experience in areas of supply chain (i.e. procurement) or manufacturing is required.
  • Above average capabilities with Microsoft Excel and SAP.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Exceptional organizational and time-management skills.
  • Strong regard for product safety and quality standards.
  • Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage.
  • Basic life insurance and short-term disability coverage provided by employer.
  • Supplemental life insurance and long-term disability coverage options available.
  • 401K with employer contribution.
  • Personal, Vacation, and Holiday paid time off for all full-time employees.
  • Onsite Aurora Health & Wellness Center available for all employees.
  • Employees are continuously encouraged to learn and grow their careers in smart manufacturing.

title: Production Technician (2nd Shift)
description:
Location: Lowell,Massachusetts,United States

Position Overview:
The Production Technician is responsible for all aspects of plant processing from post-crop harvest through packaging and labeling of the final product ready for customer sale as outlined by the management team and SOPs. These responsibilities include post-harvest tasks including the drying and curing stage all the way through trimming, packaging, and labeling the product. This position works in a timely manner and strives to increase productivity and acts with professional regard to the management and use of all production facilities and processing equipment.

Pay: $17

Schedule: Full time 4:00PM-12:30AM M-F

Travel %: 0
FLSA status: Non-exempt


Major Areas of Responsibility include:
•Assists in the post-harvest plant processing of cannabis.
•Fan leaf removal, harvest, drying, trimming, curing, weighing, packaging, labeling, recording, and inspection of product in addition to cleaning and sanitation.
•Maintains a clean and organized work environment.
•Transport harvested plants to drying room and hang to be dried.
•Hand trims and/or operates a trimming machine to remove excess plant material.
•Weighs, records, and shreds plants waste and adds a non-cannabis medium for compliant disposal.
•Receives instructions and assists on tasks as delegated by management team.
•Works in a quick and efficient manner.
•Complies with all HR policies including confidentiality and non-disclosure.

Minimum Qualifications (Skills, Knowledge & Abilities):
•All applicants must be at least 21 years of age.
•1-3 years of experience in production position; including hands-on production activities.
•General knowledge of weights and measurement.
•Evening/night/weekend work may be required.
•Speed and precision with equipment and attention to detail.
•Ability to multi-task and maintain work consistency on a daily basis.
•High attention to detail.
•Standing/sitting for long periods of time.

Additional Abilities Required:
•Exposure to pollen, dust, and plant particles due to the handling of raw plant materials.
•The job requires physical activity, including prolonged sitting, standing, repetitive bending, climbing, and lifting or moving up to 50 pounds (or more with a coworker). Good visual acuity, hand-eye coordination, manual dexterity, and ability to perform repetitive motions with accuracy is required. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.


Note: Nothing in this job description restricts the company’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this position at any time. Reasonable accommodations may be made in appropriate circumstances to enable individuals to perform the essential functions of the position.

title: Regional Head of Latin America and Caribbean Hub
description: At the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. MIGA’s guarantees help mitigate risks. In fiscal year 2026, the WBG Guarantee Platform delivered a total of $17.8 billion in guarantees. For more information, visit https://www.miga.org/ MIGA’s Operations Department (MIGOP) is seeking a Regional Head of Latin America and Caribbean Hub with extensive political and public sector credit risk underwriting, new business origination, and client relationship management experience, who will identify new business opportunities for MIGA and the WB’s GP, achieve business targets and grow the World Bank Group guarantee business. This position will be based in one of the relevant hubs of the World Bank Group in LAC - Panama City, or Sao Paulo. The final duty location will be decided by the Hiring Manager based on business needs. The selected candidate will report to MIGA’s Financial Institutions Group (FIG) Director based in Washington D.C. Duties and Accountabilities The Regional Head of Latin America and Caribbean Hub plays the primary role in developing MIGA’s business pipeline in the Latin America and Caribbean Region, with a particular focus on lesser developed countries in the region. He/she will be responsible for developing and implementing strategies to identify clients/ projects in priority sectors, countries, and areas. He/she will oversee the provision of technical underwriting support from the region, conduct outreach to clients and provide overall quality assurance for work produced by the Latin America and Caribbean regional team. The Regional Head will primarily report to MIGA’s FIG Director with the responsibility to support both the FIG and Industries Directors in all areas including pipeline and portfolio management, new business development and meeting overall business targets for MIGA. The Regional Head will also support the Directors and MIGA’s Senior Management Team overall in policy, planning and strategy for the region. In addition, the Regional Head will be the primary counterpart for World Bank and IFC regional engagements. S/he is expected to maintain close contact with the various country management units (CMUs) on sector and regional issues impacting MIGA’s pipeline. The work of the Regional Head involves frequent interaction with top government officials and equivalent contacts in other international organizations, private sector companies and financial institutions that are clients, potential clients, and partners of MIGA, including counterparts within and across sectors, networks, and other WBG units. The role also requires contact, as required, with the MIGA Board and Board Committees, and senior and executive management at Headquarters and in the field. Responsibilities include: • Ensuring proper financial and fiduciary management of MIGA's resources; • Ensuring the successful delivery of the WB GP commitments by closely coordinating with WBG sister institutions and relevant staff, host governments, and partner institutions, including conducting ongoing roadshow / briefing sessions to regularly inform such stakeholder groups on the goals and objectives, and progress of the WB GP; • Ensuring the agreed Accountability and Decision Making (ADM) protocols for the WB GP are consistently and comprehensively applied where/when applicable. • Managing relationships with Host Government and Host Government Officials in countries identified as priority markets for the Agency; • Collaborating with other units within MIGA, IFC, and the WBG to deliver high level business results, with a particular focus on WB/IFC regional staff; • Working with the FIG, Industries, and World Bank Infrastructure Guarantees Unit managers and staff to provide oversight of all political risk insurance underwriting and business origination work of the Latin America and Caribbean team, including quality control of all papers and presentations for MIGA management and MIGA's Board, and providing high level client management oversight including leadership or participation in client teams; • Ensuring consistency of MIGA’s guarantees with WBG country partnership strategies; • Identifying new business opportunities for MIGA and WB GP using the IDA PSW and other Blended Finance modalities at MIGA’s disposal, among other business development tools; • Providing a specialized focus on business development and origination in lesser developed countries in the Latin America and Caribbean and other developing regions covered by the WBG, and develop and implement strategies for sub-sectors and priority areas such as climate / energy transition, and gender; • Developing client/ project leads; assist clients through the application process; structure initial deals, provide high-level client relationship management; working with MIGA FIG and Industries teams as needed when a new application is received to facilitate the underwriting of a transaction and to ensure excellent client service; developing and maintaining partnerships with regional DFIs and other like-minded institutions involved in foreign investment. • Developing and maintaining contacts with private sector investors, lenders and other institutions involved in the development and implementation of investment projects; • Meeting with prospective clients to market MIGA's guarantee products as well as with MIGA partners to better understand the market for political risk insurance and public sector credit risk guarantee solutions in priority areas and to identify new market opportunities for MIGA and the WB GP; • Structuring complex transactions and assessing project risks; • Coaching and mentoring junior staff, supervising the staff located and working in the region; • Representing MIGA and the WB GP at high-level conferences or other events where MIGA desires to market its services and products; overseeing sponsorship at such events where needed; • Advising MIGA's Management Team on business development strategies as needed. • Frequent travel is required to follow up on project opportunities that are likely to result in new business for MIGA.

Position summary

The Export Coordinator manages every export order from entry to shipment, making sure product leaves the plant and cold stores on time with complete, accurate, USDA-certified documentation. The role is the link between export customers, production, the loading dock and USDA FSIS.

  • Reports to: VP of Export Sales
  • Department: Export Sales
  • Employment type: Full-time, exempt
  • Location: On site at the plant, with occasional visits to third-party cold storage facilities

Key responsibilities

Order management

  • Enter export orders into the order system accurately and promptly, matching customer specifications, pricing and destination requirements.

Export documentation and USDA coordination

Shipping and loading coordination

  • Work with loading dock staff to schedule export inspections and coordinate container loading.
  • Confirm product, counts and labeling match the order and documents before shipment.

Regulatory knowledge

  • Know and follow the import requirements of each country we export to, using the USDA FSIS Export Library as the primary reference.
  • Track changes to country requirements and plant eligibility and alert the VP of Export Sales and plant management to anything that affects orders.
  • Keep complete, audit-ready export records.

title: Controller
description:
About the role

We are looking for a hands-on Controller to own the integrity, timeliness, and scalability of our accounting operations. Reporting to the VP, Accounting, you will lead the day-to-day close, manage our US and international audits, help us build a scalable pricing, packaging, and billing engine for our multi-channel business, serve as a senior technical accounting resource, and build the processes and team that keep us audit-ready year-round, not just at year-end. This is a role for someone with technical depth, sound business judgment, and a bias for building. We welcome both experienced Controllers and standout Assistant Controllers ready to step into their first Controller role.


What you'll do


Close & Financial Reporting

  • Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close, driving continuous reduction in close cycle time while maintaining accuracy
  • Review account reconciliations, journal entries, and flux analyses; ensure clean, GAAP-compliant financial statements
  • Prepare and review financial reporting packages for the board, PE sponsor, and lenders, including covenant compliance

Technical Accounting

  • Apply US GAAP to complex SaaS and usage-based transactions, including ASC 606 (revenue recognition), ASC 340-40 (capitalized commissions), ASC 718 (stock-based compensation), ASC 805 (business combinations), and ASC 842 (leases)
  • Account for revenue across our multi-channel business (direct, partner and reseller, and marketplace), including principal vs. agent, gross vs. net, and channel incentive considerations
  • Draft and maintain technical accounting memos and accounting policies
  • Evaluate the accounting impact of new contracts, pricing models, and strategic transactions, including M&A

Audit & Controls

  • Lead the consolidated US audit as primary liaison to our Big 4 auditor; manage PBC lists, timelines, and year-round audit readiness
  • Own audits at key international entities, including the UK and Germany
  • Design, document, and monitor internal controls with a SOX-readiness mindset and drive continuous improvement
  • Coordinate tax compliance with external advisors, including sales/use, income, and international

Global Payroll & Compliance

  • Review and ensure compliance for US payroll and international Employer of Record (EOR) services across all countries where Nerdio employs people

Team Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop the accounting team (GL, revenue, AP, payroll, and related functions)
  • Set clear expectations, build succession, and foster a culture of ownership and accountability

Systems & Process

  • Act as a champion for our finance tech stack (NetSuite, Ramp, FloQast), driving automation and efficiency
  • Identify and implement process improvements, including AI and automation tooling, to scale without proportional headcount

Pricing, Packaging & Billing

  • Be a key finance partner in building a nimble pricing, packaging, and billing solution that lets us launch and change offers quickly without breaking the close
  • Translate new pricing models and channel structures into scalable billing, revenue recognition, and reconciliation processes, working closely with Product, RevOps, and Systems teams
  • Ensure billing data flows accurately and consistently from each channel into NetSuite and the financial statements

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with FP&A, Revenue Operations, Legal, Sales Ops, and HR on forecasting, deal structures, and compensation accounting
  • Support finance integration for acquisitions and new entities
  • Contribute to the accuracy and understanding of SaaS metrics (ARR, NRR, churn) alongside GAAP results

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance
  • Active CPA license
  • 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 2-4 years in a Controller role, or a strong Assistant Controller / Accounting Manager ready for a first Controller role
  • Strong command of US GAAP, with demonstrated SaaS revenue recognition experience (ASC 606)
  • Experience managing and developing accounting teams and supporting external audits
  • Exceptional analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills

Preferred skills

  • Big 4 or national public accounting firm experience
  • Experience in a PE-backed company, including sponsor and lender reporting
  • Hands-on experience with NetSuite, Ramp, and FloQast
  • Multi-entity and international accounting experience, including foreign currency and local statutory audits
  • M&A and purchase accounting experience
  • SOX or SOX-readiness experience


Benefits and Incentives

  • Competitive Base + Annual bonus up to 10%
  • Stock Options
  • Health and Welfare Plans*
  • Life and Disability Plans*
  • Retirement Plan*
  • Unlimited Flexible Paid Time Off......including your birthday off!
  • Collaborative Team Culture

* Benefits for international employees, outside the US, vary by country.

· Drive Master Data Accuracy and System Reliability. Maintain and continuously improve material master data, including part numbers, supersessions, and depletion indicators, ensuring high data accuracy as a foundation for operational stability and supply chain efficiency.

· Lead Part Lifecycle and Change Management Processes. Manage end-to-end part number updates, supersessions, and regional transitions (e.g., GLC to NAFTA), ensuring smooth system integration and avoiding disruptions in supply or inventory inconsistencies.

· Govern Supplier and Procurement Master Data Structure. Oversee the creation and maintenance of supplier codes, planner assignments, and buyer information within SAP Paragon, ensuring proper system governance and enabling efficient procurement execution.

· Use Mercedes-Benz standard methods and systems to manage the supplier readiness information and use reporting tools to manage timely reports to higher management and Headquarters.

· Enable Cross-Regional Coordination and Communication. Act as the central liaison across Germany, USA, and Mexico teams to align changes, synchronize system updates, and ensure consistent execution across all regions through structured communication and meetings.

· Act as Key Interface for Cross-Functional Topics (Finance & IT). Support and coordinate change-related topics impacting Finance and IT systems, ensuring alignment between business requirements and system capabilities, while facilitating issue resolution and process improvements.

Main Tasks\:

1. Lead Master Data and Change Management Governance\:

Drive the overall governance of master data and change management activities in SAP Paragon, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and system integrity across all material and supplier data.

2. Manage Scheduling Agreements Lifecycle (TPOP Parts)\:

Ensure the creation, validation, and maintenance of Scheduling Agreements, confirming alignment with demand and guaranteeing correct system releases to suppliers.

3. Execute Part Number Changes and Supersessions\:

Lead the implementation of part number updates, supersessions, and material transitions (e.g., GLC to NAFTA), ensuring seamless system updates and no supply disruptions.

4. Maintain and Update Material Master Data\:

Ensure all material master data remains accurate and up to date, including depletion indicators, part number attributes, and system consistency to support operations.

5. Govern Supplier and Procurement Data in System\:

Oversee the creation and update of supplier codes, planner assignments, and buyer information in SAP Paragon, ensuring correct system structure and procurement alignment.

6. Coordinate Cross-Regional Change Implementation\:

Act as the central interface between Germany, USA, and Mexico teams, ensuring alignment, communication, and proper execution of change management activities across regions.

7. Support Cross-functional Topics (Finance & IT)\:

Serve as liaison for Finance and IT-related topics linked to system changes, supporting issue resolution and ensuring alignment between business and system requirements.

8. Drive Communication and Stakeholder Alignment\:

Ensure continuous communication through emails, meetings, and follow-ups, aligning stakeholders and securing timely execution of all change management activities.

title: Automotive Assistant & Service Managers
description:
Mavis Tires & Brakes at Discount Prices - Automotive Assistant & Service Managers


Put your career into high gear with Mavis Tires & Brakes at Discount Prices! We're looking for full-time Automotive Assistant and Service Managers to join Team Mavis at one or our state-of-the-art automotive service and retail tire sales centers in the Mount Ephraim, NJ area. With over 4,000 retail locations, Mavis is one of the largest tire sales and automotive repair chains in the United States.

About the Position of Assistant Manager

As a future leader of Mavis, the Assistant Manager supports the Store Manager to ensure each Mavis retail location operates efficiently, safely and effectively. Using fundamental leadership skills, Assistant Managers are responsible for enforcing established policies, procedures and standards, scheduling mechanics/technicians' work, managing outside orders, ensuring the quality and timely completion of jobs, meeting customer expectations, and the safety of team members

The Service Manager is responsible for assisting customers with tire selections and recommending necessary under-car repair services. In addition, to ensure complete customer satisfaction by delivering timely completion of high-quality vehicle repair and maintenance, Service Managers must direct the workflow of Mechanics, Alignment Technicians and Tire Technicians and stage vehicle repair/maintenance work. While driving the sales initiatives of Mavis, Service Managers must communicate directly with customers, assess customer needs, provide information regarding requested and/or necessary automotive repairs and maintenance, ensure customers are satisfied with their in-store experience and strive to meet customer expectations.

Employee Benefits

At Mavis, we understand that our people drive our success. We provide our team members with competitive weekly pay, including weekly incentive compensation, a good working environment and an excellent combination of additional benefits like health, dental and vision insurance, a 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match, paid vacations, paid time off, paid holidays, life insurance, on-the-job training, and opportunities for career growth and advancement.

Qualifications

We recruit team members who share our commitment to providing complete customer satisfaction and delivering the highest quality service. To be eligible for the position of Automotive Assistant / Service Manager, you must (1) be at least 18 years of age; (2) be legally authorized to work in the United States; and (3) possess (i) 1 year of experience and/or training in automotive parts and/or tire sales, (ii) 1 year of experience and/or training in automotive repairs/maintenance, or (iii) any combination of education, training, and experience which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties and responsibilities of the position.

title: Engineer In Training (GeoSystems Analysis)
description:
GeoSystems Analysis, Inc., a Trinity Consultants team, is adding an Engineer In Training to join our growing team in the southwest. The Engineer in Training (EIT) supports the analysis, design, and technical documentation of mine reclamation, managed aquifer recharge, habitat restoration, and related engineering projects. Working under the direction of senior engineering staff, this position performs engineering analyses and design activities, supports project and task coordination, and develops technical expertise through progressively responsible project assignments and continued professional development.

What will I be doing?

  • Perform engineering analyses and design activities related to stormwater management, hydrology, hydraulics, earthwork, landform stabilization, and related projects.
  • Assist with the preparation of engineering designs, calculations, technical reports, specifications, drawings, and other project documentation.
  • Collaborate with CAD designers and technical staff to develop engineering drawings, layouts, and design plans.
  • Collect, manage, and evaluate technical data, including topographic, survey, mapping, and other project-related information.
  • Monitor assigned task progress, identify potential challenges or delays, and communicate concerns to project managers and senior engineers.
  • Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams, subconsultants, and agencies to support project activities and deliverables.
  • Participate in field investigations, site visits, data collection, and construction observations as needed.

What qualifications are required for this role?

  • A bachelor's degree and/or a master's degree in a related engineering discipline.
  • Engineer in Training (EIT) certification required or ability to obtain certification within twelve (12) months of hire.
  • Previous relevant engineering experience in civil, environmental, water resources, geotechnical, mine reclamation, habitat restoration, or a related engineering field.
  • Relevant engineering internship, academic research, field, or professional experience related to water resources, mine reclamation, restoration, environmental, or geotechnical engineering preferred.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience with AutoCad Civil 3D and engineering modeling software preferred.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, Project, Outlook).

The salary range for this position is $66,000 - $76,000 annually.

In addition, Geosystems Analysis has a discretionary bonus program that considers business profitability and individual performance.

What does GSA/Trinity offer you?

  • Comprehensive benefits package: 9 paid holidays, healthcare benefits, PTO, and 401k matching for full-time employees. Flexible work schedules and remote/hybrid possibilities for most roles.
  • Multidisciplinary environment: Unique, creative, and challenging projects where you can develop your vision of clientele and work with industry leaders daily.
  • Success-oriented environment: Two-way mentorship, financial incentives to publish work, tuition reimbursement, and a career-path structure to help you reach the next steps in your career.
  • Collaborative work environment: Clear and frequent communication, shared information and ideas across teams, and a welcoming atmosphere for everyone.

GeoSystems Analysis, Inc., a Trinity Consultants team, is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.
